Too soft falls short into the Swamp (no skill shot, but banks a lock if one is lit there); too hard flies past into the pop bumpers for nothing but bumper value.
The core shot loop

Four shots form the spine of the entire ruleset: the **Bear Kick (center) ramp**, the **left orbit** ("Adv X" loop, the hardest shot on the table), the **Million Plus (left/side) ramp**, and the **Swamp** (a wide sinkhole scoring the Graveyard jet-bumper value, boosted 5x when "5X Graveyard" is lit). Chaining these scores the game's two named **3-way combos** (5M each) and the **4-way combo** (10M, plus the embedded 3-way — 16-25M total once built up). The **"Chopping Wood" loop** (Thing Ramp → Million Plus ramp → Swamp) is the most-repeated money sequence once ramp value and Graveyard are maxed.
Mansion rooms & Tour the Mansion

Shooting the flashing **Electric Chair** or **Swamp** collects whichever of 12 mansion rooms is currently lit: three flat point rooms (3M/6M/9M), five 20-30 second timed rooms (**The Mamushka**, **Hit Cousin It**, **Fester's Tunnel Hunt**, **Seance**, **Raise the Dead**), the **Quick Multiball** and **Thing Multiball** rooms, **Graveyard at Max**, and **Light Extra Ball**. Clearing all 12 lights the "?" insert; shooting it starts **Tour the Mansion**, the game's wizard mode — an instant 50,000,000 points, relit 3M/6M/9M, Special lit in the outlanes, Quick Multiball lit, Graveyard maxed, and a temporary Extra Ball at Thing's Eject, followed by all five timed rooms run automatically back-to-back. The Vault is locked shut for the whole thing.
The Vault / Multiball

Hitting the **Bookcase** standups spells **G-R-E-E-D**, swinging it open to reveal the **Vault** and lighting a lock. On the very first multiball of the game, locks 1 & 2 can come from either **Thing's Eject** or the **Vault**; every multiball after that requires re-spelling GREED and only the Vault locks. Lock 3 is always at the Vault and releases all three balls, activating **The Power** magnets. Multiball is started at the Electric Chair or the lit Vault. The **Jackpot** lights at the **Train Wreck** target and climbs +1M per Bear Kick ramp or Bookcase hit (capping at 25M); the **Super Jackpot** at the Million Plus ramp pays double on the first multiball, triple thereafter, and relights the regular Jackpot.

Two smaller multiball modes also exist: **Quick Multiball** (lit at Thing's Eject, opens the Vault for direct 5M-10M scoring) and **Thing Multiball** (a DMD hurry-up countdown from ~15M to a 3M floor — shoot Thing's Eject before it bottoms out to lock in the value and start a 2-ball multiball).
Multipliers

TAF has no global playfield multiplier — only **Bonus X** (1x-5x, lit by the right inlane, advanced at the left orbit, applied only to the end-of-ball bonus) and the shot-specific **5X Graveyard**, which pays 5x the Graveyard jet value on a single Swamp shot when lit.
Extra balls

Multiple independent paths all serve the ball at Thing's Eject: Bear Kick milestones (~8 and 50 kicks), the Light Extra Ball mansion room, Train Wreck completions, and a temporary EB during Tour the Mansion.
Strategy in one line

Soft-plunge skill shot, loop Bear Ramp into the Million Plus ramp to build value and THING letters, bank a Train Wreck early to carry the built Graveyard value into the next ball, clear every mansion room before ever spelling GREED (rooms can't be collected during multiball), and save the Vault/GREED multiball as the endgame farm after Tour the Mansion.

name: Baywatch
description: Baywatch pinball rules: complete the five Vertical Modes, run Swimmer Jackpot Multiball, climb the Shark Feature ladder, and reach the Earthquake wizard mode.

body.text: Baywatch is a single-SKU, single-hardware-revision Sega machine (no Pro/Premium/LE editions — that tiering didn't exist in 1995, ~2,000 units built). Its rules split into two documented code versions: the **original 1995 Sega factory ROM** (what most stock/unrestored machines run) and **"Chad's Unofficial" tournament ROM** (v4.01 2017, v4.02 2025), which rebalances skill-shot values, speeds up the bonus multiplier, and removes stock code's guaranteed-lock bug. Values below follow the stock code, with tournament-code differences called out where they diverge.

**Skill Shot.** The ball auto-plunges (no manual pull) onto an elevated wireform. Use the flippers to steer into one of three lit options: the **Top SPF Lanes** (10M, safest), the **Shark Super Scoop** via the shark-fin mini-flipper (20M stock/40M tournament), or the **Side Ramp** off the upper-left flipper (50M, hardest — also spells a letter toward IRONMAN). Each successful skill shot bumps future values +10M; hitting all three different across a game scores a 50M Variety Award, the same one three times also scores 50M.

**The five Mode/GUARD shots** — Left Ramp, Center Ramp, Upper VUK, Right Ramp, and Spinner Lane — are the backbone of the entire ruleset. Hitting a given shot 4 times cumulatively across the game starts its 30-second **Vertical Mode**: CPR (Left Ramp, 3-ramp escalating 50/60/70M), Chopper Rescue (Center Ramp, 5 vehicle standups rescuing swimmers, but a notorious center-drain trap), Diver Trapped (Upper VUK, repeatable scoop shots, ends in a 15-second Extra Ball), Shark Cove/Shark Attack (Right Ramp, kill shark waves on the SHARK bank then finish at the Shark Super Scoop for uncapped double points), and Tidal Wave (Spinner Lane, feeds the Upper Ball Launch to a Side Ramp "Rescue Award"). Completing all 5 modes once lights **Horizontal Mode 1, "Guard"** — all five shots pay a decaying countdown award (~50M down to a ~20M floor); completing them a second time lights **Horizontal Mode 2, Tourist Season**, a 2-ball multiball collecting six countries at the Right Ramp (25M each) before 100M Jackpots open at the Side Ramp.

**Multiball.** Complete the **3-Bank Drop Targets** to light locks on the **Left Ramp**'s internal Trap Door; three locks launches a 5-ball Multiball with ball saver. All five Mode Shots light for **Swimmer Jackpots**, valued at 15M + 5M x Balls-In-Play + 10M x Jackpots-already-collected + 1M x Drop-Target hits (each hit boosts the value, to a maximum boost of 20M), plus a separate 'Sneaky Shark' bonus of +10M (collectible up to 5 times per multiball). Routing a shot through the Spinner Lane into the **Upper Ball Launch** holds the ball ~10 seconds, during which all Jackpot values are doubled. After all 5 Jackpots are collected, a **Super Jackpot** (50M x Balls-In-Play) lights at the Shark Super Scoop, followed by a **Double Super Jackpot** (2x that) at the Side Ramp.

**Multiplier.** Baywatch has exactly one multiplier — the **SPF Bonus Multiplier** — which only affects the End-of-Ball Bonus (there's no real-time shot-value multiplier). Spelling S-P-F at the Top Lanes steps it 2X→10X; it never carries between balls. Completing SPF once more at 10X scores a bonus 20M and lights a one-time Extra Ball at the Upper VUK.

**Shark Feature ladder.** Shooting the Shark Super Scoop collects Sharks in escalating waves (1/2/3/4). Five cumulative tiers award, in order: 10M+Video Mode, 20M+Super Laser Kick, 30M+Shark Frenzy, 50M+Extra Ball, and finally 100M+**Earthquake** — a direct shortcut to the game's wizard mode.

**Wizard Mode — Earthquake.** Two qualification paths: (1) complete all 5 Vertical Modes plus both Horizontal Modes (Guard, Tourist Season), or (2) reach Shark Feature tier 5. Either way, shoot the lit **Upper VUK** to start it: the bonus multiplier locks at max 10X, MEGA Pops turns on (3M/hit), and for 30 seconds balls auto-launch continuously while all five Mode Shots recollect the total value of the modes played from that shot (minimum 25M each) — when the timer expires, flippers die and the field drains. The mode-completion path resets all modes afterward; the Shark shortcut path does not.

name: Breakshot
description: Breakshot pinball rules: play Eight Ball, Nine Ball and Rotation, lock balls at the Center Pockets, and reach the Cutthroat Countdown wizard mode finale.

body.text: **Designer:** Greg Kmiec (frequently misattributed to George Gomez). Art by Stan Fukuoka/Paul Mazur/Hugh van Zanten, software by Bill Pfutzenreuter/Tony DeFeo. One production run, ~1,000 units, May 1996, model BRK3002. No Pro/Premium/LE editions exist — that convention postdates this game.
The table

A single-level, EM-throwback design — no ramps, no spinner. Two main flippers plus an unusually capable upper-right "3rd" flipper that can trap and catch. The playfield reads bottom-to-top: slingshots/in-out lanes → Green (left) and Brown (right) drop-target banks near their respective orbits → a two-ball Captive Ball left-of-center → Purple/Orange standups flanking the **Center Pockets** (the signature toy: 3 saucers behind a rising post) → 3 jet bumpers → 3 rollover lanes (Yellow/Blue/Red) at the very top, fed by the Left and Right Orbits running up each edge.
Three pool "games"

Only one is active at a time (chalk icons over the slings show which), cycling **Nine Ball → Eight Ball → Nine Ball → Rotation**, repeating: - **Eight Ball** — sink 7 assigned colors (solids or stripes) via the rollover lanes, Purple/Orange standups, and Green/Brown banks, then shoot the 8-Ball Saucer. 100K. - **Nine Ball** — hit any of 5 shots (Left Orbit, Captive Ball, Right Orbit, Green standup, Brown standup) 9 times total. 200K, plus a Points/Special/Extra-Ball bonus wheel at the Center Pockets entrance. - **Rotation** — sink all 15 balls, cycling the same 7 shot-groups twice. 500K.
Both **Super Cues** (lit orbit shots) and any **Center Pockets saucer hit** auto-sink the lowest unsunk ball regardless of which game is active.
Center Pockets — the lock/multiball engine

A ball entering (post down) trips an opto, raises the post, and ejects a fresh ball to the plunger (up to 2 locks). A hard hit on the post with resting balls propels them into the side saucers — a **Good Shot** (base value), a **Trick Shot** (+100K, one ball into a lit side saucer), or a **Nice Combo/"Breakshot"** (+250K, both side saucers made on one hit — the game's namesake).

**Ball-O-Rama** (2-ball multiball, 2x scoring): lock one ball, then shoot the lit 8-Ball Saucer to start. Jackpot starts at 100K, climbs 10K/sec, never resets. **Breakshot Frenzy** (3-ball, 3x scoring): lock both side saucers, then capture a 3rd ball in the center saucer to auto-start. Jackpot starts at 200K, resets after each collect (2 "easy" jackpots before relighting is required); a fast second ball into the entry opto right after a collect scores a **Double Jackpot**. No ball saver runs during either multiball.
Multipliers

items: **Bonus multiplier** — rollover lanes advance it, seen up to 13x, paid at end-of-ball.
**Multiball state** — Ball-O-Rama 2x / Breakshot Frenzy 3x, global while active.
**Bank Shot streak** — each consecutive Bank Shot make (uninterrupted) doubles/triples the payout, no stated cap.
**Left Super Cue → Bank Shot Bonus** — pre-loading Left Super Cue shots before cashing the Bank Shot doubles a stacking 50K bonus (reported max 3.2M).
**Super Cue chain** — 60K × consecutive makes, reset by any other switch.

body.text: Combos and the money loop

**Capcombo** (250K): Bank Shot → Right Orbit, or Left Super Cue → Right Orbit, immediately. The headline technique is the **Bank Shot catch-and-relaunch loop**: light-plunge onto the upper-right flipper, catch, shoot the Bank Shot, re-catch, repeat — each lap sinks a ball and the value escalates fast (1M+ per lap is reachable by the eighth to tenth rep, and a single shot can pay far more). Landing **both Super Cues back-to-back** (both lit simultaneously, then the two orbits shot one right after the other) lights the Captive Ball for an Extra Ball.
Wizard mode — Cutthroat Countdown

Reached after completing 3 regular games (default). A 60-second timer calls balls one at a time (≤10 sec each); hitting the right target sinks it, scores 1M, and adds 10 seconds. A second pass calls missed balls in random order. Ending with at least one ball sunk lights the center saucer for a **Super Jackpot worth 2M/ball sunk**, scaling to 2x then 3x on repeat completions. Sinking every ball ("perfect") auto-spots the next game complete and chains straight into another round. The Frenzy multiball multiplier still applies to the per-ball 1M Cutthroat scoring during Cutthroat Countdown (up to 9M/ball when 3x is running), but it does not apply to the Super Jackpot itself.
Risk notes

Fast ricochets off the Center Pockets are the game's biggest drain hazard — approach it off a controlled trap, not a bounce. Multiball has no ball saver and the jackpot shot isn't forgiving. The Bank Shot loop's biggest risk is a mistimed catch, which resets the escalating value to base — skilled play means consciously bailing once you've banked a big number.

name: Ghostbusters
description: Ghostbusters pinball rules: capture Ghosts, clear the three Scene ladders, stack the 2X/3X Playfield multiplier, and reach Are You a God, the final wizard mode.

body.text: Designed by John Trudeau, Ghostbusters is built around **collecting Ghosts** as its core currency, three parallel **scene ladders** themed to the movie, and a heavy emphasis on **playfield multipliers**. It ships in Pro, Premium, and Limited Edition variants sharing an identical rule set — Premium/LE add a physical subway ball-lock, Ecto Goggles Pepper's-ghost effect, magnetic slingshots, and a harder-routed right ramp, but score identically to Pro shot-for-shot.
Skill Shot

Every ball offers two simultaneous, untimed picks: a **P-K-E top lane** (left flipper button) and one of **six playfield shots** shown as a blue arrow (right flipper button). Either successful shot pays roughly 1M + 5% of your current score plus its specific award (top-lane awards include Bonus X, playfield multiplier lighting, and Super Jackpot value; playfield-shot awards mostly start a scene or advance ghost/video-mode progress).
Ghosts and Milestones

Ghosts are captured at any of the game's lit-insert shots, by defeating Slimer, completing scenes, and via Storage Facility jackpots. Milestones unlock content automatically: 20 ghosts lights Tobin's Spirit Guide (a 3-5 prize mystery award), 40 lights the "Negative Reinforcement on E.S.P. Ability" video mode, ~49 lights an Extra Ball, 60 starts Loopin' Supers, 80 starts PKE Frenzy, and 100 starts Mass Hysteria Multiball.
Scene Ladders (9 "Scenes" total)

Three ladders, each started at a different shot, must be cleared scene-by-scene: - **Public Library** (Left Scoop, 2 scenes): Spooked Librarian → Back Off, Man! - **Sedgewick Hotel** (Left Ramp, 3 scenes): We Got One! → He Slimed Me! → The Ballroom - **Dana Barrett's Apartment** (Right Orbit, 4 scenes): Okay, Who Brought the Dog? → Spook Central → Gozer the Gozerian → Stay Puft Marshmallow Man
Completing a scene relights its ladder's start shot so you can chain immediately into the next one.
Multiballs

items: **Storage Facility Multiball** — light via the Triple Newton Ball/Tobin's/Pop Bumpers, lock 3 balls at the Left Ramp, then recapture every released ghost for escalating Jackpots and three Super Jackpots.
**Mass Hysteria Multiball** — auto-starts at 100 ghosts; a 6-ball multiball with flippers reversed for the entire duration (its biggest drain risk).

**We Came, We Saw, We Kicked Its...** (mini-wizard) — qualifies by finishing any single ladder; a 2-4 ball multiball where literally every shot pays a flat Super Jackpot, farmed by hammering the Left Ramp.

body.text: Multipliers

Two standups flank the Left Ramp entrance: **2X and 3X Playfield**, which stack **multiplicatively to 6X** on nearly all scoring — the single biggest scoring lever in the game, best saved for the start of a mode or multiball. **Bonus X** (end-of-ball multiplier) builds separately via the P skill-shot lane, Pop Bumpers, and Tobin's.
Combos and Farms

The Left Ramp is the hub of nearly every repeatable scoring pattern: **Collecting Gear** (loop the ramp, cash in at the Library standups), **Loopin' Supers** (continuously-lit Super Jackpots for ~21 seconds), and the We Came We Saw jackpot farm. On the right side, **River of Slime** (Right Orbit → Right Scoop) and **PKE Frenzy** (Right Ramp jackpots fed by a decaying switch-built multiplier) mirror the same build-and-collect structure.
Wizard Modes

Completing all 3 ladders (9 scenes) auto-starts **"We're Ready to Believe You!"** — a 4-ball multiball racing to collect 100 ghosts in 60 seconds across rising ranks (Junior → "Maybe a God?"). Reaching 100 ghosts inside it triggers the final **"Are You a God?"** — Level 1 runs two named 10-second two-shot combos (Left Ramp→Left Scoop, Right Orbit→Right Scoop), Level 2 runs a 7-link forced chain (Slimer → Librarian → Terror Dog → Gozer → both Scoleri Brothers → Right Orbit → Left Ramp), and Level 3 banks a 1-billion-point bonus before a 6-ball victory-lap multiball.
Notable Hazards

This is a physically unforgiving Trudeau design: a wide flipper gap, a center GHOST target that can send airballs straight down the middle, Scoleri Brothers drop targets that can fling the ball over the flippers, and double-inlane geometry that turns near-misses into drains. Play controlled, not desperate, around the multiplier standups and center targets.

name: The Machine: Bride of Pin·Bot
description: The Machine: Bride of Pin-Bot pinball rules: progress the rotating robot Face through Multiball, spin the Big Wheel, and chase the game's Billion-point finales.

body.text: Designed by John Trudeau and Python Anghelo, code by Brian Eddy — Williams' sequel to 1986's Pin·Bot, ~8,100 units produced. The last Williams title with a segmented (non-DMD) score display. There is only one hardware edition; the sole variant is a 2014 third-party Dutch Pinball "2.0" ROM conversion on identical hardware, not covered here.
The core engine: the Shuttle Ramp and the rotating Face

The whole game is built around one progressive objective rather than modern named "modes." The **Shuttle Ramp** feeds a robot head unit whose face physically rotates through four states. Shooting the ramp when it's **unlit** just diverts the ball into the **Pin·Bot mini-playfield** (a repeating 100K-600K scoring ladder that lights an Extra Ball every 7th entry) and returns it to the plunger. Shooting it when **lit** advances the Face:

items: **Activate Voice** (Face 1→2) — 250K
**1st Eye** (Face 2) — 250K, launches a second ball into play
**2nd Eye** (Face 2) — 1M, **starts 2-ball Multiball**, Face becomes 3

body.text: Multiball and Metamorphosis
All scoring doubles during multiball (except Big Wheel awards, Jackpot, and Power Charge). The Face keeps progressing through multiball via more Shuttle Ramp shots, which now **lock** balls:

items: Face 3, 1st shot — **Human Influx** (500K), locks a ball
Face 3, 2nd shot — **Metamorphosis** (1.5M), releases both balls, Face becomes 4 (the Bride's human face)
Face 4, 1st shot — **Increased Pulse** (500K), locks a ball
Face 4, 2nd shot — 2M, releases both balls, awards a **Big Wheel** spin

body.text: The Big Wheel has six outcomes (10M / 50M / Special / 5M / 1M / **Lights 1 Billion**) — Billion must be collected via the **Heartbeat Ramp within 12 seconds** or it's lost. During multiball, shooting the **Left Lane** builds **Power Charge** (100K per shot, capped at 1M, not doubled).
Loops, ramps, and combos

The **Left Loop**, **Right Loop**, and **Heartbeat Ramp** each carry their own escalating shot values (25K→500K for the loops, 100K→1M for the ramp) and all three feed one shared **combo counter**: any 4 loop/ramp shots within roughly 3-4 seconds of each other score a **4-combo (500,000 pts)**, and every shot beyond that (5 through 9) is worth a flat **1,000,000**. A **10-combo** scores the secret **"Backdoor Billion"** — an alternate route to a billion points entirely outside the Big Wheel, though it's exceptionally hard (on the order of 49+ consecutive shots without a drain) and still counts against the game's Billionaire's Club award cap. The Left Loop additionally lights an **Extra Ball** at its 500K tier; the Right Loop contributes toward lighting **Jackpot** (4 shots) and auto-advances the **bonus multiplier** on every exit pass.
Jackpot, Small Wheel, Jets, and the standups

**Jackpot** (1M-8M, built mainly from Jets hits) is lit by a Small Wheel "Light Jackpot" award or four Right Loop shots, then must be collected via the **Left Lane** within 20 seconds. The **Small Wheel** (spun via the Left Lane, outside multiball, when Jackpot isn't lit) awards one of six prizes including Extra Ball. **Jets** pay a flat 10K/hit but roughly 50 hits advance a separate tier-award ladder. Three **standup targets** (one left, two right) advance the **bonus multiplier** when all three are completed.
Multipliers

The **skill-shot multiplier** increases +1x every time the ball returns to the plunger lane (Pin·Bot return, a released lock, a new extra ball). It persists within a ball — including any extra balls played on that same ball-in-play — and resets to 1x only at the true start of each new ball; it can run into the high teens or 20s+ within a long ball. The **bonus multiplier** climbs via the standup targets and free Right Loop advances, and is applied to the end-of-ball bonus (base = loop shots that ball × 10,000).
Extra balls and wizard-level scoring

Extra balls come from the Left Loop (4x quick shots), the Small Wheel, every 7th Pin·Bot entry, and a mercy "WIMP" award for a struggling game; a practical stacking cap sits around 4 EBs. There's no formal named wizard mode in the original ROM — instead there are two independent routes to a billion points: the **Big Wheel Billion** (full Face 1→4 double-lock progression, then a lucky wheel spin collected on the Heartbeat Ramp) and the **Backdoor Billion** (a 10-loop combo chain). Both post to a separate ~19-20 slot **Billionaire's Club** high-score table.
Strategy in one line

Take the skill shot every ball, rush the Shuttle Ramp to reach multiball fast, farm the Left Loop for Extra Ball insurance, then park on the Heartbeat Ramp during multiball for safe, doubled, repeatable points — and avoid the Small Wheel lane and cold Right Loop shots — both are low-value drain risks.

name: Playboy
description: Playboy pinball rules: light all five Grotto Keys, build the Bonus Multiplier up to 5X, and farm the self-feeding Grotto shot for the highest possible scores.

body.text: Bally's *Playboy* (December 1978, ~18,250 units, the #4 all-time bestselling pinball machine) is an early solid-state, two-flipper table themed to Hugh Hefner's Playmates. It predates ramps, multiball, timed modes, and wizard modes entirely — the whole game is a flat, lamp-driven shot-and-collect loop that plays identically from ball one through ball five. No multiball, no ball lock, no timed modes, no video mode, no ramps, and no dedicated skill shot on the plunge.

**The core loop: 5 Keys to the Grotto.** The heart of the ruleset is five "Keys": the four rollover lanes across the top of the playfield (Key #1-4) plus a red center standup (Key #5). Lighting all five in a single ball does two things at once: it advances the Bonus Multiplier one step (1st full completion = 2X, 2nd = 3X, 3rd = 5X, every completion after that scores a 50,000-point Special instead), and it lights the Grotto — an upper-left kickback lane reached via the right orbit or left chute. A shot into the lit Grotto pays out on a graduated table (1 lit key = 1,000 pts + 1 bonus advance, up to 5 lit keys = 5,000 pts + 5 bonus advances + 25,000 points), then kicks the ball back up to the top of the playfield, re-presenting the Key lanes. This is the only shot on the table that both scores big and re-feeds itself, making it the default "farm" for experienced players.

**Bonus and Super Bonus.** Base bonus climbs in 1,000-point steps (fed by Keys, Grotto, and Playmate hits) up to a cap of 39,000 within a ball. Crossing 20,000 locks that value in as a "Super Bonus" floor carried into every later ball (up to 100,000 held). Bonus pays out at ball-end, multiplied by whatever Bonus Multiplier is currently lit — with 5X and a maxed 39,000 base, a single ball-end bonus can reach 195,000, the biggest scoring event available. Because the multiplier holds across the whole game rather than resetting each ball, stacking it to 5X on ball one is the single highest-leverage strategic move. A tilt nullifies the bonus score entirely.

**Secondary banks: Drop Targets and Playmates.** A 5-bank of drop targets (rabbit-head logos) sits top-center / above the bumpers, a horizontal row below the four top Key lanes and in front of the pop bumpers. Clearing it the first time lights both outlanes for 25,000 points (previously a pure drain); clearing it again awards a 50,000 Special, and it resets to repeat. A separate bank of five Playmate standup targets (January/March/May/July/September) runs down the left side; each hit scores 500 points plus a bonus advance, and clearing the full set the first time lights a dedicated rollover button just above the bank for an Extra Ball — clearing it a second time re-lights that rollover for a 50,000 Special instead. Both banks sit in higher-drain territory than the Keys/Grotto loop, so the strategic consensus is to leave them alone except opportunistically — when the ball is already headed there, or only one or two targets remain.

**Specials.** Specials are awarded from three places (4th+ Key-set completion, 2nd+ drop-bank completion, 2nd+ Playmate-bank completion) and are operator-adjustable: typically a free replay, or 50,000 points if the machine is set to score-only.
**Bottom line:** the entire game is Keys, Grotto, Drops, Playmates, and the Bonus ladder — a tight, honest, single-ball ruleset with no hidden modes to chase.

name: Space Jam
description: Space Jam pinball rules: build locks at the Jump Shot to start Multiball, light all Seven Planets, and reach the 60-second Final Jam grand wizard mode.

body.text: Space Jam is a single-edition 1996 Sega Pinball machine (Whitestar hardware, ~800 units built) tied to the Michael Jordan / Looney Tunes film. There is no Pro/Premium/LE split — that convention didn't exist until Stern introduced it around 2016 — so this is the complete ruleset for the one production run. Two flippers, no upper/mini flipper, and a fixed center post between the flippers that explicitly blocks death-save recoveries.
Layout

Clockwise from the drain: SPACE standup bank (lower-left) → Left Orbit → Captive Ball → Left Ramp (a narrow, low-percentage jump-shot, not a true loop) → pop bumper cluster (3) with the Super Duper Jackpot standup dead-center at the back → Monstars drop targets (3) below the pops → Wabbit Hole saucer (center) → Jump Shot lock lane (center-right, the single most important shot in the game) → 23 targets and Right Ramp → Right Orbit → JAM standup bank (lower-right) → shooter lane, feeding a mini basketball hoop ("The Basket") used for the skill shot. Four in/outlanes double as the SLAM lane set.
Skill Shot

While the ball sits in the shooter lane, the DMD cycles an award (flipper buttons change selection): 300,000 points, Lite Lock, Wabbit Hole, or Super Pops. Shoot into the basket to bank it; a miss still scores 50,000. Both flippers held = auto-plunge, still credited. Making the basket with 300k/Lite Lock/Super Pops selected, then hitting the left ramp within a few seconds, adds a Super Skill Shot bonus of +10 basket points.
Multiball

Locks are built at the Jump Shot lane. The very first hit of the game lights all three locks simultaneously — a huge head start — so three more Jump Shot hits lock every ball and launch Multiball (four total Jump Shot hits: one to light all locks, three more to lock balls 1, 2, and 3 and start Multiball). Each subsequent multiball raises the requirement: the 2nd needs one dedicated shot per lock, and each one after that adds another shot, capping at five. Once running, Multiball plays out as four escalating jackpot waves that loop: (1) both ramps lit for Double Jackpot, (2) both orbits plus Jump Shot lit for Jackpot, (3) captive ball for Super Jackpot (base 3,000,000), (4) right ramp lights the center Super Duper Jackpot target for a 15-second window (base 5,000,000, re-lightable by re-shooting the ramp). Base jackpot is 500,000, and every switch hit registered along the way adds 1,000 to the eventual payout — the game's core "let it build before you cash" mechanic.
The Seven Planets (wizard qualification)

Seven objectives light lamps toward the wizard mode: SLAM (clear all 4 SLAM lanes once), IN YER FACE (3 captive-ball hits, unlocked by knocking the Monstars drops twice), FIRE (4 right-ramp shots), SPACE JAM (clear both SPACE and JAM banks, which also starts the 45-second Superjam mode), REBOUND (25 pop bumper hits), FAST BREAK (5 shots to each orbit, after which the right ramp becomes an escalating 200k→700k shot), and SUPER JACKPOT (score one during regular Multiball). Lighting all seven and shooting the left ramp starts **Final Jam** — a 60-second, all-5-balls-in-play wizard mode where every switch hit anywhere adds 10,000 to a running pot and every basket make collects the full accumulated value before it resets and keeps building. This is the sole terminal wizard mode.
Wabbit Hole

Lit by clearing both red "23" standups beside the right ramp. Hitting it shows three of a pool of possible awards and auto-selects one; awards stack and carry across balls until collected. Confirmed pool includes flat points, 1-on-1 and 2-on-2 mini-multiballs, Video Mode, a drop-target Defence hurry-up, Super Pops, and Full Court Frenzy — a rare 5-ball multiball with all six arrow shots lit, an escalating value, and an unusually long ball-save, the single biggest scoring opportunity in the game.
Bonus Multiplier

The only multiplier is Bonus X, advanced by completing all four SLAM lanes (the in/outlanes double-duty as letter lanes). It caps at 6X, and reaching it lights a free Extra Ball at the Jump Shot — good synergy since Jump Shot is already the priority shot all game. End-of-ball bonus is 10,000 per basket/orbit/ramp/Jump Shot switch made that ball, times Bonus X, plus a flat bonus per planet lit.
Basket Points (secondary track)

A separate scoring ladder running alongside normal points: captive ball = 2, left ramp = 3, left ramp during FIRE or as a Super Skill Shot = 10. 23 basket points banks 300,000; 45 points grants a direct Extra Ball.
Strategy in brief

There is no dedicated "combo" system (no combo meter/timer/named combo awards — this predates that design convention), but the game has clear repeatable money sequences: the jackpot wave loop, the Superjam chain, and Fast Break's ramping right-ramp value. The dominant strategy is to spam the Jump Shot almost exclusively pre-multiball (it's the highest-percentage, most important shot and the direct route to locks — four total hits: light all locks, then lock balls 1, 2, and 3 to start Multiball), picking up SLAM/SPACE/JAM/pop-bumper progress only incidentally, then broaden out to the full ramp/orbit/captive-ball jackpot geometry once Multiball is actually running and those shots pay real jackpot value. The left ramp is a low-percentage, hard-to-make shot and should not be chased early. No forgiving ball-save exists beyond the skill shot, and the fixed center post removes the classic death-save recovery, so aggressive nudging and rushed shots (especially under the Super Duper Jackpot's 15-second countdown) are genuine drain risks.

name: Tales from the Crypt
description: Tales from the Crypt pinball rules: spell CRYPT for Crypt Multiball, run the 12 Creature Features, and reach the Crypt Jam wizard mode, the game's finale.

body.text: Designed by John Borg, released Nov/Dec 1993 (~4,500 units). Single production release — no Pro/Premium/LE editions exist; that convention postdates this era. The only meaningful variance is ROM revision (factory 2.x, 3.01, 3.03, plus an unofficial fan rebalance "v4.00" many home/route operators run) which changes scoring values, not the physical layout.
Layout basics

Three flippers: standard lower-left and lower-right, plus a 3rd upper-right flipper that feeds and catches returns from the Electric Chair scoop and center spinner — the two most-repeated shots in the game. Two ramps (Left Ramp, Right Ramp) each cross the top of the playfield and drop into the *opposite* inlane. Two orbit spinners (left, right) loop into each other. A 3-target drop-target bank ("Guillotine") doubles as the skill-shot target. A large Tombstone standup blocks the Crypt eject hole until spelled open. Six eyeball standup targets (K-E-E / P-E-R) spell KEEPER. A captive ball sits lower-left. Three pop bumpers cluster top-center.
Skill shot

An auto-plunge sends the ball up and into the shooter lane where it drops on the Guillotine bank; a light travels across the 3 targets as the ball travels. Landing on the lit target pays 2M on ball 1, 3M on ball 2, +1M each ball after. The ball saver covers only the first two skill-shot attempts of the game.
CRYPT spelling and Crypt Multiball

Hitting the Tombstone spots C-R-Y-P-T letters in sequence. 'C' is auto-spotted at game start, and the game continues auto-spotting letters between balls so that a well-played ball 3 nearly guarantees CRYPT is complete. Once spelled, the Tombstone lowers, opening the Crypt VUK — shoot the Crypt (or, the first time only, the center spinner) to start **Crypt Multiball**. The designed money loop is: Left Ramp = Jackpot (base 25M, built by left-spinner spins and Crypt hits) → Right Ramp = Double Jackpot (2x the Jackpot, min 50M) → hit the Tombstone 5 times to respell CRYPT and light Monster Jackpot (50M + Double Jackpot value, min 100M, +50M every repeat) → loop back to the Left Ramp. Captive-ball hits add balls before the Double Jackpot is collected.
Creature Features (12 modes)

The center scoop ("Electric Chair") starts whichever Creature Feature (CF) is currently flashing on the playfield's door-mechanism display. Shooting either orbit spinner cycles which CF is flashing; the door-handle plunger button locks the current one in (press again to unlock) before it rotates to something worse. All 12 CFs — Thunder Storm, Lite Skull Cracking, Door Prize Select (the game's one video mode), Frightmare, Psycho Pops, Robbing the Crypt, Lite Extra Ball, Super Guillotine Targets, Lite Werewolf Countdown, Lite Super Crypt Kicker, Electric Chair, and Super Keeper Targets — can run concurrently with each other and even during multiball, and stacking two at once is the closest thing the game has to a genuine scored "combo" system. Two CFs are themselves multiballs: **Electric Chair Multiball** (instant 6-ball, scoop pays 1M x balls in play) and **Skull Cracking** (20-sec captive-ball add-a-ball, escalating per-hit value).
Multipliers

The **Bonus Multiplier** (2x→4x→6x→8x, then flat 1M/hit) is advanced by clearing the Guillotine bank or fully spelling KEEPER, and applies only to the end-of-ball bonus. The **Right Orbit Loop** value escalates on consecutive, uninterrupted right-spinner shots (roughly 0.5M→1M→1.5M→2M→2.5M, capping and repeating). There is no general playfield-wide "X" multiplier — the game's other escalating values (Fast Goring frenzy tiers, Super Guillotine/Keeper per-target growth, Crypt Multiball's balls-in-play scaling) are self-contained inside their own modes.
Fast Goring frenzies

Collecting 4 "bat" lights via the Left Ramp advances a 15-second Frenzy tier started via the Right Ramp: Living Dead → Chainsaw Mode → Grave Digger → Play the Organ, each raising the flat per-switch value (roughly 250K/500K/750K/1M). Best farmed with multiple balls in play during Crypt Multiball.
Wizard mode — Crypt Jam

Complete all 12 Creature Features at least once each to light the scoop for **Crypt Jam**, the game's single wizard mode: a 6-ball multiball with a 25-second ball saver where every switch hit scores a flat 1M while 2 or more balls remain in play. There is no deeper second-tier wizard mode.
Strategy notes

Chase multiball over grinding single modes — nearly every big number scales with balls in play. Once in multiball, spam the scoop shot off the upper-right flipper (it returns directly to that flipper, making it the most controllable repeat shot in the game). The left outlane is a live drain unless KEEPER is lit — hit any K-E-E target early to relight the kickback. Route center shots off the upper-right flipper rather than the lower flippers, since scoop mishits from below feed straight down the middle.

name: Terminator 2: Judgment Day
description: Terminator 2 pinball rules: load the Cannon to start Multiball, complete Payback Time's Security ladder, and farm the Chase Loop and Escape Route award ladder.

body.text: Designed by Steve Ritchie (programming Dwight Sullivan, art Doug Watson), T2 was a single production run of ~15,202 units — no Pro/Premium/LE split exists; the only variance across machines is ROM revision. It pioneered the gun-grip trigger auto-launcher (no plunger rod) and one of pinball's first mandatory ball-savers.
Skill Shot

No manual plunger — pull the trigger to auto-launch, then time a second trigger pull to hit the lit target on the moving 5-bank of standups. First success pays 1,000,000; each subsequent ball's successful skill shot is worth 1,000,000 more than the last.
Multiball — the Cannon

Knock down the **skull drop target** (center, below the T-800 skull graphic) to feed a saucer that loads the motorized **Cannon**. Pull the trigger as the Cannon swings past its lit standup to fire and start a 2-ball multiball. During multiball, the ball already loaded in the Cannon counts as the first lock; re-lock further balls at up to three saucers — the left eject (Database) saucer, the left orbit saucer, and the skull saucer — to raise the Jackpot multiplier: 1 ball locked = 1x (10M), 2 locked = 2x (20M), 3 locked = 3x (30M), fired by the Cannon again. Collecting a 2x or 3x Jackpot lights **Super Jackpot** (50,000,000): reload the Cannon and hit the independently-moving skill-shot target while another ball is still live. Multiple Super Jackpots are possible per multiball.
Modes and awards

items: **Payback Time** — Alternate the **left ramp** (Cyberdyne AI Lab) and **right ramp** (Skynet Command Center); each ramp needs 5 hits, alternating, to light 10 "Security" circles (each consecutive alternating shot also pays 1,000,000). Completing all 10 auto-starts a ~20-second window where 6 shots — both ramps, the chase loop, the skull drop target, the escape-route saucer, and the 3 green pop-bumper timer lights — each pay a flat 5,000,000 in any order. This is T2's closest thing to a climactic mode; there is **no true wizard mode**.

**Chase Loop (right orbit)** — An escalating value ladder: 250K → 500K → 750K → 1M → 1.25M → 5M, then sticky at 5M for the rest of the ball (resets each new ball). Fast consecutive shots stack an uncapped "Million Plus" bonus (+1M per quick consecutive make) on top.

**Escape Route** — A 6-step award ladder advanced by completing the **red center 3-bank** and collected at the **left orbit saucer** (the kickout hole isn't directly shootable — it's fed via the left orbit): Security Pass → Hold Bonus → Return Lanes (unlocks Hurry-Up and Video Mode) → Multiball → Extra Ball → 10,000,000. Carries over ball to ball; an aggressive timer applies from step 4 onward.
**Hurry-Up** — Qualified via the Escape Route return lanes or a Database award. Starts at 15,000,000, decays to a 3,000,000 floor over ~15 seconds; collected at the right orbit.

**Video Mode** — Pinball's first-ever video mode. Qualified the same way as Hurry-Up, collected at the left orbit; use the flipper buttons to shoot descending Terminators (3 shots per wave) on the DMD.

**Database** — Shoot the lit left eject saucer for a random pull from a 16-item award table (Extra Ball, Multiball, Hurry-Up, points, Video Mode, Chase Loop Advance, and more). The skull saucer does not award Database — it only loads the Cannon and serves as a Jackpot-multiplier lock location.

body.text: Multipliers

items: **Bonus Multiplier (2X–8X)**: advanced by completing the 3 top lanes (repeatedly); maxing it out (6X or 8X, operator-adjustable) lights an Extra Ball at the skull drop target. **Hold Bonus** (Escape Route award #2) carries accumulated bonus and multiplier into the next ball (doubled if collected on ball 3).

**Jackpot Multiplier**: a separate system tied to how many balls are locked during multiball, counting the ball already loaded in the Cannon as the first lock (1/2/3 balls locked = 1x/2x/3x), independent of Bonus X.

body.text: Extra Balls (four paths)
Maxing Bonus X; Escape Route award #5; a random Database pull; and catching the falling Extra Ball box in Video Mode.
Combos and money shots

T2 predates the modern on-DMD "COMBO!" callout but has two real chaining mechanics: the **ramp-alternation Security combo** (1M per consecutive alternating ramp shot) and the **Chase Loop Million Plus** stack (uncapped +1M per fast consecutive right-orbit shot once the base ladder caps at 5M). The top human-executed scoring line is running a Cannon multiball while Payback Time is also active, so ramps, the chase loop, and Jackpots all pay simultaneously.
Physical layout

Two ramps (left/AI Lab, right/Skynet), two orbits (left/Escape Route, right/Chase Loop), a center skull drop target feeding a saucer and the Cannon, a red 3-bank of standups, a moving 5-bank skill-shot target, 3 pop bumpers under a large chrome skull toy, 3 top lanes, and a gun-grip trigger launcher — no spinner or captive ball on this table.

name: White Water
description: White Water pinball rules: clear the seven Hazard shots, build River Class, collect the six Whirlpool Awards, and reach the Vacation Bonus wizard mode.

body.text: Designed by Dennis Nordman, programmed by Mike Boon, art by John Youssi. A widebody WPC (Fliptronics II) title, 7,008 units produced. No Pro/Premium/LE editions — that convention didn't exist yet in 1993. Rule variance is by ROM revision only (notably L-3 vs L-4+), affecting a few point values and 5X interactions noted below.
Layout in brief

Two main flippers plus a single **upper flipper** on a raised upper playfield. Seven named **Hazard** shots form the backbone of the ruleset: **No Way Out** (center lock scoop, flanked by two green Lite Lock targets), **Spine Chiller** (left ramp to the upper deck), **Disaster Drop** (center ramp/loop that runs under the upper deck and drops out near Boulder Garden), **Boulder Garden** (left orbit), **Boomerang Bend** (right orbit, the hardest shot in the game), **Insanity Falls** (upper-playfield ramp, shot with the upper flipper, doubles as the Multiball Jackpot and Skill Shot), and **Bigfoot Bluff** (upper-playfield ramp guarded by the animated Bigfoot figure, who normally diverts the ball into the **Whirlpool** unless distracted). Other key features: **Lost Mine** (scoop, also the Whirlpool's exit point), the 5-target **R-I-V-E-R** bank, the 2-target green **Lite Lock**, the 3-target red **Light Bounceback** bank, the 2-target white **Hotfoot** bank, an **Extra Ball** standup, and the hidden **Secret Passage** rollover reached only by a soft Boulder Garden shot.
Skill Shot

A gentle-medium plunge sends the ball onto the upper deck and into Insanity Falls, worth an escalating 1M→5M across the game. Too hard a plunge overshoots into Spine Chiller instead (5K consolation on later ROMs).
Hazards & Raft

Each of the 7 Hazards pays 500K × current **River Class** when lit (50K flat unlit). Completing the currently-lit set advances your **Raft** number (1M × destination raft) and relights a new set — roughly 1-5 shots required per raft as you climb. Eight completed rafts leads to **Wet Willie's**.
River Class (multiplier)
Complete the 5 R-I-V-E-R standups (or roll the currently-lit inlane) to advance River Class 1→6. It multiplies both lit-Hazard value and the end-of-ball bonus, but resets to 1 every new ball.
Whirlpool Awards (6-step cycle)

Shoot Insanity Falls to light the current award, then collect it at Bigfoot Bluff: (1) **Whirlpool Challenge** (2-ball multiball, escalating Bigfoot Bluff hits), (2) **Man Overboard** (hurry-up, all lit Hazards worth 20M counting down to 3M), (3) **Light Extra Ball**, (4) **Advance Raft**, (5) **Mystery Canyon** (random bonus), (6) **5X Playfield** (25-second full-scoring multiplier, hard cutoff, no grace period).
Multiball

Hit both green Lite Lock targets to light lock, then shoot No Way Out — three locks (two-hit pattern each) starts Multiball with all 3 balls fed to the upper-right flipper. The opening volley through Insanity Falls sets the Jackpot tier for the rest of the multiball: 3/3 = Triple, 2/3 = Double, 0-1/3 = Single. Base Jackpot ≈10M, +2M per Raft advanced. No ball-save during multiball.
Bigfoot Hotfoot & Camera Craze

Hitting the two white Hotfoot targets (default ~3-4 hits) distracts Bigfoot for ~20 seconds — Bigfoot Bluff shots pay repeat 10M Jackpots and spot Lost Mine items (flashlight, map, key, camera, cow) in sequence. Collecting the camera (4th item) triggers **Camera Craze**: every Hazard except No Way Out pays a flat 3M for the rest of the ball.
Gold Rush
Collect the flashlight, map, and key (via Lost Mine or Hotfoot), then shoot Lost Mine again to start a 2-ball multiball where every switch hit scores 250K.
Boulder Bash
Every 3rd Boulder Garden hit triggers a 20-second window of escalating Jet Bumper value.
Wet Willie's

Reached after climbing the Raft ladder. Stage 1: all 7 Hazards lit at once, 10M each, collect all seven. Stage 2: a single travelling hazard light rotates through the same 7 shots every ~3 seconds for a 25-second window, 100M per hit (50M on early ROMs); draining resets you to Raft #2.
Combos

Every combo starts **Spine Chiller → Insanity Falls** (2M). Extending to No Way Out, Disaster Drop, or Boomerang Bend makes a 3-way (5M). Looping back through Insanity Falls from the No Way Out branch makes a 4-way (8-10M depending on ROM). Extending that with Disaster Drop or Boomerang Bend completes a 5-way (10M, ~25M+ stacked total) — the hardest shot in the game, tuned around a deliberately difficult backhand off the upper flipper.
Wizard Mode — Vacation Bonus

Requires four legs completed in one game: River Class 6, Wet Willie's started, all 6 Whirlpool Awards collected, and all 3 balls locked. Locking the 3rd ball once legs 1-3 are done pays the Vacation Bonus (200M + 10K × prior games played) plus a Special, then starts an elevated Multiball. Competitively deprioritized — most players score more from repeated Multiball/Hotfoot cycles than chasing it.
End-of-ball bonus
(50K × Hazards collected + 75K × Rafts advanced + 100K × Whirlpool Awards collected) × River Class. River Class resets each ball, so bonus does too.

name: World Cup Soccer
description: World Cup Soccer pinball rules: light the four BUILD shots for Multiball, travel between nine cities, and beat Germany in the Final Match wizard mode.

body.text: Designed by John Popadiuk and Larry DeMar (software: DeMar/Matt Coriale; art: Kevin O'Connor; callouts: Tim Kitzrow), released February 1994 on Midway's WPC-S hardware, roughly 8,743 units built. There is no Pro/Premium/LE tiering — this predates that convention entirely, and it's a single production run. Notably, WCS94 has **only two standard flippers** — no upper, lower, or mini-flipper — unusual for a WPC-era title. The **Magna-Save** is a player-activated magnet (not a flipper) that catches a ball headed for the center drain.
Core shots

Two orbits/ramps mirror each other: the **Left Spiral** (orbit, hosts the Ultra Spinner and city travel) and **Left/Right Ramps** (feed BUILD, multiball lock, and Ultra Ramps). Center stage is the **GOAL** — a wide net hole guarded by a moving plastic **goalie**, fed either directly or safely via the **Assist saucer** (upper-left, flipper-fired straight past the goalie). A **spinning rubber soccer ball** toy sits upper-mid-playfield and deflects shots unpredictably when Goal is lit or during multiball. Other shots: twin **Free Kick saucers/target**, **Striker standups** (spell S-T-R-I-K-E-R), **Star Rollovers** (relight Goal), **Striker Scoop** (mystery awards + Extra Ball), **TV/Final Draw scoop** (dual-purpose: TV Awards and Multiball start), 3 **jet bumpers**, and a real mechanical **plunger** feeding a 3-way Skill Shot divider.
Skill Shot
Manual plunge into one of three flashing top-lane dividers: 1st = 5M, 2nd = 10M, 3rd = 30M + spots a city. Clearing all three across the game nets a bonus city.
Multiball

Four flashing **BUILD** shots (left spiral, left ramp, right ramp, Striker scoop) each light a word on the soccer-ball graphic — Strength, Stamina, Skill, Speed, Spirit. All five lit → **Lock** (physically held on the left ramp's upper shelf). Shoot the lit **Final Draw** scoop to start. A random Striker Scoop award can also start multiball (guaranteed on ball 3 if not yet achieved, but low starting rank). Multiball is **ranked** against 15 national teams, USA (20M) up through Germany (250M) — Goal scores the jackpot and beats the current team; either ramp relights Goal and advances rank. The Assist saucer is scripted not to miss during multiball, making it the most reliable jackpot loop. Draining before a jackpot lets you resume via a ramp or the scoop. Beating Germany lights **Special** at the right outlane and unlocks flat 50M **Victory Laps** (Goal/ramps, alternating after 5 laps).
Modes

**Ultra Modes** (Ramps, Spinner, Jets, Goalie) are awarded one per Goal scored, stack up to all four concurrently, and cap at 30M + 10M bonus each — but only pay out through end-of-ball bonus, not live score. **TV Awards** run in a fixed sequence at the Final Draw scoop, re-lit every 4 Goals: Big Goal Round (3 Goal shots, 15/15/30M), Extra Ball Round, Hit The Goalie!, and Where's Striker (3 Striker standup hits). **Boston Tea Party** is a hurry-up (40M counting to a 10M floor, collected at the left spiral) unlocked by traveling to Boston.
Cities and travel

Nine cities (Chicago, Dallas, Boston, New York, Orlando, Washington DC, San Francisco, Detroit, Los Angeles) are advanced by lighting TRAVEL at the left spiral (both ramps or both top lanes, then shoot the spiral), by a Striker "Advance Three Cities" award, or by clearing all three Skill Shot lanes. Washington DC lights Extra Ball; reaching Los Angeles (9th city) qualifies the wizard mode.
Multipliers

There is **no true 2X/3X playfield or bonus multiplier** anywhere on this table. The closest analogues are escalating values: jet bumpers jump from 100K to a flat 1M/pop for the rest of the ball after 25,000 cumulative hits, and the Super Free Kick award climbs +5M per consecutive Free Kick target hit from a 10M base.
Wizard mode — Final Match

Reach Los Angeles (9th city) and shoot the lit Final Draw scoop to start a 45-second, 5-ball timed multiball against Germany, every ball manually plunged. Each Goal scored is worth 75M; Germany accrues its own virtual counter. Beat their total at the buzzer for a 500M bonus; a tie forces sudden-death overtime.
Bonus

Unusually, end-of-ball bonus draws on **career (whole-game) totals**: 5M per Goal scored so far this entire game + 5M per city traveled to this entire game + that ball's own Ultra Mode earnings — no bonus multiplier applies, and a tilt forfeits it.
Strategy

Center drain is the dominant killer (roughly 7 of 10 balls lost down the middle), so trapping discipline matters more than on most contemporaries lacking an upper flipper for playfield control. Two competing high-score approaches: safe "Goal-only" grinding (Goal → relight → repeat, banking Ultra bonus, no lock/drain risk) versus rushing the 4 BUILD shots to lock and grind the ranked multiball jackpot ladder up to Germany's Victory Laps, the single best sustained per-shot value in the game.

name: Labyrinth
description: Labyrinth pinball rules: spell LABYRINTH to start the six modes, level up your Friends, collect all 13 Orbs, and battle through to Battle Jareth wizard mode.

body.text: Labyrinth is a boutique, single-configuration title (MSRP ~$10,600, 1,100-unit run — no Pro/Premium/LE split) themed to Jim Henson's 1986 film. Design: David Van Es, rules by Phil Grimaldi and Bowen Kerins, on the FAST pinball platform. It has three flippers (two lower, one upper-right) and no pop bumpers.
Skill Shots

Seven plunge-strength options route the ball to different first shots — Ello Worm (short), Wiseman scoop (medium-strong, sets up a **Super Skill Shot combo** if followed immediately by the bridge/inner loop off the upper flipper for 1.2M), the Change Mode target (**Target Skillshot**, the highest flat value and double-duty toward mode progress), the bridge/inner loop, "Egdirb" (a reverse-loop mis-route), or the back Village scoop (long plunge). Values scale roughly ×2 on ball 2 and ×3 on ball 3.
Modes (6 total, in two tiers of three)

Spell **LABYRINTH** on white-arrow shots to flash Start Mode inserts at the Horseshoe, then shoot the Horseshoe (either side) or the Wiseman scoop to launch the lit mode. The **Change Mode** target cycles which mode is lit within its tier (upper: Knockers/Four Guards/Fireys; lower: Cleaners/Oubliette/Bog). Spelling **HELP** at the in/outlanes arms Sir Didymus's ball-save post and lights Helping Hands scoop to finish LABYRINTH or swap tiers.

items: **The Knockers** — pass the ring on yellow shots, hold the knocker's nose at the Wiseman drop target, replace the ring at the scoop, open the door at the right orbit.
**The Four Guards** — toggle four shots red/blue, reveal the true color at center ramp/bridge, answer at the right Horseshoe.
**The Fireys** — a 2-ball mini-multiball: pop Firey heads at the captive ball (add-a-ball, capped at 5), relight forks with red-arrow shots, chase the roving Super Jackpot.
**The Bog of Eternal Stench** — a 5-shot discrimination sequence (left ramp → right ramp → left orbit → right Horseshoe → right orbit) avoiding the green "Bog" shots.
**The Oubliette** — hit any lit violet door, then a different lit door to move the flash, hit it twice to escape; five doors total.
**The Cleaners** — timed; spin the left-orbit spinner to build a hurry-up, collect at the right orbit, repeatable 3 times before the "13th hour" clock expires.

body.text: Multiballs

**Brick Keeper** locks via wall/Fairy targets then green targets at left orbit, center ramp, and right orbit; red-arrow jackpots light the forks for a captive-ball-into-spinner Super Jackpot. **Friend Multiball** starts at Helping Hands scoop once all three Friends (Hoggle/Ludo/Sir Didymus) have a jackpot. **Tea Time Multiball** starts from an Ello Mystery award; orbit shots multiply and Horseshoe shots increase a hurry-up banked under the left ramp. **Wiseman Multiball** auto-starts on the 4th completed Wiseman Quest, scoring jackpots at the Wiseman scoop.
Friends, Quests, and Mystery

Hoggle/Ludo/Sir Didymus each level up 1-4 through found items and collected jackpots, granting scoring bonuses, easier locks, and ball-save perks; Level 4 lights a Collect Orb insert for each. **Wiseman Quests** are started by knocking down the Wiseman drop target and shooting the scoop; each of 6 completions adds +1x Bonus Multiplier, with milestones lighting Friendzy, Extra Ball, Wiseman Multiball, and an Orb. **Ello Mystery** awards are lit by hitting the paired Wiseman targets and collected at the lane under the upper flipper.
The Orb System and Wizard Modes

Thirteen Orbs — one from each mode, each Friend at Level 4, Brick Keeper (5 cumulative Super Jackpots), Wiseman Quests (6 completions), Friend Multiball, and Goblin City — are each lit by their achievement and collected at the lane under the upper flipper (10M + a stacking "rainbow" multiplier). Completing all 3 modes on one tier triggers **Poisoned Peach**, a timed mini-wizard mode where ramp-to-ramp combos power up two drop targets that must each be hit twice to break the spell. Completing all 6 modes qualifies **Goblin City Multiball**, a three-phase wizard mode (Defeat The Gate → Evade Capture → Counterattack) ending in an all-shots-lit jackpot frenzy. Collecting all 13 Orbs qualifies **Battle Jareth**, the super/ultimate wizard mode, where draining or hitting the mode clock's "13" costs an Orb.
Strategy in Brief

Open with the Target Skillshot, take an early Friend shot, and start a Wiseman Quest as soon as possible so its multiplier compounds all ball. New players should aim for The Knockers or The Oubliette first (simplest execution) over The Bog or The Four Guards. At a competitive level, Orbs — not any single combo shot — are the real currency: prioritize clearing modes, grinding Quests, and cashing every lit Orb over farming one shot repeatedly.

name: Night Moves
description: Night Moves pinball rules: build the N-I-G-H-T-MOVES bonus ladder, work the Lock/Switch/Release multiball chain, and light the rare Double Entire Score award.

body.text: Night Moves is a rare (roughly 450 units), single-level **cocktail-table** pinball machine — no backbox, just a flat playfield with the alphanumeric display embedded directly in the surface, and only **two flippers total** for up to 4 players sharing them via buttons on opposite cabinet edges. Built by Premier/Gottlieb on System 80B hardware for the International Concepts label, designed by John Trudeau, model C101. It's also a **2-ball-game cabinet** — the trough only holds two balls, which is why its multiball is hard-capped at exactly 2 balls.
The bonus engine: N-I-G-H-T-MOVES

Two standup-target banks — **CLUB** (4 targets) and **RIO** (3 targets) — score 10,000/target while flashing and **self-reset on completion**, making them the game's primary grindable shots. Completing either bank advances one letter of a six-segment **N-I-G-H-T-MOVES** bonus ladder and flashes a random **Collect Bonus** lamp at one of the two Holes. Shooting a Hole while Collect Bonus flashes pays **50,000 points per letter lit** (up to 300,000, doubled to 600,000 with 2X Bonus active) — the single largest explicit single-shot value in the ruleset. Completing all six letters lights the **Top Right Spot Target** for **Special**.
Lock, Switch, and Multiball

The **Left Hole** and **Right Hole** run an unusually plumbed three-step chain: 1. **Lock** — shoot a Hole while its LOCK lamp flashes: captures the ball, serves a fresh one, and starts the opposite Hole's SWITCH lamp flashing. 2. **Switch** — shoot the opposite Hole while SWITCH flashes: captures a ball there too, cancels the first lock, and kicks the original ball back into play. This *relocates* the lock; it does not by itself start multiball. 3. **Release** — pop bumpers and slingshots toggle a **Multiball Release** lamp on/off whenever a ball is captured. Once Release is flashing, shooting the **Upper Right Side Rollover** kicks the locked ball out to join the live ball for genuine simultaneous **2-ball multiball**. There is **no jackpot of any kind**. Multiball's only benefit is doubling your shot rate for normal points until the balls drain back to one.
Display Feature Award (the closest thing to a "mode")

Night Moves predates mode-based design — there are no named story modes and **no documented automatic skill shot**. The nearest equivalent is the **Display Feature Award**: any Return Rollover or R-O-C-K rollover arms a random award, then shooting the **Upper Left Side Rollover** while it's flashing collects the value (or 50,000) plus one of: light Special, light Extra Ball, score 500,000, light 2X Bonus, Collect 4X Bonus, Win Extra Ball, or **Double Entire Score** — the single biggest possible payout in the game, and the closest thing to a wizard-mode endpoint (there is no actual wizard mode of any kind).
Multiplier

There's exactly one persistent multiplier: a binary **2X Bonus** lamp, lit via the **Top "Lite 2X" Rollovers** or as a Display Feature Award outcome. It doubles Hole-shot Collect Bonus payouts. The **right flipper button** (a standalone input) rotates lit Extra Ball/R-O-C-K lamps and freezes the current 2X state — useful right before a big cash-in. A separate one-shot **Collect 4X Bonus** award multiplies the current bonus once rather than persisting.
Other scoring

**R-O-C-K rollovers** (4 lanes) light Extra Ball on completion, or pay 100,000 flat if EB is already won. **Return Rollovers** pay 3,000, award EB when lit, and briefly flash the **Spinner** to 25,000 (vs. 5,000 base) — the only stated timed shot-value window in the whole ruleset. **Outlanes** pay 50,000 and award EB when lit rather than being pure drains. Only **one extra ball is awarded per ball-in-play** regardless of how many EB conditions stack. **Tilting wipes all accumulated bonus and multipliers outright** — the costliest mistake available once you're carrying ladder letters.
There are no Pro/Premium/LE editions and no rules differences across the cabinet-hardware variants collectors discuss — one C101 ruleset, period.

name: Star Trek
description: Star Trek pinball rules: complete six Missions across three levels each, run the three Vengeance rounds, and reach the Five Year Mission grand wizard mode.

body.text: Designed by Steve Ritchie, licensed to the 2009/2013 J.J. Abrams film reboot. Three editions — Pro, Premium, LE — share an identical ruleset and physical layout; Premium/LE add a motorized "crash" Vengeance ship, a star-field laser, a left-outlane kickback, and a VUK that safely feeds the left scoop into the left ramp (Pro's scoop kicks out unpredictably). None of this changes scoring, modes, or multiball logic.
The playfield

Seven major shots anchor everything: **Left Orbit** (houses the spinner), **Left Ramp**, **Right Ramp**, **Warp Ramp** (reachable only from the upper-right/third flipper), **Right Orbit**, **Left Scoop** ("Mission Start"), and the center **Vengeance** drop target/ship — the most dangerous shot on the table, prone to rebounding hard toward the outlanes. Supporting hardware includes Shield standups, a bank of 3 green "lock" standups, a bank of 3 orange Weapon standups (loads torpedoes fired via the "Punch It" lockdown-bar button), a scattered family of Red Matter/Black Hole standups, three top BEAM-ME-UP rollover lanes, and a pop-bumper nest.
Skill shots

There's no traditional "flip the lit lane" skill shot. Instead: a soft plunge sets up a **Warp Ramp Skill Shot** off the upper-right flipper; holding the left flipper on a full plunge lights a **Super Skill Shot** (1M, +250K each repeat) at Vengeance or the right ramp; holding the right flipper for a full-power plunge that rejects off the top gate into the right orbit sets up the **Super Warp Skill Shot** (1.5M, the highest-value but riskiest option).
Missions (the "modes")

Six color-coded Missions — Prime Directive, Space Jump, Save the Enterprise, Nero, Destroy the Drill, Klingon Battle — each played across three Levels (18 mode instances total). Start any lit mission at **Mission Start** (left scoop) or **Away Team** (upper-flipper shot). Level I is a timed shot-collection pattern (Bronze/Silver/Gold medal thresholds); taking Away Team mid-timer adds +20 seconds and unlocks a bonus "Galactic Mode" shot sequence. Level II and III raise the complexity (roving shots, attacker pairs, dynamically-shifting lit shots) and medal thresholds. Fully clearing a mission's Level III permanently lights a dedicated shot for 2X scoring for the rest of the game (e.g., Nero → Left Orbit, Klingon Battle → Left Ramp).
Multiballs

items: **Klingon Multiball**: complete the 3 green standups to light locks at Vengeance and the left scoop; lock 3 balls to start. Jackpots climb from 200K, with a 7th-jackpot 6.25M Super Jackpot, 14th-jackpot 10M Super Jackpot, a traveling 4M Double Jackpot, and a 20M **Double Super Jackpot at the Warp Ramp** (plus a free Gold medal).

**Vengeance Multiball** (round 1 of 3 sequential Vengeance rounds): build hits on Vengeance via direct shots or Punch It torpedoes (any of the 10 shots except the final one may be a torpedo); starts 2-ball with a magnet-capture mechanic, extends to 3-ball, and destroying the ship after 10 shots pays 5M and unlocks escalating "Victory Lap" shot loops.
**Vengeance Scoring** (round 2): a hurry-up requiring 5 direct shots to Vengeance — the only repeatable Extra Ball source in the game.

**Vengeance Battle** (round 3): raise then knock down the Vengeance target, then land a sudden-death shot worth the greater of 10M or 10% of total score (up to 40% comboed under Double Scoring) — the single biggest lever in the ruleset.

body.text: Combos

Every major shot carries a red combo insert that stays lit for ~4 seconds after the prior shot; hitting a different eligible shot within the window doubles its value (repeating the same shot does not combo). Five named "crew combos" — **Kirk** (Left Orbit→Warp Ramp), **Bones** (Left Orbit→Left Ramp), **Sulu** (Right Orbit→Right Ramp), **Uhura** (Right Ramp→Left Ramp→Right Orbit), and **Spock** (Left Ramp→Right Ramp→Left Orbit→Warp Ramp) — each pay a flat 1,000,000 the first time and permanently raise the base value of all future combos.
Multipliers

Completing the three **BEAM-ME-UP** top lanes adds +1X to that ball's bonus multiplier (resets each ball). Repeated **Warp Ramp** shots climb a Warp Speed counter: 7 shots lights a one-time Extra Ball (collected at Vengeance), 10 shots lights 60 seconds of global 2X scoring, and 18 shots re-lights 2X scoring plus adds a ball into play (both repeatable after the first time).
Captain's Chair

Completing three same-level missions in a row lights a bonus tied to the side of the playfield: left-side missions → Super Pops, right-side → Super Ramps, bottom-row → Super Spinner. Super Ramps is generally considered the best single pick for players who can only manage one line.
Wizard modes

Qualification is built on finishing an entire Level of all 6 missions, which lights the center Vengeance shot white: 1. **Kobayashi Maru** (after all 6 Level I's) — 2-ball multiball where every shot needs 2 hits. 2. **Enterprise Amok** (after all 6 Level II's) — 2-ball multiball across 6 escalating switch-hit rounds. 3. **Five Year Mission** (after all 6 Level III's, the true final wizard mode) — 4-ball multiball, clear every lit shot for a Super Jackpot.
Strategy in brief

Open with the Super Skill Shot, launch a default Level I mission, use Away Team to extend it, and work toward Klingon Multiball locks and Warp Ramp shots. Tournament players deliberately start a mode just before locking the final multiball ball so mode scoring and jackpots run concurrently, save Double Scoring for a jackpot-heavy moment, and treat Vengeance Scoring/Battle as high-value, single-purpose detours rather than shots to chase mid-mode.

name: Twilight Zone
description: Twilight Zone pinball rules: spell GUMBALL for locks, collect all 15 rotating Door Panels, and reach the Lost in the Zone six-ball wizard mode finale.

body.text: Designed by Pat Lawlor (co-design Larry DeMar & Ted Estes), Twilight Zone is a single-hardware-revision 1993 widebody (~15,235 units) — there is no Pro/Premium/LE split; that concept is a modern Stern-era convention. Variation across units is limited to ROM code revisions, not physical layout.
The core loop: GUMBALL, Locks, and Multiball

The Left Ramp spells **GUM** and the Right Ramp spells **BALL**. Completing GUMBALL lights the **Lock Lane** and the **Gumball Machine** (a ball-holding prop that also dispenses balls when shot directly via the Right Orbit, and periodically loads the ceramic **Powerball**). Locking one ball and starting **Standard Multiball** gives a 15M starting Jackpot; locking a second ball first (respell GUMBALL) jumps that base to 40M — the single biggest EV decision in the ruleset. In Multiball, the **Player Piano** is the Jackpot shot and the **Camera** relights it; each collection steps the base up to 5 times, and the seven **Greed Targets** flashing throughout add 5M apiece directly to the live Jackpot. The Powerball landing in the Jackpot shot doubles its value. Two balls draining ends Multiball; a 15-second Lock Lane restart window follows if no Jackpot was collected yet.
Other multiballs

**Fast Lock Multiball** is qualified via its Door Panel award: a radio hurry-up (~17-20M counting down to a 5.3M floor) plays, and shooting the **Lock Lane** while it's live banks the value and starts 3-ball multiball instantly, with Lock Lane repeating that same value on every subsequent shot (no restart grace period). **Powerball Mania** kicks off when the ceramic Powerball loads into the Gumball Machine: an immediate payout, a three-ball multiball (one ball from the Gumball Machine plus two from the Lock/trough — the Powerball itself stays loaded in the machine), and every switch scoring 250K toward a frenzy total. The **Right Ramp** sends the ball onto the raised **Powerfield** mini-playfield, where player-controlled **Magna-Flips** work alongside the real flippers; walking the ball out the upper exit ("Defeating the Power") pays a flat, repeatable **50M Mania Jackpot**. Most Mania scoring banks into end-of-ball bonus rather than paying live.
Modes: 15 rotating Door Panels

One of 15 Door Panel awards is always "flashing." **Jet Bumper hits rotate** which panel is flashing; panels are collected by shooting the lit **Player Piano**, by **Defeating the Power** on the Powerfield (same effect as a Piano hit), or by the **Slot Machine** scoop (awards a random panel instead of the flashing one). Notable panels: **Town Square Madness** (every switch adds to a running total, Jet Bumpers step their own value), **Clock Millions** (the **Clock Target** pays the current hour-hand value, up to 12M/hit), **The Spiral** (escalating orbit-shot values, no grace timer), **Greed** (clear all seven Greed Targets for 5M each), **Fast Lock**, **Lite Gumball**, **Lite Extra Ball**, **Camera** (stacks the Camera's 8-award cycle), **Hitchhiker**, **Clock Chaos**, **Super Skill Shot**, **10 Million**, **Super Slot**, and **Battle the Power**. Each panel is collected once per cycle; once all 14 non-wizard panels are cleared, the 15th slot — **"The Handle"** — becomes flashing.
Multipliers

TZ has no continuous playfield multiplier. The only true multiplier is **Bonus X**, built by shooting the **Left Ramp** while it flashes (lit via a Right Inlane rollover): steps 2X→3X→4X→5X, capped, and lost entirely at ball end — it never carries over. A handful of shot-level escalators function similarly: the Powerball doubles the Multiball Jackpot shot, Camera's **3X Town Square** award triples the Town Square subtotal, and Defeating the Power doubles the current Powerfield subtotal.
Wizard mode: Lost in the Zone (LITZ)

Collecting all 14 rotating Door Panels lights **The Handle**; collecting it launches **Lost in the Zone**, a fixed **45-second, 6-ball** frenzy (all balls auto-plunged from the emptied Gumball Machine, with continuous ball-saving). Nearly everything runs simultaneously — Clock Millions, Town Square Madness (Jets only), the Powerfield (50M Mania Jackpots still available), all seven Greed Targets, a permanently-lit Piano paying random "Odd Change," a permanently-lit Slot Machine, flat-rate Hitchhikers, and 10M-per-hit Left Ramp shots. When the timer expires, virtually everything accrued banks into end-of-ball bonus — a strong LITZ is worth roughly 300M.
End-of-ball bonus & strategy

Base bonus is `(500K × Hitchhikers + 500K × Door Panels) × Bonus X`, plus banked subtotals from Town Square, Clock Millions/Chaos, Greed, and Powerfield play. Because so much scoring is deferred, protecting a large bonus (don't tilt) matters more than rushing to cash out. The standard opener is the safe **Left Ramp → Right Ramp → Player Piano** loop, which simultaneously spells GUMBALL, loads the Gumball Machine, and progresses Door Panels while avoiding the table's worst drains: the Jet Bumpers/Town Square area and a mishandled Slot Machine kickout.

name: Doctor Who
description: Doctor Who pinball rules: pick a Doctor before each plunge, run the W-H-O shot combo, build Playfield X to 4X, and battle through to the Davros wizard mode.

body.text: Designed by Bill Pfutzenreuter (mechanics) with Barry Oursler (rules/software), released by Bally/Midway in September 1992. A single production run of 7,752 units — there are no Pro/Premium/LE variants of this title; every machine shares identical playfield geometry. WPC / Fliptronics II hardware, three flippers (two standard plus a mid-left upper flipper), and an electronic auto-launch "Shooter" button instead of a spring plunger.
Doctor Selection (the "skill shot")

Before each plunge, cycle through the seven Doctors with the flipper buttons (right = next, left = previous) and launch on your pick — there is no lane-based skill shot on this machine. Each Doctor modifies rules for that ball only: **Doctor 1** doubles Escape-letter spotting; **Doctor 2** doubles/extends Hang-On; **Doctor 3** extends the W-H-O shot timer; **Doctor 4** speeds Repair-bank completion; **Doctor 5** doubles Jet Bumper contribution to Transmat; **Doctor 6** reaches 4X Playfield multiplier in 3 Loop Ramp shots instead of 6; **Doctor 7** auto-spots Time Expander targets and eases multiball. Doctors are permanently spotted via Transmat, Video Mode completion, or the Emperor Dalek Jackpot; spotting all 7 pays a large bonus and can be repeated across a game.
W-H-O — the core combo

A three-shot chained sequence: **Right Ramp ("W")** → **Hang-On target ("H")** → **Loop Ramp ("O")**, each shot lighting the next on a timer. Completing it repeatedly raises the per-letter award and lights Extra Balls after 2 completions (then further intervals). Every ~10th completed Loop Ramp shot triggers **Sonic Boom**, converting the next W-H-O into a 10,000,000-per-letter hurry-up — shoot W and H first and save the Loop Ramp for last, or an early loop shot ends the round prematurely.
Multipliers

**Playfield X** climbs 1X→4X in 0.5X steps per Loop Ramp shot (1X steps with Doctor 6), applying to nearly all scoring, including Video Mode's wave bonuses (build it before shooting for Video Mode) — only the self-adjusting Last Wave/set-completion bonus is exempt. Once capped, further loop shots pay a flat 250,000. A separate **Bonus multiplier**, built by Jet Bumper hits (up to ~40X), applies only to the end-of-ball bonus.
Modes

**Video Mode** — complete the six-target **E-S-C-A-P-E** bank (lower-right) to light it at the Police Box entryway; play a jump-obstacle video sequence in escalating wave "sets," each clean set paying a large completion bonus. **R-E-P-A-I-R** — a six-target bank (left side) with an escalating hit ladder that, once fully lit, pays "Unlimited Millions" on every further hit (best farmed with Doctor 4). **Hang-On/Collision** — a single target past the upper flipper that pays a permanently-growing value when lit as Hang-On, or a flat Collision award when unlit. **Transmat** — Jet Bumper hits build hidden charge; the lit Transmat target spots a Doctor when hit.
Multiball — the Time Expander

The **Time Expander** is a rising three-level mini-playfield and the sole path to multiball. **Level 1 (Lock Mode):** lock two balls in the flanking lock holes (a center standup re-arms locks after the first multiball). **Level 2 (Target Mode):** hit five dome targets (3 hits each) to count down a 15-hit Target Mode; Doctor 7 auto-spots the most-needed target. **Level 3 (Jackpot Mode):** three gates open — shoot any gate to start multiball, then clear all three gates within a rolling timer to collect a **Dalek Jackpot** (Bronze 30M → Silver 35M → Gold 40M → Supreme 45M → Emperor 50M). Missing a gate or dropping to 2-ball demotes the rank a tier. Failing to score a Jackpot leaves a brief Re-Lock window to restart multiball instead of falling back to single-ball play.
Wizard Mode — Davros

Collecting the **Emperor Dalek Jackpot (50,000,000)** spots all 7 Doctors and triggers **Davros**: the five dome targets must be hit for real (no Doctor 7 auto-spot) — once each for **Single Davros (100,000,000)**, twice each for **Double Davros (200,000,000)**, three times each for **Triple Davros (300,000,000, up to 1.2B at 4X)** — the game's ceiling, which then repeats indefinitely. Missing the gate timer at any level demotes back to a plain Emperor Jackpot. A ball ending mid-Davros carries the level into the next multiball.
Strategy notes

The Time Expander lock saucers and REPAIR bank are the machine's primary center-drain risks (large drain gap, no outlane kickback rubber). Competitive time-based tournament play favors grinding the safe W-H-O/Loop Ramp combo (Doctor 2 or 3) over forcing multiball, which is largely overrated due to slow setup and high drain risk; raw-score play instead favors Sonic Boom farming or Video Mode wave-stacking under Doctor 1 at high Playfield X.

name: Abra Ca Dabra
description: Abra Ca Dabra pinball rules: step the Bonus Value ladder through drop targets and rollover lanes, then cash it in at the lit bullseye for the Special award.

body.text: Abra Ca Dabra is a single-player electromechanical wedgehead — no multiball, no modes, no wizard modes, no ramps, no spinners, no saucers, and no extra ball. It's one of the earliest pinball machines ever made, designed by Jeff Brenner with magician-themed art by Gordon Morison. Everything the game does routes through one system: an escalating **Bonus Value** ladder (1000 → 2000 → 3000 → 4000 → 5000, shown down the center of the playfield) that gets scored the instant you cash it in — there is no end-of-ball bonus collect on this machine. Anything labeled "Bonus Value" is real-time scoring, not a stored total paid at drain.
**The two feed paths.** Two independent shots step the ladder up:

items: **Drop-target banks.** Two banks of 5 targets each (left and right) sit in the upper playfield. Within each bank, one target is "lit" at a time (the lit position cycles with hits from pops, slings, and target hits). Hitting the lit target scores the full current Bonus Value; hitting an unlit target only scores 500. Clearing a bank lights the center bullseye standup target — clearing *either* bank is enough to light it, on both the 3-ball and 5-ball operator settings; the ball-count setting doesn't add a both-banks requirement for the standard bullseye (that stricter both-banks condition applies only to the 5-ball Special award once Bonus Value is capped at 5000 — see below). Hitting the lit bullseye then scores/advances Bonus Value one tier and resets the bank(s) for another lap.

**The 1-2-3-4 lane sequence.** Four numbered rollover lanes sit across the top of the playfield, with a second numbered set nearer the flippers (likely, though not fully schematic-confirmed, wired into the same sequence). Completing all four numbers — in any order, carrying over ball to ball once lit — instantly scores current Bonus Value, bumps it a tier, and resets. On the 3-ball setting only, hitting lane 2 or 3 auto-spots its partner ("two numbers for the price of one"); on 5-ball, all four must be earned individually.

body.text: **The plunge.** There's no named "Skill Shot" feature (that mechanic postdates this game), but the plunge is a real strategic choice: it launches straight at the top lanes, and lanes 2/3 are the safe target — lanes 1 and 4 are explicitly flagged as SDTM-drain-prone off a hard plunge, and are better collected later via direct flipper shots.

**Special/Replay.** Once Bonus Value caps at 5000, the same two paths (bank-clear+bullseye, or 1-2-3-4 completion) instead award a **Special** — an added free game/replay credit, not an extra ball. If both banks happen to be down simultaneously at 5000, the bullseye is worth two Specials at once.
