**Outlanes matter.** Both outlanes are labeled "BONUS" and score the currently-lit Bonus Value on drain, since a dead-center drain scores nothing extra — the one deliberate way to salvage value from a ball that's about to be lost.

**What's absent, stated plainly:** no multiball (physically impossible on this hardware), no timed modes, no ramps, no saucers/kickout holes, no spinners, no captive balls, no bonus multiplier unit (2X/3X/5X — Bonus Value is a single stepping number, not a multiplier), and no extra ball. Tilt behavior isn't fully documented, though EM convention of the era strongly suggests it ends the ball (possibly the whole game) and forfeits uncollected value — treat with real caution. Standard Gottlieb end-of-game score-match awards a replay separately from all of the above.

name: Theatre of Magic
description: Theatre of Magic pinball rules: spell THEATRE for hurry-ups, lock balls for Theatre Multiball, run the eight Illusions, and reach the Grand Finale wizard mode.

body.text: Bally, March 1995. Designed by John Popadiuk (WPC-S, DMD). Single production model — no Pro/Premium/LE splits; the only "editions" are factory ROM v1.3 versus the 2021 community "2.0" balance mod, which changes rules but not the layout.
Skill shot

The plunge rides a wireform to the **right inlane**. The DMD cycles three awards (10M/20M, 2x Bonus, Advance Clock +2, and Begin Illusion *or* 2x Combos); plunging locks the one showing, and the first **Magic Trunk** hit collects it. Once any ball is locked, later plunges instead offer a fixed captive-ball skill shot that always advances the clock.
The Left Lane (Theatre lane)

The backbone shot. Each shot spells a **T-H-E-A-T-R-E** letter and returns to the right flipper, so it self-loops. Completing the word lights a **THEATRE Hurry-Up** at the trunk hole (~10 s, 50M base + ~100K per pop hit). Weak shots fall into the **Bonus X rollovers** — complete both (lane change, read via the back-panel mirror) to step bonus toward **8x**. Bonus X resets every ball, and end-of-ball bonus multiplies everything: letters (500K each), MAGIC letters, clock hours, Illusions started, magicianship rank. The tournament meta is simply: 8x first, then Theatre-lane loops — bonuses can exceed 300M.
Theatre Multiball

Spell **MAGIC** on the ramps (both count for the first two multiballs, right ramp only after), lock two balls at the **inner loops** (20M each), then shoot the trunk's **bulls-eye magnet face** to start 3-ball play (4-ball if a Vanish ball waits). The **Rear Trunk Entrance** is a Secret Ball Lock that spots all of MAGIC. At the start, the trunk hole during the 5-4-3-2-1 countdown is an instant **100M**. Jackpots (50M base) collect at the trunk and pump +5M per major shot — the value never resets; relights cost escalating trunk hits.
Tiger Saw Multiball

Three captive-ball hits (later six) light **Vanish**; the Left Lane then locks the ball (40M — the third Vanish lights Extra Ball) and the **right orbit** starts 2-ball play. The captive ball is an always-lit jackpot: 30M, +10M per collect, 70M max. Letters and clock stay live during it.
Illusions (8 modes)

Three trunk hits light an Illusion; the trunk's open **hole face** starts it (~20 s each): Tiger Saw, Levitating Woman, Trunk Escape, Spirit Cards (spinner), Safe Escape (11-04-69), Metamorphosis, Strait Jacket, Hat Magic. **Starting** — not completing — counts toward the Finale.
Clock, Trap Door, extras

Every **right orbit** advances the clock an hour: 6:00 lights Extra Ball, 12:00 starts **Midnight Madness** (magnet catches worth 2M x hour). Four trap-door target hits light **Raise Trap Door** at the center ramp; the raised door (blocking the right ramp) pays 15M + a **Basement** mystery. Hocus Pocus standups arm ~15 s outlane magna-save magnets. Combos: any two-in-a-row among the six major shots, 2M and +2M per link, uncapped in factory code, doubled all ball by the 2x Combos skill award.
Grand Finale (wizard)

Light four diamonds — spell THEATRE, play Theatre Multiball, reach Midnight, start all 8 Illusions (the hard one) — then start at the inner loop: one ball, 60 seconds, every major shot 50M + a MAGIC THEATRE letter; all 12 letters pays **500M**. Diamonds also set your Magicianship rank (Novice → Master).

name: Centigrade 37
description: Centigrade 37 pinball rules: spell A-B-C-D to feed the kickout hole, climb the mechanical thermometer, and light the perpetual Special award at 37 degrees.

body.text: Single-player electro-mechanical wedgehead (design Allen Edwall, art Gordon Morison, ~1,600 built, model 407). Theme: revive a cryonically frozen woman by raising her temperature to 37 °C / 98.6 °F, tracked by a **mechanical backbox thermometer** that physically climbs as you play. One production version only — no add-a-ball export, no editions; the only variance is operator settings (3/5 balls, Special award, Double Advance persistence).

**EM convention:** this is a single-ball, single-level game. There are **no multiballs, no timed modes, no bonus or playfield multipliers, no end-of-ball bonus, and no software combo system** — there is simply less to chase here than on a modern machine. The goals below reflect what actually exists on the machine; nothing has been invented to fill category quotas. The "combos" are the documented repeatable sequences, the "modes" are the standing features, the one "multiplier" is Double Advance, and the "wizard" goal is the game's beat-the-game achievement: the temperature check.
The progression

items: **A-B-C-D letters.** A/B/C are the three top rollover lanes (skill-plunge territory; re-fed by a right-flipper lob up top just left of the leftmost pop). **D** is a separate upper-left rollover, habitually a right-flipper shot. Letters stay lit all game. Each letter adds a green light to the kickout hole (+1,000 per shot), advances the thermometer, and lights a drop-target spot.

**Kickout hole (upper right)** — the shot to master, from the **left flipper, all day**. Pays 1,000 base + 1,000 per lit letter (up to 5,000), advances the thermometer one step per lit letter, ejects into the bagatelle lanes, and collects the Special when lit.

**Bagatelle / waterfall** — two columns of three serial rollovers cascading down the right side. Lit (white flashing) rollover = 5,000 + one thermometer advance; unlit = 500. The game's main point source (perfect run ~20,000); steer with nudges and avoid the bottom-most lane, which feeds the right outlane (nudge-save possible at the open elbow).

**Drop targets (left 4-bank, right flipper)** — 500 each (a lit-5,000 reading exists but is disputed/settings-dependent). Clearing the bank lights the two **bullseye standups** (5,000 each) alternating between **Double Advance** and the green **bank reset** — hit green before collecting Double Advance and you start over.
**Double Advance** — the game's only multiplier: 2× on every thermometer advance (factory default: rest of game).
**Thermometer → Special** — 24 zero-point advance steps to 37 °C; topping it lights a **perpetual Special at the kickout hole** (factory: replay). This is the replay chase, not the score chase.

body.text: Strategy in one line

Letters early, drops once, then **shatz right-to-left through the lit 5,000 inlane and shoot the saucer forever**, nudging every waterfall descent into lit lanes. Dangers: right outlane under the waterfall, SDTM bullseye bounce-backs, pop exits down the middle, and the gapped inlanes (never roll-cradle the right flipper; don't dead-bounce the left). Tilt ends the game, not the ball.
Note on achievements

No electronically tracked achievements exist on a 1977 EM; the achievements tracked in this app are written to mirror the machine's own documented milestones rather than anything the hardware itself records.

name: Black Knight 2000
description: Black Knight 2000 pinball rules: master the Skyway one-touch, build the WAR Hurry-Up ladder, run Castle Multiball, and reach the King's Ransom wizard mode.

body.text: **Williams, April 1989 · Steve Ritchie design · System 11B · one production model (no editions)**
The big idea

BK2K is a split-level game. The plunge delivers the ball to the **Upper Deck** (back ~40% of the table), where a single downgrade-mounted right flipper shoots the **Sky Loop**, the **Drawbridge 1-2-3 targets**, and the **Drawbridge ramp** into the **Black Knight's Castle** lock. The only way off the upper deck is through the **W-A-R lanes**, whose wireform feeds the lower right flipper. The core axiom: *"Avoid the lower playfield — while the ball is on the upper playfield, you can't lose it."* The game's defining skill is the **Skyway one-touch**: the instant a ball drops off the upper deck to the right flipper, flip it straight back up the **Skyway ramp**.
Scoring engines

items: **Hurry-Up ladder** — completing W-A-R lights a countdown on the Skyway: 200K → 500K → 750K → 1M → 1.5M. Any collect advances the ladder, and it **persists across balls**. This WAR → Skyway cycle is the tournament bread-and-butter.

**Sky Loops** — consecutive upper-deck loops escalate (20K/40K/60K...). Two in a row holds the bonus X and lights Extra Ball on the Skyway. The machine keeps a dedicated **Loop Champion** record (default 6 in a row; beating it pays an extra ball).
**Ramp-Loop Combo** — a full-power Skyway carries around the whole Sky Loop: loop value **+100K** in one shot.
**U-Turn ladder** — consecutive horseshoe shots inside ~5-second windows: 50K up to 250K (7 shots ≈ 875K). Risky but fast, and it lights the Challenge Lane.

body.text: Multiballs

items: **Castle Multiball (3-ball)** — hit the 1-2-3 targets to lower the drawbridge, lock three balls via the ramp (the bank may re-close between locks on harder settings). During multiball the Drawbridge scores the **Jackpot, 1M building to 4M**, and spots RANSOM letters. The Challenge Lane holds a ball ~10 s as a legal park. **Locks are shared in multiplayer** — third lock takes the multiball. On the last ball with exactly two locked, an outlane drain triggers **Last Chance**, kicking both locked balls into play (once per game).

**Double Knight's Challenge (2-ball)** — U-Turns light the far-right Challenge Lane; shoot it lit for the 2-ball mode where **spelling WAR = 1,000,000, repeatable**. Classic line: pre-light two WAR letters, start the mode, plunge with the flipper held up, lane-change the last letter under the ball.

body.text: Wizard mode: King's Ransom

Spot **R-A-N-S-O-M** letters by shooting the open Drawbridge within ~20 s of completing the W-I-N lanes (or via the Wheel). **Letters carry over between games on the machine.** Completing the word starts a ~20-second 3-ball frenzy with unlimited ball save: bonus X jumps to 5X **and stays held for the rest of the game**, first Skyway = 1M + Extra Ball, WAR = 1M repeatable, U-Turns = 250K, Jackpot lit. Park a ball in the plunger lane as the timer ends for a de-facto extra ball.
Multipliers and bonus

Bonus X (2X-5X) advances only via **W-I-N completions** and resets each ball unless **held by two consecutive loops** (or permanently by King's Ransom). The bonus pool is 2K × your cumulative game total of U-Turns + loops — it **never resets**, so loops and U-Turns made early pay bonus on every ball. There is no playfield-X or mid-ball bonus collect.
Lower deck support systems

items: **Lightning Lane (SPIN)** — always VUKs the ball back to the upper deck, lit or not (the safe escape). Lit — at ball start or briefly after the left inlane — it spins the **Lightning Wheel** for 1 of 16 awards (points to 200K, Extra Ball, Special, Light Kickback/Magna-Save, Lower Drawbridge, Knights Challenge, Spot RANSOM, Hurry Up).

**KNIGHT drop targets** (K-N-I far left, G-H-T center, timed) — each full six-target completion spots a **B-L-A-C-K** letter and **relights Kickback and Magna-Save**; completing BLACK lights the Skyway for 1M. Low points, but it's how you keep your outlane insurance alive.
**Magna-Save** — a right-outlane magnet fired by a separate yellow cabinet button (~5 s of magnet time); **Kickback** guards the left outlane. Both are one-use until relit.

body.text: Extra balls

Loops (2-in-a-row lights EB on the Skyway, escalating requirement), first Skyway in King's Ransom, the Wheel's EB slot, Special, beating the Loop Champion, and the replay level (default 4.8M). Factory cap: 3 per game.
Behavioral variance
Behavioral variance between individual machines comes from operator adjustments (drawbridge re-close difficulty, timer lengths, WAR memory, free spins), not editions.

name: Gorgar
description: Gorgar pinball rules: build the Bonus Multiplier up to 3X, work the G-O-R and G-A-R drop banks, and light the Snake Pit for the machine's biggest single scores.

body.text: Gorgar is a Williams System 6 solid-state game (December 1979, design Barry Oursler, 14,000 made) and the **first talking pinball machine** — a 7-word vocabulary ("Gorgar speaks", "Me got you", "You beat me") over an accelerating heartbeat. It is a **single-ball, lamp-ladder game**: there is **no multiball, no timed modes, no wizard mode, and no lane change** (that arrived with Firepower in 1980). Every feature is a persistent ladder that advances as you complete banks and lanes, and much of the progress is remembered ball to ball. The "mode" and "wizard" goals below are this era's closest analogues — its feature ladders and Special/high-score quests — not modern features grafted on.
Bonus is king

items: Bonus advances (1,000 each) come from the A/C top lanes, D/E inlanes, each 1-2-3-4 target, and the eject hole; the **B lane gives 3 advances**. Base bonus caps at **29,000**.
Completing the **A-B-C top lanes** advances the bonus multiplier: **2X, then 3X (max)**. Max end-of-ball bonus = 29,000 × 3 = **87,000** — bigger than any single shot on the playfield.
The **spinner** (right-side lane, left-flipper shot, feeds the top lanes) is lit for 1,000/spin **only while bonus is between 10,000 and 20,000** — rip it inside the window.

body.text: The Snake Pit

The signature toy: an under-playfield **magnet** grabs the ball at the snake's head, scores 1,000 unlit or the flashing value, then releases it. **G-O-R bank completions** climb the value 20K → 30K → 50K; **completing the 1-2-3-4 targets lights it for 50,000 instantly**. Values of 20K+ reset to 1,000 when collected; below that it re-collects freely.
Drop banks and the eject hole

items: **G-O-R** (upper left, right-flipper shot): spells GOR, advances the Snake Pit ladder.
**G-A-R** (center, either flipper): spells GAR, and its own ladder lights the jet bumpers (100 → 1,000), then **GAR 5,000**, then the **alternating outlane Special**.

Every GOR or GAR completion also advances the **eject hole** (left kick-out): 5,000 → 10,000 → 15,000 → **X-TRA BALL** (max one EB per ball). The 15K value doesn't reset on collect — the famous "eject farm."

body.text: 1-2-3-4, Stars, and Specials

Each number is made by hitting its bullseye standup **or** by completing both **D and E inlanes** (which spots one number). Full completions light the 50K Pit and climb **Star 1 → Star 2 → the 1-4 Special arrows**; a lit-arrow target awards **SPECIAL**. The inlanes (3,000 + bonus advance each) are the legendary **cross-shatz** lanes — alley-passing them is the tournament farm: safe points, max bonus, and a spotted path to the 50K Pit.
Strategy and dangers

Multiplier first (B-lane plunge + spinner loops to 3X), then G-O-R/Pit collects and inlane shatzing. **Never shoot the lower 1-2-3-4 standups on the fly** — rebounds feed the outlanes, the game's main drain path. Control the Snake Pit release and the eject kickout. Factory replay ladder: **300K / 430K / 550K**; High Score to Date 500,000 — beat it and the demon admits **"You beat GORGAR."**

name: Monster Bash
description: Monster Bash pinball rules: start and complete all six monster modes to collect their instruments, then reach Monsters of Rock, the final wizard mode.

body.text: Design George Gomez, software Lyman Sheats. A two-flipper fan layout in the Attack From Mars family, plus three toys: Frankenstein on his operating table, a Dracula figure that rides a track across the mid-right playfield, and the Creature glowing under a translucent lagoon window. Reissued by Chicago Gaming in 2018 (Classic / Special / Limited) — all edition differences are cosmetic/hardware; the ruleset is identical to the 1998 original.
The objective: form the band
Six classic monsters each have a mode. **Starting** a mode collects that monster; **completing** it collects that monster's **instrument**:

items: Creature — How to start: 4 lagoon (left eject) shots; How to complete: Clear all 5 major shots — escalating 1M–5M hurry-ups, 20s each; Instrument: Saxophone
Wolfman — How to start: 4 combined loop shots (moon phases); How to complete: Collect four loop hurry-ups (1M→4M) in one Full Moon Fever; Instrument: Drums
Bride — How to start: 3 shots on each ramp (Ball & Chain); How to complete: 3 more per ramp in 30s (Mosh Pit resets timer ×3); scoring then **triples**; Instrument: Microphone

Frankenstein — How to start: 7 hits on his target bank, then the exposed center ramp → 3-ball multiball; How to complete: 6 Super Jackpots off Frank (Double/Triple Supers via 2/3 intervening jackpots); Instrument: Keyboard
Mummy — How to start: 60 jet hits, start at scoop; How to complete: Score 7.5M in 45s of Mayhem Jackpots; Instrument: Bass
Dracula — How to start: Spell D-R-A-C-U-L-A (D-R-A free), start at scoop; How to complete: Hit the moving Dracula 5× (2X while moving); Instrument: Guitar

body.text: All modes are timed — and **every mode timer freezes during any multiball while the modes stay playable**. That is the game's defining strategy: start several modes, start a multiball (ideally Frankenstein's, last), then finish the modes with the clocks stopped. "Better to start two things than finish one."
Multiballs and wizard modes

items: **Mosh Pit Multiball** — 6 center-lane spinner shots light it, start at the scoop. Begins 2-ball; more Mosh Pit shots add balls (to 4). Jackpots 750K + 5K per lifetime Mosh Pit shot (cap 1.5M); ladder: 10 Frank-ramp shots = Super (~7–10M), then 5 raised red targets = a 3X second Super, repeat forever.

**Monster Bash (mini-wizard, 4-ball)** — light by **starting** all six modes; start at the scoop. Every monster shot 2M; the center lane cashes Bash Jackpots of 2M + 500K per monster bashed (max 7.5M). Reaching it "should just about guarantee a replay."

**Monsters of Rock (wizard, 4-ball)** — light by **completing** all six modes (all six instruments); start at the scoop. Start bonus alone: 5M per instrument + 25M per complete set (≥55M), **+50M if you never started Monster Bash**. Monsters 4M each; shooting all six monster shots = MOR Jackpot (4M × set completions), Mosh Pit spots monsters toward the lap.
**Lyman's Lament** — the scoop's mystery tours concert venues; the 44th non-multiball visit plays the programmer's secret award (+25X bonus, boosted switch values).

body.text: Everything else

items: **Skill shot:** auto-plunge into the flashing D-I-G top lane — 150K + a Monster Bomb.

**Monster Bombs:** launch-button "smart missiles," one flavor per monster (Garlic Clove, Hair Dryer, Ancient Scroll, Silver Bullet, Spear Gun, Flaming Torch); each spots a shot in its mode. Earned from the skill shot, every 3rd/9th/15th Mosh Pit shot, scoop awards, and extra DRACULA spell-outs.
**Instrument Bonus:** each instrument lights the five major shots for ~1M "victory lap" collects on that ball.

**Multipliers:** no playfield-X system — only end-of-ball **Bonus X** (bonus = switch count × X), advanced by D-I-G completions and the Tomb Treasure standup (+1X each); Hold Bonus X from the scoop. 20–30X is routine; bonus is modest, so don't play for it.

**Extra balls:** ~3 monsters started (renews after each Monster Bash), 12 Mosh Pit shots (operator-adjustable), or scoop award — collect at the scoop. **Special** on alternating outlanes at ~4 instruments.
**Phantom Flip:** 7 hits on the three blue standups earn 2 auto-flips on the inlanes (carries over; often disabled in tournaments — it misses most shots).
**Danger notes:** the Mosh Pit lane and right-ramp misses feed the center drain; Frank rejects and Dracula bounces are drain hazards in single-ball play; ramps + lagoon + scoop are the safe diet.

name: RoboCop
description: RoboCop pinball rules: complete the color-coded Arrests to start Multiball, master the signature Jump Ramp, and farm the Sweet Jump loop for high scores.

body.text: An alphanumeric-era Data East game (Nov 1989, ~1,500 built; design Joe Kaminkow / Ed Cebula, code Rob Quinn) and the machine that shipped the world's first solid-state flipper. Single production model — no editions; the only variation is operator settings and ROM revision. Competitively it is famously a **two-shot game**: the left spinner lane and the right jump ramp. Everything else supports those two shots.
Skill Shot — 100K Top Lane

At each ball start, two of the four ball-guide lamps around the 2-0-9 top lanes flash. Plunge through that lane for **100,000 × ball number**. The lane *guides* can't be lane-changed, but the lane *inserts* can — flip an unlit insert under the lit guides first and the same plunge also spots a colored target.
Prime Directives → Arrests → Multiball

The three colored objectives map to three locks ("arrests") at the ramp: - **Green** — 4 standups (mid-left bank) - **Yellow** — 3 standups (center bank) - **Red** — ONE hit on the right captive ball (no red standups exist)

Crucially, each **unlit 2-0-9 top lane spots a target of its matching color** — the universal advice is to complete the colors this way and **never shoot the standups directly** (rebounds feed the right outlane). Each completed color lights an arrest; a made **jump-ramp** shot then locks the ball in the staged upper-left lock. **Three locks start the 3-ball Multiball** and light the Jackpot.
The Jump Ramp

The signature shot: the ball must fly a gap in a girder bridge across the top of the playfield. A made jump scores 100K and returns via catch ramp → VUK → **left inlane** (30K) to the left flipper. A missed jump drops into the pop nest — a notorious drain source. **Two consecutive jumps start Double Scoring** (2x everything, factory ~20s), and every two more consecutive jumps refresh it — the "Sweet Jump loop" (ramp → inlane → ramp) sustains ~230K per lap and is the game's peak farm.
Multiball Scoring

The **Jackpot starts around 500K and everything scored during multiball builds it to a 1,000,000 cap** — rip the spinner before collecting, because a made ramp jump collects it and there is **only one Jackpot per multiball**. After the Jackpot, hitting five targets (default) lights the **Ramp Special** (1M when set to points) — the only time standup-hunting is correct.
Spinner

Spinner value scales with color/lock progress (green/yellow/red spinner lamps) from base spins to **3,000/spin — about 140K per full rip**. Every rip recirculates through the top lanes, spotting more targets, so the spinner farm advances locks, bonus X, and multiball qualification passively. "Rip the spinner all day."
Modes & Awards

items: **Target Practice → ED 209 Million:** completing a bank sets its crosshair "sight" lamps flashing; 4 flashing-sight hits (default) light a timed **1M ramp shot**.
**Mystery Scanner:** the right eject hole awards a mystery value and spots one R-O-B-O-C-O-P letter per visit; the complete word = **extra ball**.
**Laser Kick:** left-outlane kickback, relit by one captive-ball hit (or by lighting the third arrest).
**Bonus X:** completing all three top lanes advances end-of-ball bonus 2X → 5X.

body.text: Everything Is Lit (the wizard-equivalent)

There is no conventional wizard mode. The endgame feat is tying the machine's stored **Jumpmaster** jump record (default 14 successful jumps in one game, adjustable to 5): everything lights, including Special, and beating the record pays a one-time 500K.
Strategy in One Line

Skill shot every ball → max the spinner while the top lanes light your locks → take multiball, pump the Jackpot to 1M, collect on the ramp, then five targets for the Special → between multiballs, loop sweet jumps if the machine jumps clean, otherwise keep ripping the spinner — and never touch the standups outside multiball.

name: Scared Stiff
description: Scared Stiff pinball rules: start all six Tales of Terror, work the Spin the Spider wheel, climb the Stiff-O-Meter and reach Monster Multiball.

body.text: Scared Stiff is a game about collecting six things and then cashing them in. The six Tales of Terror are the spine of the ruleset, and the machine only cares that you have *started* each one — not that you scored well on it. Understanding that distinction is the single biggest jump in scoring on this machine, because it turns the game from six separate challenges into a checklist you can route efficiently.
The six Tales of Terror

items: **Stiff In The Coffin Multiball** — the Left Ramp lights a lock in the Left Loop. Three locks start a 3-ball multiball where the two ramps alternate as 500K jackpots. Hitting the *unlit* ramp still adds 10K to the jackpot value, so there is no truly wasted ramp shot here.

**Night Of The Leapers** — three standup targets, one hit each. Two sit either side of the Left Ramp and the third is beside the Right Ramp. This is the cheapest Tale on the game and should usually be your first.
**Return Of The Deadheads** — light all three top rollover lanes. You rarely shoot for this directly; it falls out of Left Loop and Middle Loop shots that carry the ball around the top.

**Terror From The Crate** — bank hits into the Crate. Four the first time, four more on each later run. The last hit swallows the ball and starts a 2-ball multiball with 250K jackpots for every re-entry.
**The Monster's Lab** — pure bumper accumulation, around twenty hits on a factory setting. The one Tale you cannot aim at, so never spend shots chasing it.
**Eyes Of The Boney Beast** — three Left Ramps. Conveniently, those are the same shots that arm your Coffin locks, so these two Tales build together for free.

body.text: Spin the Spider is the real ruleset

The backbox spider wheel is the most under-used feature on the machine and the reason good players outscore casual ones by an order of magnitude. The Right Ramp lights the scoop, the scoop starts the spider spinning, and a flipper button stops it. Where it lands decides the award.

Two things make the wheel worth planning around. First, three of its positions are Eyes, and collecting all three lights an extra ball. Second — and this is the part most players miss — two positions restart a multiball that would otherwise be ending. The Coffin restarts Coffin Multiball with three fresh balls, and the Crate restarts Crate Multiball. Spinning the spider *during* a multiball is therefore worth dramatically more than spinning it during single-ball play.

The wheel also hands out Double Trouble, which doubles every shot for twenty seconds; Beat The Crate, which pays the Crate value multiplied by a Stiff-O-Meter reading that moves while you watch; and Boogie Man Boogie, where every shot pays 10K and each sink hole you feed adds 5K to that value for the rest of the mode. One caveat: landing on something already collected pays nothing at all, so the wheel gets steadily less valuable the more you spin it.
Useful misses

Two shots on this layout reward failure. A Left Loop attempt that lacks the speed to complete the loop drops into the Secret Passage, which spots a Tale outright — a genuinely useful way to fill in the one Tale you cannot otherwise reach. And a Right Loop shot that comes up short falls into the Skill Shot hole rather than dying, so the right side is more forgiving than it looks.

The Telepathetic Power target is worth a mention too. It toggles the right outlane light on and off with every hit, and with it lit a right outlane drain pays a random award instead of simply costing you a ball. Never shoot for the outlane, but check the light's state before you play the right side loose.
Getting Scared Stiff

Once all six Tales have been started, the Crate lights the wizard mode. From there the sequence is strict and simple: ramp, Crate, ramp, Crate, climbing ten levels of the Stiff-O-Meter. Each shot pays 250K plus 50K more than the last, and the tenth and final shot must be the Crate.

That last Crate shot starts Monster Multiball — four balls, five million points just for arriving, and all three jackpots lit at a million each. There is no alternation this time; both ramps and the Crate are live simultaneously. It runs until fewer than two balls remain, so use the opening seconds while you still have all four up.
Opening plan

Clear the spell target bank first. The Cast A Spell ball saver at the left outlane is *off* when the game starts on most machines, and this game drains left freely — earning that ball saver before anything else is usually worth more than any Tale. The first light costs two full passes through the bank; later ones cost one.

After that, take Leapers, Deadheads and Boney Beast early, since they are cheap and largely overlap with shots you want to make anyway. Let the Monster's Lab arrive on its own from bumper traffic. That leaves the two multiball Tales as the only real work, and both of them score while you collect them.

name: Cirqus Voltaire
description: Cirqus Voltaire pinball rules: collect all nine marvels, defeat the Ringmaster, stack multiballs and trigger the Join the Cirqus wizard mode.

body.text: Cirqus Voltaire asks one thing of you: collect all nine marvels. Do that and Join The Cirqus, the wizard mode, begins automatically — there is no shot to start it. The marvels can be taken in any order, which makes route planning the entire game, and they vary enormously in cost.
The nine marvels, cheapest first

items: **Acrobats** — four Right Ramp hits, and the switch sits flush at the very start of the ramp. Shots that barely climb it still count, from either direction. This is close to free and completing it lights Super Spinner on both spinners.
**Spin** — four passes through the inner loop around the Ringmaster spells S-P-I-N.

**Boom!** — spell V-O-L-T on the red rollovers and a pop bumper physically rises out of the playfield for about ten seconds. Its hit counter is cumulative across the whole game, so a weak Boom! is deposited rather than wasted.

**Menagerie** — a caged ball with a false slingshot beside it. The award ladder continues past the marvel into Spot Marvel and Light Extra Ball, making the cage one of the best shortcuts on the machine.

**Side Show** — a hidden backward-facing scoop, lit from the start of the game and relit every five or six Ballyhoo standup hits. Its ten-item award table includes a video mode, Neon Multiball and an extra ball.
**Juggler** — three Left Loops light it, three more lock balls and start the multiball.
**Highwire Multiball** — work the LIGHT and LOCK standups to arm the queue beside the Left Ramp, then lock three.
**Ringmaster Frenzie** — earned by defeating the second Ringmaster.
**Defeat All Ringmasters** — four Ringmasters, each needing WOW spelled and then five hits. This is the long pole of the whole game.

body.text: One rule worth knowing before you rely on it: spotting the Juggler or Highwire marvel awards the marvel but does *not* start the multiball. If you wanted the balls, you have to earn it properly.
The Ringmaster

The main toy sits recessed beneath the playfield until you spell WOW on the target bank. You do not have to hit each letter individually — any target counts toward the total. The first Ringmaster costs a single hit; every one after costs three.

Once he is up, a magnet built into his head grabs the ball, holds it while he taunts you, then flings it somewhere unpredictable. There is a ball saver after each fling in case it goes straight down the middle. Occasionally the fling lands in the lock queue, which the game rewards as a free lock.

Each Ringmaster takes five hits to defeat, and the two yellow Ballyhoo standups beside him also spot hits — often a safer way to whittle him down than shooting him directly. Awards climb by a million per Ringmaster, and each defeat plays a different multiball: Frenzie, then Razz, then Special.
Which multiball is which

Ringmaster Frenzie is a 2-ball where he lifts a few inches to open the hole, and every shot at him pays 250K. Hitting him again *while the jackpot animation is still playing* pays substantially more — with four balls up, 750K and a million are both reachable.

Ringmaster Razz uses a hurry-up jackpot. It starts at 500K and counts down slowly to 250K, and wherever you stop it becomes the jackpot for the rest of the mode — so landing that first shot early is worth real money. There is also an extra ball lit.

Ringmaster Special is the one with a lever you can pull. The spinner raises the jackpot value, but only until the ball drops under the Ringmaster, at which point it is locked in. Pump the spinner first, cash in second. Despite the name there is no special.

There is a fifth, unmarked Ringmaster multiball — Ringmaster Battle — that appears nowhere on the playfield. You only reach it if you know it exists, and reaching it locks out further Ringmasters until you have played the wizard mode.
Stacking, and the open left side

This machine carries eight multiballs before the wizard mode adds four more, and up to three can run concurrently. Stacking is where the enormous scores come from, and the Left Ramp is the hub — it handles locks, Highwire, marvel spotting and Strike-An-Arc.

Finally, the left inlane and outlane are one continuous open area with no dividing wireform, just posts and a lot of rubber. The outlane post is adjustable, so no two machines drain the same way — read the setting before you commit. It is also one of the best machines in the hobby to learn nudging on, precisely because that area is so open.

name: FunHouse
description: FunHouse pinball rules: advance the clock to midnight, work the Trapdoor ladder and the Mystery Mirror, and start Midnight Multiball with Rudy.

body.text: FunHouse is a clock game. It starts at 8:00, holds its value from ball to ball, and getting it to midnight is the whole point of the machine — that is when Rudy falls asleep, his mouth drops open, and the game finally lets you shoot him. Almost every shot on the playfield moves the clock, so knowing which ones move it most is the difference between reaching midnight and running out of balls.
What actually advances the clock

items: **30 minutes** — the Manhole below the jet bumpers, and starting a ball. The Manhole is the single most efficient shot on the machine and it opens the Steps at the same time.
**15 minutes** — the Wind Tunnel, and the Center Ramp. The ramp then climbs to 20, 25 and 30 on repeat hits, but resets every ball.
**10 minutes** — the Hidden Hallway, the Trapdoor, and the Trapdoor loop.
**5 minutes** — the S-T-E-P targets and the Superdog targets.

**0, 5 or 10** — the jet bumpers, depending on whether they are unlit, lit or flashing. Lighting them first genuinely matters, and the Mirror's Jet Bumpers At Maximum award leaves all three flashing for the rest of the ball.

body.text: Two hard limits are worth committing to memory. The clock will not move past 11:25 during Quick Multiball or during Frenzy, so do not waste those seconds trying. And once you reach 11:30, the *only* thing that advances the clock is locking a ball in the Hidden Hallway — that takes you to 11:45, and the next lock is midnight.
The Trapdoor ladder

Running the Trapdoor loop opens the Trapdoor for about eight seconds. The first one is worth 500K off a single loop. After that the price goes up with the prize: two consecutive loops for 750K, three for a million.

A quirk in your favour — whenever the Trapdoor is open, a ball rolling back over the loop sensor behind it also collects the award. That usually happens when a shot just clears the sensor and rolls back down over it, so some collections arrive unearned.
The Mystery Mirror

With the white MIRROR light on, the Wind Tunnel pays whichever of six awards is flashing: Extra Ball Is Lit, Million Is Lit, Jet Bumpers At Maximum, Steps Open, Quick Multiball and one more. The light is on at the start of every ball, goes out when you collect, and comes back when you hit Rudy's jaw — or briefly, about four seconds, from the right centre lane.

There is a reward for exhausting it. Once all six awards have been collected, the Wind Tunnel stops giving awards and starts Super Frenzy instead: 1.5M base with every target worth 100K, against the 120K and 50K of an ordinary Frenzy. Nothing on the playfield announces this.
Rudy, and the shot most players never find

Jaw hits from the side flipper are the quiet scoring engine here. Your end-of-ball bonus is 50K per Rudy hit, hits carry from ball to ball, and you start the game already holding one. Each jaw hit also relights the Mirror.

The hidden one is the Rudy Gulp. Rudy comments on your play constantly, and while he is talking his mouth is open — putting a ball in there mid-sentence is worth 250K. Most players assume his mouth only opens at midnight and never try it.
Midnight Multiball

Get to midnight, shoot Rudy's open mouth for a million — two million if you are holding Million Is Lit from the Mirror — and the Trapdoor becomes a ladder. The first hit scores 2M and closes it; the Center Ramp reopens it for 3M; each cycle adds another million up to a ceiling of ten. The Steps and Mirror are disabled throughout.

Know the ending before it happens to you. If the multiball finishes with at least one Trapdoor hit made, the clock simply resets to 5:00 and normal play resumes. If you made *no* Trapdoor shots, the Hidden Hallway lock relights and a countdown starts on the playfield clock — relock the last remaining ball in time and another ball is served. Nothing can stop that timer.
Two things in your favour

Shooting the Steps ramp all the way to the top buys twenty seconds of Superdog. Its real value is not the time itself but that the Frenzy timer stops whenever the Superdog timer would stop — Superdog is how you make a twenty-second Frenzy last.

And FunHouse is unusually generous about bad plunges. A ball that runs from the plunger to the drain without hitting a scoring target is returned, and in practice the game often gives back weak plunges that dribbled through the bumper lane into the right outlane even though those did touch switches. Do not panic on a bad plunge.

name: Demolition Man
description: Demolition Man pinball rules: build combos, work the five Cryo-Claw modes, stack four multiballs and reach Demolition Time.

body.text: Demolition Man is a widebody five-ball game with two gun-grip handles mounted forward of the flipper buttons. Each handle has a trigger that acts as a flipper button and a thumb button on top used by some modes. It is a busy playfield, but the ruleset comes down to two systems: combos, and the Cryo-Claw.
Combos are the game

A combo is any sequence of the seven major shots taken while its flashing red arrow is lit. The elegant part — and the reason this game still plays so well — is that the machine lights the next shots for you. Hit any major shot and it lights whatever is easily reachable from where the ball is about to end up. The left inlane lights the right ramp, right loop and AcMag ramp; the right inlane lights the left orbit and left ramp; the right orbit lights the Computer and Side Ramp.

Values climb 5M, 6M, 7M and onward with no apparent ceiling, dropping back to 5M only when the lit arrows time out. Shots you make in between do not break anything — the lit arrows stay lit. Combos light the Computer every ten, and an extra ball at twelve and again at fifty.

This is why the skill shot matters more than it looks. Plunge full strength so the ball travels all the way to the upper left flipper, then shoot the Side Ramp. It is technically the first lit combo, which is why it pays 5M — and every skill shot you make permanently raises the base value of every combo for the rest of the game.
Explodes, and the counter-intuitive way to light them

The left and right loops and left and right ramps carry Explode lights worth 10M each. You light them by hitting the Underground while it is NOT the current lit combo shot. It may still be lit for the Computer or Demolition Time — that does not disqualify it. Only being the active combo shot does.

The Retina Scan drives an Explode Hurry-Up: one hit triggers the first, four the next. All four Explode ramps light at 15M and start counting down, and every one you collect adds 10M to the next. The round ends when the countdown reaches 5M.
The Cryo-Claw and its five lanes

Access is a two-step people often get the order of wrong. Completing the M-T-L rollovers lights the LEFT INLANE — not the claw. Rolling that lit inlane is what lights Claw Ready on the right ramp. Only then does the right ramp divert the ball up the elevator to the magnetic claw, which you steer with the two gun triggers before dropping into one of five lanes.

items: **Lock Freeze** — the most valuable lane when you are near multiball. It locks as many Freeze lamps as you still need, or starts multiball outright — and when it starts one it adds an *extra* frozen ball on top.
**Start AcMag** — repeated Center Ramp shots for a climbing award, 5M up to 12.5M then 6M up to 13.5M, adding a million per successful ramp.

**Prison Break** — fast and reflex-based. The ball drops above the upper left flipper and hands you 15M; a quick Underground doubles it and a quick Side Ramp triples it. Also lights Car Chase, alternating ramps at 5M each.
**Super Jets** — bumpers light for 25 hits at a million each, and the ball is dropped straight into the bumper area. Every yellow target adds to the hits remaining.
**Capture Simon** — the seven major shots light at 5M but only three shots are offered, with a 25M completion bonus for a 40M total. A left loop into the top lock counts as two Simon awards at once.

body.text: All five claw awards increase the second time around.
Four multiballs, each shaped differently

Freeze lamps are lit by the yellow standup targets, balls are locked via the left ramp or the Claw, and multiball starts at the Top Lock off the left loop. Fortress needs one frozen ball and runs three jackpots into a triple Super Jackpot on the right ramp. Museum needs two and lights every shot for a jackpot simultaneously. Wasteland is Fortress with bigger numbers and more than one jackpot lit at a time.

Cryo-Prison is the one to understand before you play it. All the jackpot shots are lit, but they pay nothing directly — they only ADD to a Super Jackpot collected at the right ramp. After each Super you must re-hit a regular jackpot shot to relight it, and you cannot collect another until the current animation finishes.
The two end-games

Completing all five Claw modes lights Demolition Time at the Underground under a blue lamp. It opens with a flat 50M, every major shot lights for 15M, and unusually those shots STAY lit for as long as you keep more than one ball alive. Completing the yellow targets adds a ball and raises the award by 5M; losing a ball lowers it. The total is banked to its own high-score table.

Separately, completing all four multiballs lights a Demolition Jackpot on the right ramp. The game takes your best jackpot from each multiball mode and multiplies it by how many jackpots you scored in that mode — so both quality and quantity of your multiball play are being recorded the whole game.
Two warnings

The Car Crash target has a well-earned reputation for deflecting the ball straight down the middle. There is a short ball saver to compensate, but it can be disabled in LA-4 ROMs, so do not count on it.

And the outlanes are unusually hostile: the divider posts ship without rubber, the ball takes wild spins in that area, and there are no Specials or awards down there at all. There is nothing to gain from the outlanes on this machine — play away from them.

name: Safe Cracker
description: Safe Cracker pinball rules: manage the timer, break into the bank, survive the board game and reach the Vault for a token.

body.text: Safe Cracker is not a three-ball game. It is a timed game with an interactive board game bolted onto it, and your score comes from combining the two. You start with a set amount of time, the clock runs continuously during pinball play, and when it expires you enter sudden death — where the next drain ends the game outright.
Feeding the clock

Almost every switch on the playfield adds a small amount of time or briefly pauses the timer. That is deliberate: the machine is paying you to keep the ball moving rather than to trap and aim. Time remaining shows on the centre playfield timer lights and as a life bar on the display during score sweep.

items: **The Wheel** is the best time source on the machine. Time added is proportional to how far it spins, and a lit wheel adds more than an unlit one.
**Jet bumpers** add time on every hit, and lit jets add more. Complete drop target sets to light them.
**The A-B-C top lanes** add five minutes outright when completed.
**Extra Time outlanes** — once lit, rolling an outlane adds time, and uniquely it still works during sudden death.

body.text: Sudden death is survivable but narrow: most normal events stop adding time there, so the usual routes are closed. The outlane Extra Time lights still work, and the wheel's Disable Computer award holds the timer and stops a drain from ending the game. Any successful time add pulls you back out of sudden death and normal rules resume.
Breaking into the bank

Shoot the blinking drop target sets to light an entrance, then take the lock shot on the left ramp. The bottom left 3-bank is worth hitting early because it spots targets in the other sets, and after the first ball is locked it starts lighting additional entrances.

There are three ways in and the choice genuinely matters: the Cellar behind the sliding target, the Main Entrance scoop in the centre, and the Roof at the centre top lane. The entrance you use determines how far you must travel on the board to reach the Vault — your path is drawn from that entrance's light, clockwise around the centre circle, to the first unlit gate.
The sliding target is where the game is won

This is a two-part shot most players get wrong: you must drive the target ALL the way back, then drop the ball through the hole behind it. A partial hit does nothing. The awards it hands out are the ones that rewrite the board game in your favour.

items: **ATM Card** — multiplies the '$' spots on the board. Collect these BEFORE you break in; afterwards is too late.
**Note to Teller** — gets you past the teller.
**Safe #** — a letter toward V-A-U-L-T.
**Explosives** — a frenzy where the drop sets score big points.
**Lite Outlanes** — arms the Extra Time lights.

body.text: The board game

No ball is in play here. You stop a spinning safe knob with the flipper buttons to move, while a guard chases you using a purely random dice roll. He starts after you have moved several spots, from the same entrance you used. If he catches you, the run ends.

Several spots are items you can stockpile, and knowing them changes how you play the pinball half. Keys unlock locked gates and you can hold several. Dog Biscuits defeat the CyberDog, one consumed per landing. The stopwatch adds clock even in sudden death. Money Bags and '$' build your stash, with '$' multiplied by your ATM Cards. Code awards another VAULT letter.

Two spots can backfire. Move Cop Backwards is usually good, but if it moves the guard backwards onto you, you are caught. The '?' box hands you a random item and those items can be bad as well as good. If the continue-or-quit adjustment is enabled, you may stop after any successful spin and bank your stash rather than pushing your luck.
The Vault, and the long game

Completing the board game lands you in the Vault, which awards at least one token plus a large points award. Safe Cracker physically dispenses collectable tokens — twenty of them, including a silver one — which is what makes it the first machine of its kind.

The hidden top end is Token Multiball. Spelling V-A-U-L-T turns your next Vault entry into a multiball instead of an ordinary award, and crucially those letters are held FROM GAME TO GAME. A session on the same machine compounds, which is a rule almost nothing else in pinball has.
The tilt rule

Tilting is punished in two tiers. Tilt with time left and the game continues, but you are dropped straight into sudden death. Tilt while already in sudden death and the game ends with no bonus at all — and since the bonus is only computed at the very end, and every bank entrance has been stepping your multiplier, that is an expensive mistake. Nudge carefully once the clock is gone.

name: Apollo 13
description: A guide to Sega's Apollo 13: advancing the spacecraft with inlane passes, the nine missions, Shoot The Moon, regular multiball and the thirteen-ball.

body.text: Apollo 13 is a crowded playfield with narrow shots, almost none of them further than halfway up. Balls come off the ramps fast, the post between the flippers pops up constantly, and the whole game plays as catch-and-shoot rather than flow. The upside is that you are rarely punished for taking a moment to think.
The orbits are the real game

Collecting a lit orbit advances the Odyssey around the moon and back toward Earth, and each stage of that journey hands you a mode. Both orbits start the game lit solidly. After that, **the inlanes relight the opposite orbit for a few seconds each** — left inlane lights the right orbit and vice versa. The switches sit low in the lanes, parallel to the flippers, so an inlane pass registers easily and immediately gives you something to shoot at.

You do not need to complete the circuit. Anything lit is collected by the switch inside the lane, and a slow ball that trips it again on the way back down credits **two orbits from one shot**. The journey pays out in stages: Video Mode, Power Down, Power Up, then Splashdown.

items: **Video Mode** is a lunar landing flown on the flipper buttons — left and right for lateral thrust, both together for up. Turning the plunger handle kills your drift, which makes the 109M centre landing manageable.
**Power Down** lights six shots at once for 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 and 90 million. A clean sweep is around 450M.
**Power Up** uses the same ladder but lights one shot at a time and picks the order for you.
**Splashdown** is a timed multiball with the orbits lit for jackpots — the deepest thing on the machine.

body.text: The skill shot is a choice, not a shot

Before you launch you pick from three awards: Start Mission, Mystery, or a Multiball Countdown step. There is no aiming involved. Early on, take Mystery until it gives you the two-orbit award — two free orbits are worth an entire spacecraft mode. After that, switch to Start Mission.
Missions

Nine missions start at the right saucer, which stays lit in normal play until you have seen them all. Pop bumper hits rotate which one is flashing, and turning the plunger handle locks it in — but that lock evaporates when you plunge your next ball, so do not bank one for later. While a mission runs almost everything else shuts off, bar the Rocket ramp and a lit BLASTOFF letter.

items: **Manual Burn** lights three shots to correct a seven-degree course error, each worth 50 to 90 million. It scores far more if you never correct it, because getting back on course ends the round.
**Under Volt** starts a 42M value falling; a Battery target freezes it and lights every major shot for that value for twenty seconds. A second Battery hit buys another twenty and pays again.
**CO2** runs through the spinner, collecting four items for 10, 20, 30 and 40 million.
**Docking** needs four hits anywhere in the D-O-C-K bank for 100M and an extra ball.
**Orbiter**, **Life Support**, **Moon's Gravity** and **Rocket 2-Ball** fill out the set.

body.text: Play all nine and **Master Alarm** lights — a forty-second frenzy where every target is a million and adds a million to a Blastoff ramp jackpot. That jackpot does not reset when you take it. Once Master Alarm is reached, the mission saucer only relights after a spinner shot.
Shoot The Moon and the spinner

The M-O-O-N standups must be taken in flashing order, leftmost first. Finishing them lights a hurry-up on the Blastoff ramp that counts down slowly enough to set up properly — but collect it, because an uncollected one falls back to twenty million. **Every pop bumper hit adds the bumper's current value to the Moon total**, which is why long games see hundreds of millions here.

That connects to the top lanes: completing the 1 and 3 rollovers adds 250K to both the bumper and spinner values, each capped at two million. The spinner backhands, so a maxed one is easy repeat money — and it is the only shot CO2 uses.
Multiball, and then thirteen of them

The LED under the Rocket ramp counts your shots down: three start the first multiball, five the second, seven the third. When it reads one, the next Rocket shot launches three balls with no ball saver and four jackpots at the left orbit, spinner lane, right orbit and mission saucer. Clear all four for a Super at the ramp — or complete M-O-O-N during multiball to light it early.

Collect the eight BLASTOFF letters and the next multiball becomes **13-Ball** instead. Three or four balls launch, then eight more arrive at once about five seconds later. The Rocket is lit for jackpots typically worth 100 to 250 million. Be warned: the centre post does **not** rise after a 13-Ball jackpot, so the returning ball heads straight down the middle. Letters come from the yellow ramp lamp at the start of each ball, from Mystery, and from a ramp combo.
Bonus

The bonus counts four things and nothing else: Rocket ramp shots, Blastoff ramp shots, orbits collected, and missions started. All four count equally, so a safe late ramp shot is worth as much as a hard orbit. Double Bonus doubles the lot, and Hold Bonus carries the count into your next ball.

name: Austin Powers
description: A guide to Austin Powers: reading the five-light mode stacks, the six main shots, all six modes, MOJO and Virtucon multiball, and the two ball saves nobody tells you about.

body.text: Austin Powers is a mode game built on six main shots, it tells you what to do through one thing: the stack of five lights under each of those shots. Most players never look, start four modes they never finish, and wonder why the score does not move.
Read the light stacks first

items: The four lower lights count down what you still owe that shot. One flashing with three dark means four more hits; three solid with the fourth flashing means the next hit starts the mode.
The **red light at the top is dark** if you have never started that mode.
The **red light is lit while the counter is still running** if you started that mode and failed it. The mode is available again at the same price.
**All five solid** means you finished it. Shooting it again pays a flat million and does nothing else — stop feeding it and go somewhere useful.

body.text: This matters because the display badly undersells modes. Starting one is around ten million and completing one around fifteen, neither announced. A successful laser shot reads as three million and is worth closer to thirty. Play for completions, not for the numbers you can see.
The six modes and what each wants

items: **Mini Me** — four completions of the counterweighted spinner starts a hurry-up. One more spin locks the value in, then keep shooting to collect against it.
**Fat Bastard** — four ramps start a four-ball multiball with a long ball saver. All six main shots need four hits each, and only the fourth hit on a shot pays the super jackpot.

**Big Frickin' Laser** — four left ramps arm it, a fifth loads the ball into the cannon on the apron. Fire it at the Austin hole with the lockdown bar button. Each miss can be bought back with a quick ramp, but the third miss kills the round.
**Time Machine** — four shots up to the spinning disc start a two-ball multiball. Six shots are lit for jackpots and an unlit one is worth nothing, so look before you shoot.
**Sub-Drill** — a timed round asking for four shots on each ramp.
**Henchmen** — one shot each at all six main shots against a clock, the red light above each staying on until you make it.

body.text: Stacking, and what blocks what

The best scoring decision here is what you have running when a multiball starts. Mini Me and Sub-Drill both want repeated hits, and both have their timers frozen during multiball. Start one immediately before Fat Bastard and you spend it with four balls in play and a long saver underneath you.

The exclusions are worth memorising. Fat Bastard and Time Machine lock out everything else. Henchmen blocks nearly everything. The laser's retry timer blocks other modes and, annoyingly, blanks the S-H-A-G lights so you cannot see which letters to shift the lanes for. Mini Me blocks nothing at all, which is exactly why it is the mode to leave running.
The things that are not on the six-shot map

MOJO multiball comes from spelling MOJO on the left standups, and its only job is bashing Dr. Evil ten times. He drops, the six shots open, and a Time Machine shot pays a super jackpot and pops him back up for another ten. He starts at a million and climbs about a hundred thousand a hit. Elsewhere, S-H-A-G lives in the lanes — S and G on the outlanes, H and A on the inlanes — and the two top rollovers advance the bonus multiplier at roughly a million a step, which is why the Bonus 6X skill shot is worth taking seriously.
Two ball saves the playfield never mentions

items: Drain immediately after **scoring** the Time Machine in single-ball play and the game makes one attempt to relaunch you. The corollary matters more: once Time Machine is no longer available, that shot loses its saver and becomes genuinely dangerous.

Complete S-H-A-G with an **outlane** letter during single-ball play and you get the ball back. It has to register as single-ball play — two balls draining into opposite outlanes at once does not count.

On multiball, the shoot-again light stops blinking well before the save actually expires. The music runs in an ABAC pattern and the save ends near the start of the C section. Listen rather than watch.

body.text: The end of the road

Start your fourth mode and the extra ball lights. Start your sixth and Virtucon opens: a multiball with an unusually long saver where each of the six shots pays a jackpot on its first hit and all six relight once cleared. Here is the payoff for having actually completed modes rather than merely starting them — a completed shot pays a double jackpot every single time you hit it, with no need to leave. If you finished Time Machine, you can simply stand there and shoot the disc.

Above Virtucon, the backglass shows a Moon Base multiball almost nobody has seen. It is understood to need all six modes completed rather than started, which is a far harder bar, and nothing on the playfield counts it down for you. One last practical note: this game is known for missing switch registrations, especially at Mini Me and the Time Machine. Watch the light stack, not the shot — if the counter did not move, the hit did not happen.

name: Bad Cats
description: A guide to Bad Cats: the Tiger Ramp value ladder and its hidden 20 million award, the SEAFOOD wheel, the 10X Trash Can, the carry-over progressive jackpot, and bonus building.

body.text: Bad Cats is a single-ball game from the tail end of the eighties and it plays like one — no modes, no wizard mode, no multiball. What it has instead is four value ladders running at once, and two awards big enough that everything else is decoration. Learning this machine is mostly learning which ladder to climb.
The layout

The Tiger Ramp runs up the far left, over the top, and empties into the right inlane, with a five-target drop bank beside it. The centre holds the Fishbowl Ramp, the linear Fish target with the Trash Can eject saucer sitting off its left side, and the spinning SEAFOOD wheel. On the right are a three-target Milk Bottles bank and the Doghouse scoop. Three top lanes spell TOY and feed the jet bumpers, with the barbecue flashlamp in the middle of them.
The Tiger Ramp, and the award nobody tells you about

The Tiger Ramp is always lit for something, and the value climbs on consecutive shots: 50,000, 100,000, 200,000, then a million with no ceiling on repeats. The unusual part is that **this ramp does not time out.** Trap the ball, take a breath, shoot again — you lose nothing. What resets you is touching any other scoring switch, and the drop targets beside the ramp entrance are the usual culprit.

There is also a 20 million lamp on that ramp that the instruction card never explains. It lights only on your last ball, and only after you have climbed consecutively from the base value all the way up to the million. That is the single biggest award available in normal play, and it is worth planning your last ball around.
The Fish target and the 10X Trash Can

The Fish target is linear, meaning the harder you hit it, the higher the award it lights. Those awards belong to the Trash Can, not the Fish target — hit the Fish and the Trash Can becomes worth 25,000, 50,000, 75,000, 100,000 or 500,000 instead of its empty value of ten thousand. The lamps time out one at a time, roughly twenty seconds each, stepping down the ladder while you dawdle, so the Trash Can shot should follow immediately.

A lit right inlane arms the 10X multiplier at the Trash Can, and that is where the numbers get serious: 100,000, 250,000, 500,000, 750,000, a million, or five million in a single shot. The Tiger Ramp empties straight into the right inlane, which pairs the two shots naturally.

items: One inlane is lit at all times, and collecting it moves the light to the other side.
Left lit means the Doghouse is lit for a wheel spin; right lit means 10X at the Trash Can.
Slingshots, the two rubber switches, and possibly the bumpers can all shuffle which side is lit without you doing anything, so check before committing.
The Trash Can's own lamp is switched off at the start of every ball, but the Fish and 10X lamps are not — so a loaded Trash Can still pays in full even though it looks dark.

body.text: S-E-A-F-O-O-D

The wheel in the middle of the playfield is a cat fishing in a pond, and whichever of eight fish lands in the net is your award: ten thousand, fifty thousand, two hundred and fifty thousand, a BAD CATS letter with twenty-five thousand attached, Lites Jackpot, Spin Again with a hundred thousand, an extra ball, or a Special. You spin it by shooting a lit Doghouse, and the Doghouse is lit either by a lit left inlane or simply by shooting it while dark — so a mistimed shot costs you the trip, not the award.
The carry-over jackpot

Bad Cats has a progressive jackpot that does not reset when your game ends. It sits on the machine, growing by roughly a tenth of every player's score, until somebody collects it. It opens at a million and can reach the region of twenty million, and the backglass lamps give you a rough reading of where it stands. To light it, sweep the drop target banks — each completed bank awards a letter of BAD CATS — then take the Fishbowl Ramp. One shot collects it, after which it drops back to a million. Reading those backglass lamps before you put money in is a real advantage.
Bonus, and the friendly stuff

Bonus is built the old way: nothing carries between balls, and BAD CATS letters count for nothing at the end. Switch traffic is what pays. The ramps are quietly the best of it — five thousand for the Tiger Ramp switch, fifteen thousand for the Fishbowl Ramp — with ten thousand for the Bird bank or the Trash Can, twenty thousand for the Milk Bottles, and thirty thousand for any outlane on the way out. The top rollover lanes step the multiplier from 2X to a maximum of 7X, and the bonus caps at 999,000.

Two last mercies. The skill shot is a randomly chosen flashing top lane worth 120,000, a doubled bonus and a lit barbecue — the flipper buttons cannot walk that lamp sideways, so your plunge settles it. And on your last ball both outlanes light for Curiosity Spin, turning a drain into a free spin of the wheel and, if your game came in under the machine's average time, often a consolation extra ball too.

name: Banzai Run
description: A guide to Banzai Run: building laps on the ramp, challenging the four racers, riding the vertical Hill playfield, Cycle Jumps and beating the King of the Hill.

body.text: Banzai Run's upper playfield does not sit above the lower one — it stands vertically, on the backglass, which is why the machine towers over everything around it. Play up there is short and frantic because the slope is brutal, and that shapes the strategy: everything below is preparation for a trip lasting a few seconds.
Laps first, always

The ramp is the best shot on the machine and it is not close. It scores a lap, feeds your bonus, raises the value of the lower captive ball, advances you toward multiball, and eventually lights an extra ball — all from one shot. Roll the left inlane before you take it and the ramp is worth two laps instead of one. You begin every game with one lap already banked.

items: **Four laps** takes the lower captive ball from 10,000 to 25,000.
**Seven laps** takes it to 50,000, which is a genuinely safe, repeatable shot.
**Around eight laps** lights an extra ball at that captive ball.
**Twenty-five laps** awards Finish Line: 750,000 plus an extra ball, after which the lap count resets and the eight-lap extra ball does not come back.
Ignore the two 1-Lap targets. They light after each Hill trip, but they are drain shots and the ramp gives you the same lap for far less risk.

body.text: Challenge, then pass

You start the race in sixth place, and five opponents have to be lit and then passed. The first four each own a bank of three targets on the lower playfield: Green Machine on the top rollovers, Blue Beard and Red Hot on the left, and Yellow Belly through the middle. Completing a bank challenges that racer, and the Hill lights while any challenged racer is still unpassed. Actually passing them means hitting their shot on the upper playfield — the loops on either side, the target in the middle, or the Red Hot hole up in the corner.

The Bumper Saucer is the most useful hole on the machine and it does most of this work for you. It spots whichever opponent target best helps you finish a bank, relights the left outlane kickback, and later becomes the Time Lock. It can be shot straight on through the gap in the Yellow Belly targets rather than only from inside the bumpers.
Do not pass everyone at once

This is the counterintuitive part. Clearing every flashing racer on one trip closes the Hill until you challenge somebody new down below, which costs you access to the whole upper playfield. A better plan is to leave one challenged racer standing and spend your Hill time on Cycle Jumps instead.

The Cycle Jump lives at the Red Hot hole. It starts at 75,000 and climbs 25,000 every time you collect it, and the value carries between balls. Completing the A-B-C targets first — the A inside the left loop, the B and C inside the right — doubles the jump for that trip only and also extends the timer on the centre post protecting your lower flippers. Red Hot also drops you back to the lower playfield, so it ends the trip; take it last.
Multiball and the King

Defeat all four racers and the Lock Shot on the Hill lights immediately. That timing is worth planning around: if the last racer you beat is one of the ones up there, you can lock straight away, but if you finish with one of the lower three you have to make another whole trip. Get Red Hot out of the way early to avoid that.

Once you have locked, the second ball goes to the plunger and the ramp is lit for two laps for the entire multiball. The fifth opponent is the King of the Hill, and beating him is a two-stage job. First put a ball in the Bumper Saucer to start the Time Lock, then get up the Hill and hit the captive ball inside about twenty seconds. The timer pauses while a ball is actually on the Hill, so a failed trip usually leaves room for two or three more attempts before the second ball is released. Collect A-B-C and then the captive ball on the same trip and you get a million plus an extra ball.

After the King is down, the ramp is lit for the rest of multiball for two laps and a 250,000 Victory Lap, with no cap on how many you can take. This is where a serious score actually comes from, so protect both balls and keep feeding that ramp.
An honest bonus

There is no hidden number and no multiplier. Your end-of-ball bonus is 10,000 per lap plus 20,000 per racer defeated, and that is the whole formula — you can count it yourself as you play. Racers you beat carry between balls until multiball happens, then reset; the ones you already beat still pay on that ball, which is why they slide over to the Prior Race side of the standings instead of vanishing.

One last thing worth knowing on location. If the magnet that lifts balls to the Hill has failed, the game compensates: each shot to the Hill entrance spots a challenged racer, locks a ball when lock is lit, or defeats the King during multiball. You lose the Cycle Jumps and everything that only exists up top, so scores drop hard, but the game is still finishable.

name: Batman 66
description: How Batman 66 actually works: qualifying the four major villains, the Bat-Phone hurry-up, minor villain perks, Villain Multiball, Bat Turn and the Villain Escape wizard mode.

body.text: Batman 66 is a George Gomez layout carrying Lyman Sheats code, and that pairing tells you most of what you need to know before you put a coin in. The playfield is open and fast — two ramps, two orbits, a scoop, a rotating turntable in the middle and a crane that swings a wrecking ball over five spots — but the code stacked on top of it is enormous. Modes do not queue up politely and wait their turn. They all run at once, on separate television channels, and you choose which one is in front. Sold only as Premium and LE, so every machine you find has the full mechanical package.
The four major villains

Everything starts with qualifying a villain, and each one has its own price. **Catwoman** wants one shot to each ramp. **Joker** wants the Villain-Vision targets flanking the Batmobile spinner. **Penguin** wants the scoop — but only from a flipper, because a ball that falls in out of the pop bumpers does not count. **Riddler** wants the orbits. Every time you play a villain, that villain's qualifier gets more expensive next time around.

Qualifying rotates the turntable until the Bat-Phone is exposed, and shooting the phone converts the qualification into a running mode. Here is the rule most new players miss: **you do not have to cash it immediately**. The hurry-up starts at 1.5M and climbs 250K for every additional villain you qualify before answering, reaching 12M with all four ready. That number is not just a payout — every increment adds 50K to every single shot you make inside the mode that follows. Padding the phone is the difference between a two-million mode and a twenty-million one. Hitting the Commissioner Gordon target also pushes the value up.

Inside a mode, each lit shot is worth 500K plus 50K per shot already made plus 50K per hurry-up increment, and all of it banks into a super jackpot waiting at the scoop. You can cash out at the end of any stage or keep going for another 1x on the whole mode. The single strongest opening move is the **Batcave Combo**: shoot the scoop, then the left orbit while it glows orange, before you touch a single mode shot. Every base value in the mode doubles.
Minor villains and their perks

Complete the three TV standup targets and the left orbit lights for a minor villain. Fourteen of them span three seasons, each 45 seconds long, and each one you finish hands you a perk. This is the half of the machine casual players never touch, and it is where the real leverage lives.

items: **Mr. Freeze** stops every timer in the game — hurry-ups, mode clocks, playfield multipliers, Bat Turn, the Villain Escape build phase. Take it every time it appears.
**Bookworm** makes minor villain awards last the whole game instead of the ball, so its value depends entirely on taking it early.
**Shame** adds a ball to every multiball and ten seconds to the ball save, and starts as a two-ball multiball the first time you play it.
**King Tut** protects your minor villain progress and stacks the main channel multiplier.
**Mad Hatter** lets you replay minor villains you lost.
**Egghead** banks a frenzy total straight into your end-of-ball bonus.

body.text: Multipliers and multiball

Three separate multiplier systems overlap. Both standups flanking the Batmobile spinner light the Atomic Pile for a 2x playfield multiplier lasting 30 seconds; repeat the pair and shoot it again while it runs and you get 3x with a fresh clock. Three hits to Commissioner Gordon arm the white X inserts, and the next shot you make keeps that multiplier for the rest of the ball — 2x for the first, climbing to 6x for the fifth. Aim those at the shots your current villain actually needs, not at whatever you happen to hit next.

**Villain Multiball** only exists inside a major villain mode. Hit a turntable target to light locks, stack three balls at the right orbit, and every major shot goes green for jackpots starting near 300K and climbing 50K each. Twelve jackpots swings the turntable to its Batcave face and lights a super jackpot at the Atomic Pile; each one after that costs two more shots, up to twenty. Mystery becomes a guaranteed add-a-ball while multiball runs.
Bat Turn and the wizard modes

Bat Turn is a hurry-up mode you build before you start. Every pass of the Batmobile spinner adds 25K to a value opening at 500K, and ten spins lights it at the Atomic Pile. Once running, any major shot pays the current value and goes dark; the spinner relights everything and pushes the value higher again. With Mr. Freeze captured and the timer dead, this becomes the most lucrative loop on the machine.

There are two endings. Capture one minor villain from each season and the left orbit offers a choice of three chaotic six-ball multiballs. Arrest all four majors and the same shot starts **Villain Escape** — thirty seconds of switch-hitting to build the jackpot value at 10K a hit, then a four-ball frenzy in which you have to defeat all four villains again to light the super jackpot. Drain to a single ball and the whole progression resets, so get your gadgets banked and your multipliers locked in before you go.

name: Comet
description: A player's guide to Williams' Comet: the Duck and Rabbit banks, the Comet ride ladder, the bull's-eye multiplier, and how to set up the last-ball million point shot.

body.text: Comet is a carnival-themed early solid-state machine with a short rule set and one famous shot. Barry Oursler designed it, Python Anghelo did the art, and it holds a small place in history as the first solid-state game with a million point shot. Everything feeds toward that: two target banks, a centre ramp, a corkscrew, an eject hole and a jump ramp with three rings on the end. No modes, no multiball, no wizard sequence — just a few features you learn to chain.
The layout

items: **Duck targets** — four targets above the left outlane. Clearing them lights the **Corkscrew** in the upper left.
**Rabbit targets** — four above the right outlane. Clearing them lights the **Funhouse** eject hole.
**Comet ramp** — down the middle, and lit only when both banks are complete.
**Cycle Jump** — a ramp in the upper right that throws the ball into one of three rings.
**Dummy drop target** — knocking it down exposes a bull's-eye for a short window.
**1-9-8-6 lanes** — four rollovers across the top, with lane change on the right flipper button.
**Left return lane** — the only return lane on the machine, and the only way to light the Cycle Jump rings.

body.text: The banks drive everything

Ducks light the Corkscrew, Rabbits light the Funhouse, and both together light the Comet ramp. That third one is where the scoring is. A lit Comet ride pays 30,000 and then climbs: 50,000 on the second ride, 100,000 plus an extra ball on the third, and 100,000 plus a special on the fourth. The catch is that each advance has a time limit — miss it and the value drops back to 30,000, or the lights go out entirely once you have already banked the first 100,000. After four rides the whole thing resets and both banks have to be cleared again.

Repeat completions keep paying. A second clearing of both banks arms an extra ball on the Cycle Jump: the lower ring lights for five seconds, then the centre for ten, then the upper for fifteen, and missing all three simply restarts the sequence until you take it. A third clearing lights more extra balls and specials, collected on the Corkscrew — worth 20,000 regardless, so never a wasted shot.
Multipliers, and there are two of them

The **playfield multiplier** comes from completing the four 1-9-8-6 lanes, which also scores 50,000. It runs for twenty seconds, and the value depends on which ball you are on. In a five-ball game it goes 2x, 3x, 2x, 2x and then 5x on the last ball; in a three-ball game, 2x, 3x, then 5x. Because the lane change sits on the right flipper button, you can shuffle the lit lanes at any time, even with the ball nowhere near the top — get in the habit of tapping it constantly.

The **bonus multiplier** comes from the dummy. Drop the target, then hit the bull's-eye behind it before the target resets: first time 2x, then 3x, 4x and 5x, after which each hit is worth a flat 20,000. Treat this as a two-shot combination rather than two separate visits, because the window is short. It is worth doing early, because the multiplier applies to the Duck and Rabbit bonuses you have been building all ball — Ducks collected on the Corkscrew, Rabbits in the Funhouse.
The million

The Cycle Jump rings pay by height: 10,000, 20,000 and 30,000 unlit, or 20,000, 50,000 and 200,000 once the left return lane has lit them. On your last ball, with the 5x playfield multiplier running and the Jump lit, the upper ring is worth a full 1,000,000 — and the game will not let you forget it, announcing the million and lighting up the whole backglass.

The order matters. Light the rings first with a left return lane, because the multiplier lasts only twenty seconds and you do not want to spend it hunting a return lane. Then complete 1-9-8-6, then take the upper ring. The Jump also resets whenever the ball reaches the eject hole beside the lower right pop bumper, so you may need another return lane before your next attempt.
Small print worth knowing

items: Both outlanes score 10,000 and carry Special lights, and the left one advances your Duck bonus by three while the right advances Rabbits by three. Draining is not entirely a loss here.
The left outlane rubber can be nudged to send the ball back into play, which makes the left side less lethal than it looks.
A launched ball that never reaches the top and then drains without scoring anything is served again — but one switch closure and it counts as played.
Ducks and Rabbits are 2,000 for the first hit on each target and 1,000 after, so there is no value in grinding them beyond completing the bank.
