body.text: Comet also plays very differently from one machine to another, and the reason is usually physical rather than software. Five adjustable posts around the return lane and outlanes decide how forgiving it is, and pitch decides whether the ramps are comfortably reachable: nominal is roughly six degrees of rake from front to back, with no lean across the width at either end of the playfield. Most timed features sit in the fifteen to twenty second range, though operators can change them. Glance at the outlane posts before your first ball; they tell you how much risk each ramp attempt is worth.

name: CSI
description: How to play Stern's CSI: the Morgue skill shot, Evidence colours, all three multiballs, the frenzies, Ballistics, and the fifty-million shot hiding behind them.

body.text: Pat Lawlor's CSI is built around the number three: three flippers, three pop bumpers, three drop targets, three interactive toys and — the part that decides your score — **three multiballs**. There is no mode ladder to memorise. Instead you get a crowded, unusually flat playfield with exactly one ramp on it, and overlapping multiball rules that reward knowing which pieces fit together.
Reading the playfield

There are **three inlanes** — two left, one right — and they spell C-S-I, which is why the flippers sit slightly right of centre. Above the left flipper is the **Lab saucer**, with a bullet target beside it and three **DNA drop targets** out on the left rail. Directly above the saucer is the **mini flipper**, which fires diagonally to the top right corner; nothing else on the machine can make that shot.

The **Suspect Shakedown** lane loops behind the mini flipper and past the **Skull**, feeding an enclosed bumper pocket that empties back down to the mini flipper. Right of the bumpers is the **Centrifuge**, a spinning disc reachable from either lower flipper, and threaded past its right edge is the machine's only ramp, which feeds the Skull locks. Beyond that: the **Fingerprint spinner**, the **Morgue** sinkhole in the top right corner, the magnet-loaded **Microscope horseshoe** below it, and a wide right loop.
The shot you keep coming back to

The Morgue sinkhole has two names depending on how you get in. From the plunger or the lower flippers it is the **Morgue** — 500K on the skill shot, and every later lit collection is worth 100K more than the last, all game. Entered from the right off the mini flipper, the same hole becomes the **AV Lab**: 250K, Light Special at an outlane, Light Extra Ball at the saucer, or a points award starting at 325K and growing 25K a time.
Three multiballs, three sets of rules

**Skull Multiball** is the simplest to start: shoot the ramp to light a lock, shoot it again to load an eye socket, repeat. Later locks cost more ramp shots. The multiball is a four-level ladder — six yellow-arrow shots at 250K, then six bullet targets at 500K, then the Skull for 750K plus a repeat with your other ball inside five seconds for 750K more, then the Morgue and right loop for a million each. That last level completes it, and the ladder restarts.

**Centrifuge Multiball** is a counter. Every disc spin is 100 points and takes one off a target starting around a hundred spins and growing all game. At zero the disc becomes a ball lock; hit it again and a second ball is served. You then get roughly twenty seconds to inflate the jackpot: switch hits with the live ball at 250 apiece, or flipper-pumping the trapped ball for 100 a spin — the **Big Wow**. Drain the live ball in that window and the whole build is thrown away.

In multiball, a collected jackpot briefly lights a double, and a collected double briefly lights a triple. A triple counts as completing the multiball. Going back into the disc during all this pays **Super Spins** at 15K a spin, climbing 1,250 each collection, multiplied by your best jackpot since the last one — so cash a triple first and the disc pays triple.

**Microscope Multiball** is the deep one, and it needs Evidence first. Shoot the Microscope loop to light Evidence at every major shot, then collect **five pieces of one colour** from red, green and blue, starting at 600K and climbing 100K per piece. Collecting from a shot changes that shot's colour rather than clearing it, so you may need two or three hits to cycle one round. The loop then starts a six-stage, twenty-three-shot marathon: 275K jackpots, 550K doubles, 875K triples for opposite directions, 1,375K quadruples, a fifteen-lamp grid at 550K a shot, and a **5.5M mega jackpot** at the Morgue.
What to do with the rest of the game

items: **Fingerprint Frenzy** — built from right spinner revolutions at 3K each. Once running, every switch is 10K for twenty-five seconds, and both spinner lanes feed the bumper pocket.

**Suspect Shakedown** — fifty spins of the left spinner completes a face and starts a twenty-five second hunt. Six shots light yellow; one hides the suspect for a million, the rest pay from 300K upward.
**Ballistics** — five bullets off the standups at 75K, 250K for the fifth, sixth at the Lab saucer. Forty seconds, awards from 500K rising to a 750K cap.
**DNA and Lab awards** — clearing the three drops lights an award at the saucer: extra ball or 4x bumpers in single-ball play, usually an added ball during a multiball.
**The Photo award** — as a ball leaves the bumper pocket, a mini-flipper shot to the Morgue briefly lights and pays exactly what the bumpers just scored.

body.text: The stack that matters

Skull stacks with Centrifuge, and Centrifuge stacks with Microscope. Skull and Microscope will not stack, because Evidence stops counting while the Skull is running. Light Evidence early so your ordinary shots are always banking progress, then layer a frenzy or Ballistics on top of whichever multiball you are surviving. Finish all three multiballs — the three lamps between the flippers keep score — and the machine offers a single shot worth **fifty million**. Very few players ever see it.

name: Cue Ball Wizard
description: A guide to Cue Ball Wizard: working the Wagon Wheel rounds, clean bank shots, Two Ball Multiball, Pool Ball Mania and the half-billion Nine Ball shot.

body.text: Cue Ball Wizard is a ramp game with a checklist bolted to it. The ramp up the middle is the key to nearly everything, and the wagon wheel above the flippers tells you what the next ramp shot will do. Glance at that wheel before every ramp attempt — the round you start is the one flashing, not the one you were hoping for.
The Wagon Wheel loop

One ramp shot lights the ramp for a Wagon Wheel award, and the next ramp shot starts it. If the ramp goes dark, the Corner Pocket on the left relights it. The wagon wheel target above the right outlane changes which round is queued, so you have real control over what you get.

items: **Rowdy Ramp** — repeat the ramp for 2, 5, 10, 20 and finally 40 million, and the 40 can be collected again and again.
**Horseshoe Extra Ball** — one shot into either mouth of the horseshoe. Take this the moment it comes up.
**NO WAY** — 30 million a hit on a target the cue ball sits in front of.
**Spell DOUBLE** — Corner Pocket first, then the ramp for more letters. Completing it doubles every score, extra ball and special for the rest of the ball.
**Combo Shots** — ramp counting down from 10 million, then either bank shot from 20 million, then the Corner Pocket from 50 million.
**Side Pocket** — 10 million per cue ball into the side pocket, and a rack toward your bonus each time.

body.text: NO WAY deserves a note. The cue ball is parked directly in front of the target, so a straight shot rarely works. The reliable route is to let the ball roll to the very tip of the left flipper before you flip; it comes off the right slingshot at an angle that finds the target far more often than anything you aim at it.
Bank shots are free money

Two ejects sit across the top of the playfield, and there are two kinds of shot into them. A clean bank shot reaches the hole without touching a bumper, and it pays points on a climbing ladder — 1, 2, 5, 7, 10, 15 and 20 million — as well as a random award. An ordinary bank shot only gives the award. The bank shot lamps flash when the next one will count as clean.

The awards are genuinely useful: multiplier advances, racks, spotted letters in DOUBLE and WIZARD, video mode, an extra ball, or starting the current wheel round for you. There is also a window where every bank shot counts as clean — from the end of Pool Ball Mania until Nine Ball Play finishes. That is the cheapest 20 million on the machine.
Two Ball Multiball

The lamps above one drop target bank will be flashing — that is the bank that counts. Clear it and the side pocket starts flashing 8 Ball; hit that and the ramp lights for multiball. Once you are in, jackpots come from driving the 8 ball into the three colour sets on the platform. They start at 5 million each, and every drop target you hit adds a million to whichever jackpots you have not collected yet, so it pays to knock targets around before you cash anything. All three colours light the ramp for a 100 million super, and taking it resets the cycle.
Pool Ball Mania and the half-billion shot

Complete all six Wagon Wheel rounds and the ramp lights for Pool Ball Mania — three balls, with every target on the playfield worth 5 million. Targets, not lanes: the NO WAY shot, both drop banks, the change targets and the side pocket all count, while slingshots, bumpers and the in-and-outlanes do not. The round ends when two of your three balls drain, and none of the total is banked until every ball is gone. Do not tilt during Pool Ball Mania. You will lose the lot.

When Mania ends, the ramp lights for Nine Ball Play, and it only holds that for about 99 seconds before reverting. Start it, clear the 1 through 7 drop targets, sink the 8 ball in the side pocket, and the 9 ball target lights for 500 million — a full billion if you have DOUBLE running. You get roughly fifteen seconds to take it.
The shortcut worth learning

There is a sequencing trick that removes most of the work. Clear the flashing drop bank before you start Pool Ball Mania, which lights the 8 ball at the side pocket. Carry that lit 8 ball into the multiball and then refuse to shoot the side pocket for the whole round. When Mania ends and you start Nine Ball Play, the 8 ball is already banked, so you skip the drop targets entirely and the 9 ball target is sitting there lit. One shot, half a billion.
Bonus, and where the specials hide

Your end-of-ball bonus is 500,000 multiplied by your racks and then by your multiplier, so neither half is optional. The Corner Pocket raises the multiplier; racks come from the Side Pocket round and from clearing either drop bank. Four racks lights a hurry-up extra ball at the wagon wheel target. Push the multiplier to 7 and the two red targets in the top corners light for Special — only one is live at a time, and every bumper hit swaps which.

name: Cyclone
description: A guide to Cyclone: the soft-plunge skill shot, the Comet million, the Cyclone jackpot, Double Score, the Mystery Wheel, Hold Bonus and the outlane special.

body.text: Cyclone is a 1988 carnival game with two flippers, no multiball, and a surprising amount going on. Everything worth having sits on one of three tracks: the Comet ramp ladder, the Cyclone ramp jackpot, and the Bonus X multiplier. Learn which target bank relights which ramp and the machine opens right up.
Plunge softly

The skill shot is five pockets above the top lanes, and this is one of the few machines where a full-power plunge is the wrong answer. Bottom to top the pockets pay 10K, 25K, 100K, 25K and 5K, so the centre one is the target and the back one is the punishment for overshooting. The award is also multiplied by which ball you are on, up to five times — and extra balls advance that multiplier, so a fourth-ball skill shot is possible.
The two ramps, and what relights them

items: The **Comet ramp** sits just left of centre and climbs a value ladder on the back panel in 20K steps, from 20K to 100K. Collect the 100K step and the **Million** lights.
The **Cat targets** to the left of the Comet relight it. They pay 20K each and light the HOLD half of Hold Bonus.
The **Cyclone ramp** is right of the Spook-House and set further back. Three shots while lit before the timer expires pays the jackpot.
The **Duck targets** above the right outlane relight the Cyclone. First completion pays 25K, second 50K, and the third lights the extra ball on the outlanes. Every completion also lights BONUS.
Both ramps return down the right lane, which lights the Ferris Wheel for free every time you make one.

body.text: There is a shortcut most players never spot: a small, half-hidden target on the right side of the Spook-House island spots one of the Cat targets for you. That turns relighting the Comet from a three-target job into a two-target one.
Double Score, and the biggest shot on the machine

Completing the 1-2-3 rollovers starts Double Score — twenty seconds on a factory machine, though operators can set it anywhere from off to ninety-nine. It doubles every point value on the playfield, including the Comet Million, which becomes two million with its own sound effect. It does **not** double the jackpot, so save the Cyclone ramp for outside the window.

That gives you a clear order of operations for the best score available here: build the Comet ladder to the top first, then complete 1-2-3, then make the ramp while the clock runs. Building the ladder after starting the doubler wastes almost all of it.
The jackpot is partly the machine's

Three Cyclone ramps before the timer expires pays the jackpot displayed in lights next to the Mystery Wheel. Collecting drops it back to 500K, so a second jackpot in the same game is worth far less. You can grow it a little as you go — every 1-2-3 rollover hit adds 5K.

The oddity is what happens between games: a game in which somebody collected the jackpot adds a million to the machine's jackpot once the credits run out. Look at the backglass before you start — a high number means the last player collected, and you are walking into a bigger prize.
The Spook-House lottery

A single drop target guards a sinkhole. Knock it down, put the ball in the hole behind it, and the Mystery Wheel on the backglass spins. Awards run from nothing at all up to 200K, and both the extra ball and the special live on it, which makes every trip worth taking. The drop target stands back up on a timer, so the two halves of this shot need to come close together. Your ball returns from the boomerang kickout on the far side of the playfield.
Multiplier, Hold Bonus and the special

The boomerang hole advances your bonus multiplier, but only when its Advance X light is on. That light is cheap: either return lane relights it, and so does any ramp or the Ferris Wheel. Since you are already shooting ramps, the multiplier costs almost nothing to build.

Hold Bonus is spelled across two banks: Cat targets light HOLD, Duck targets light BONUS. Get both and your bonus carries into the next ball instead of resetting — on a machine with no multiball, one of the few ways to compound a good ball. One number on the Bonus X ladder above the flippers is also flashing; drive your multiplier up to it and the special lights. That number varies from machine to machine, anywhere from three to seven.
Two things that make this game safer than it looks

An underhit Comet ramp does not come screaming back at your flippers — it falls through a second hole into the jet bumpers. So you can attack the Comet harder than the layout suggests, and a short shot still pays, because bumper hits build the Ferris Bonus at 3K each. The Ferris Wheel is lit by the right return lane, pays a 50K base plus everything the bumpers added, and returns the ball to the left return lane, relighting Advance X on the way.

The extra ball lights on both outlanes but only one is on at a time, and it toggles constantly as the ball hits flippers, slingshots and bumpers. If a drain is coming anyway, glance at which side is lit and nudge toward that one.

name: Diner
description: How to score on Williams' Diner: the jukebox skill shot, stirring the Cup, building the Dine-Time clock, Beat The Rush, and collecting a twelve million jackpot.

body.text: Diner is a short rulebook played in a specific order. Five cranky customers give you their orders, you serve them by clearing drop targets, and when the last one is fed the machine offers a single jackpot worth twelve million or two million depending entirely on preparation you did twenty shots earlier.
The clock is the score

On the backglass is an analog clock numbered one to twelve. **Whatever it reads is the Dine-Time jackpot in millions.** Three ways move it: completing the E-A-T lanes lights an advance in one of the inlanes, the Today's Special hole sometimes awards one outright, and — the big one — once the Cash Register ramp's value has climbed past 100K, **every further left ramp shot adds a full hour**. Serving your fifth customer with the clock sitting on three is the single most expensive mistake available here.
The opening shot

Shoot the **Cup ramp** — the right ramp — first. One shot does two things: it swings the Cup diverter open for about ten seconds, and it raises the Cash Register ramp's diverter so a ball can be locked underneath. A ball dropped into the Cup whips around the rim, tripping a sensor each lap, and **every two laps** lights the next letter of D-I-N-E-R. The lap value is ten times the lit letter: 25K for D, 50K for I, 75K for N, 100K for E and 250K for R. Once R is lit each further lap is another ten times 100K, up to a **3.5M ceiling** from one shot. After that, five more right ramp shots reopen the diverter.
Lock, then ring the register

With that diverter raised, a shot up the **Cash Register ramp** rolls underneath and locks. The lock stays open between balls until you use it, so a drain costs you nothing. Then hammer the same ramp for value: consecutive shots pay 20K, 40K, 60K, 80K, 100K and keep climbing 20K a time. Past 80K the **Grill lights for an extra ball**, one per ball. Past 100K you are printing clock hours. The ramp backhands from the left flipper and returns to the right inlane, so the loop is comfortable.
Multiball and the Rush

Release the locked ball and the **spinner** — the mirrored half orbit left of the jets — lights for the start. This is the shot people get wrong: it only counts if the ball carries all the way into the **upper left saucer**. A soft spinner shot dribbles into the E-A-T lanes and nothing happens. With a ball already locked, Today's Special usually hands you Start Multiball outright.

Once two balls are out, do not just bash drop targets. For ten to fifteen seconds the upper left saucer and the Today's Special hole both light for **Beat The Rush** — saucer first as Rush 1, sinkhole second as Rush 2, in that order. Make both and **each ramp is worth 500K for the rest of the multiball**, which dwarfs anything the targets are paying. The lights die if a ball drains as well as when the timer expires.
Serving the customers

A customer is served by knocking down all six drop targets across both banks — Root Beer, Fries and Iced Tea on the left; Hot Dog, Burger and Chili on the right. Both banks reset when you complete them, and leaving one or two down and then draining puts all three back up.

There is a shortcut, and it is worth the detour. Completing the **E-A-T lanes** lights a white arrow at the base of each ramp, and while those arrows are lit **a ramp shot spots an entire bank**. That turns five orders into a handful of ramp shots. The E-A-T lanes are steerable with the flippers and the jet bumpers sit right under them feeding balls back up, so completions come easily. They also raise your bonus multiplier to 2x, 3x, 4x and 5x, and pay a flat 100K per completion after that.
Collecting

Serve the fifth customer and the spinner lights for the jackpot: **one million per hour on the clock, up to twelve million**. Same rule as the multiball start — the ball must finish in the upper left saucer. Today's Special ejects into that saucer too, which is a legitimate back door if the spinner is not cooperating. You get ten to fifteen seconds. Miss the window and the machine un-serves your last customer and makes you fill that order again.
Odds and ends

items: **Jukebox skill shot.** With a ball in the shooter lane, the jukebox cycles 150K, 100K, 75K, 50K and 25K. Plunge and the ball runs to the upper left saucer for whatever it stopped on — at 1x, then 2x, then 3x on later attempts.

**The Grill.** Cold it is worth almost nothing. Clear a drop bank and it lights for roughly ten seconds, paying 100K, then 250K, then 500K, then 1.5M on successive collections before resetting. On factory settings that progress carries between balls.
**Today's Special.** Lit at the start of the game and relit by the left inlane. Eight awards: four point values from 25K to 250K, extra ball, Advance Dine-Time and a free Serve Customer.

**Outlane save.** Play your first two balls badly enough and one outlane lights for a limited time. Drain into the lit lane and you get an extra ball — and the lit lane is steerable with the flippers.

name: Dr. Dude
description: A guide to Dr. Dude: collecting the three Elements of Coolness, lighting the lock in the Mix Master, running the Reflex sequence, and the double scoring nobody notices.

body.text: Dr. Dude has a short rulebook and one very good idea in the middle of it. Collect three Elements of Coolness, mix them together in a contraption suspended above the playfield, and cash in a multiball. Around that sits a three-shot Reflex sequence that rewards a steady hand, and a scoring quirk after multiball that most players never notice.
The layout

From the lower left: a short curved lane holds the **Magnetic Personality** target, with a magnet halfway up that catches the ball when the target registers. Above it the **Left Lane** runs from the bumpers to the **Left Saucer**, the award hole for the whole game. Centre playfield is **the Ramp** — very steep, right flipper only — with the **Heart of Rock 'n Roll** standup to its right. Three bumpers and a lone **Top Target** sit above. On the right: six **REFLEX** standups, the gift-wrapped **Gift of Gab** saucer, a half-orbit **Right Lane** fed by the plunger, and four **drop targets** facing left.

The **Mix Master** hangs above the playfield: a six-sided cage with a spinning disc inside and nine standups around its sides, colour-coded in three banks of three. The ramp is the only way in. There is **no kickback** on either outlane, so ball control matters more here than the shot list suggests.
The Elements of Coolness

Three Elements, three hits each. The first hit scores 5K, the second 10K, and the third collects the Element for 25K. Two things make this the friendliest progression here: **the values hold between balls and nothing times out**, and the colour-coded Mix Master banks spot Element shots for you — roughly five hits on a bank credits a shot to the matching Element. After an Element is collected you can keep shooting it; the value just cycles again.

With all three collected, the lock is one target away — but it must be a **Mix Master** target. Making the ramp alone does not light it; the ball has to hit something up there. Then take the lock at the Left Saucer.
Multiball, and the part after it

Multiball has one instruction: hit the Mix Master. The display counts down how many target hits remain before the jackpot — starting at **15**, rising by **10** for every jackpot inside the same multiball. The jackpot is somewhere between 1M and 5M and looks random each time. Completing the four drop targets doubles whichever jackpot you are working towards.
Play it as ball control, not speed:

items: As soon as one ball goes into the Mix Master, **trap the other on the left flipper**.
Loop the ramp with the free ball. Only the right flipper can make the ramp, which is why the left flipper is the parking spot.
Never send both balls up there — they hit each other instead of the targets and tend to come out together.
Do not look away from a ball in the Mix Master; the post on the spinning disc can fling it out without warning.

body.text: Then the rule worth knowing: **when multiball ends, everything scores double for as long as you keep that last ball alive.** Awards even display at their doubled value. There is no restart shot, so that surviving ball is the whole prize — a Reflex round completed under double scoring can outscore the multiball that preceded it.
The Reflex round

Complete the six REFLEX standups (progress is remembered between balls) to light **Reflex 1** at the Left Saucer. That lights **Reflex 2** at the Gift of Gab, which lights **Reflex 3** at Magnetic Personality. Complete all three and you collect the Reflex bonus, which starts at 500K and carries all game.

The timers are not equal, and that shapes how you play it. Reflex 1 waits indefinitely, so set the next shot up properly. Reflex 2 times out **very** fast. If you miss it, let the timer expire, get the ball under control, and start again from Reflex 1 — chasing it with an uncontrolled shot is how balls get lost, and a missed Reflex 2 relights Reflex 1 immediately anyway. Reflex 3 has a longer timer, usually good for two or three attempts, but missing it ends the round outright.

Two ways to grow the value: completing the targets again while Reflex 1 is lit adds 250K, and completing the sequence adds 500K. Reflex is still available during multiball, with far more generous timers.
Awards and small print

items: **Bag O' Tricks** — a random award at the Left Saucer, lit at the start of every ball and relit by the drop targets. The pool runs from a joke ten points to Light Mix Master (spots every uncollected Element), Million Is Lit, Jackpot At Max, Bonus X At Max, Extra Ball and Special. Not available during multiball, though a drop completion there leaves it lit afterwards.
**Drop targets** — the first three completions give 2x, 4x and 6x bonus, the fourth lights Million on the ramp, and every completion relights Bag O' Tricks.
**The Left Saucer stacks.** Several awards can be lit at once and one shot collects all of them, so let them pile up.
**The sympathy extra ball** — reach ball three having played badly and the game lights an extra ball at the Left Saucer. You still have to collect it.
The Bag awards Elements in a fixed order: Magnetic Personality, Gift of Gab, Heart of Rock 'n Roll.

name: Eight Ball Deluxe
description: A player's guide to Bally's Eight Ball Deluxe: racking the drops, the 8 Ball ladder, DELUXE, the super bonus, the corner pocket, and where all six Specials hide.

body.text: Eight Ball Deluxe is early solid-state, which usually means a thin rulebook. This one is an exception. A real chain of dependencies runs through it — clear the rack, light the 8 Ball, light DELUXE, complete DELUXE, reset the rack, feed the super bonus — plus a bonus formula worth understanding before you play rather than after.
Racking the balls

Seven **drop targets** run down the right side, 2K each. All seven down lights the **8 Ball target** in the top right corner. Two things about this bank matter. In a multiplayer game the same physical targets carry different numbers for each player — you only ever clear your own rack, and the machine rebuilds your exact state next ball by standing everything up and then dropping the ones that should be down. And, contrary to what you may be told: **hitting the 8 Ball never resets the drops.** A lit 8 Ball is free to shoot at whenever you want it.
The 8 Ball ladder

The 8 Ball target pays whatever value is lit and then raises it: **20K, 40K, 60K**. Unlit it is worth a token few hundred. Hit it once 60K is showing and the corner pocket and both outlanes light for **Special** — the outlane light alternates sides on slingshot hits, so check which is live before you nudge. Completing the A-B-C-D lanes also raises the 8 Ball value, so you can push it past 60K without shooting the target at all.

There is a light between the flippers most players never read. When it is on, the next hit on a **lit** 8 Ball pays a Special as well as its points — that falls on the second and third lit hits, depending on the setting.
DELUXE, twice over

Hitting the lit 8 Ball lights the six round **DELUXE targets** offset behind and between the ball drops. They pay 3K lit or unlit, but hitting a lit one puts its letter out. Complete all six and you score 50K or a Special, **reset the entire rack**, and add 56K to your super bonus.

The generous part: if DELUXE is lit and you drain before finishing it, the machine still adds 56K to the super bonus and still resets the drops next ball. Lighting DELUXE is never a wasted shot. Depending on the setting, either only the letters you missed relight, or all six do.

Every playfield DELUXE also lights the next letter of **DELUXE on the backglass**. Finish all six and the letters dance and you are paid up to three Specials. Those backglass letters **stay lit between games** — an unusual rule, and worth a glance before you drop a coin, because someone else may have done most of the work.
The bonus formula

This is where games are won. Your bonus is **(super bonus + 7K per downed ball drop) × multiplier**. A lit 8 Ball counts toward it when down; an unlit one does not. The super bonus is a separate pot holding only 0, 56K or 112K, added **before** the multiply — which is why filling it and then setting 5x beats either on its own.

The multiplier comes from the **inline drop bank** at the top left. Each target sets it outright to the figure printed on it, up to 5x. It is also the most dangerous bank to shoot at — the rebound is unkind, so take it from a settled ball rather than on the fly.

Then there is the **corner pocket**, a pothole behind the 8 Ball target that pays your entire bonus — super bonus plus bonus, times the multiplier — while your ball keeps playing. Shooting it at 1x with an empty rack throws it away. Set the multiplier, get the rack down, then take the pocket. Some machines pay bonus only with no multiplier, so watch what it gives you the first time.
The rest of the playfield

items: **Left loop.** Pays the lit value and lights the next: 10K, 30K, 50K, extra ball, 70K, Special. The first three always come in that order, and some setups make you run the ladder twice before the Special is available. Unlit, the loop is worth a few hundred.

**A-B-C-D lanes.** A and B are the top rollovers, and on most three-ball setups either C or D spots both. Completing all four spots the uppermost unhit drops, lights a bumper, and raises the 8 Ball value.
**Thumper bumpers.** Around 500 idle, **3,000 flashing** — six times what a drop target pays. They light in a fixed order: upper left, upper right, then bottom.

**The 25K rollover.** With A and B collected but C or D outstanding, one top lane lights for 25K. The lit lane swaps sides on every bumper and slingshot hit, and goes out for good once A-B-C-D is complete.
**Bank shot.** The round target behind the multiplier drops, paying 50K or a Special. Whether that alternates, and which comes first, is an operator setting.

body.text: One caveat

More of this machine is operator-adjustable than is typical. Whether C and D spot each other, how many targets A-B-C-D spots, whether Specials alternate with points, whether the corner pocket multiplies, how many Specials the backglass pays — all of it can be changed. Treat these values as common factory behaviour and spend your first ball on an unfamiliar machine finding out what that one actually does.

name: Fire!
description: How to play Williams' Fire!: the six-value skill shot lane, putting out fire groups before the bonus level decays, locking firemen in the buildings, and reaching Rescue Multiball.

body.text: Fire! is a System 11A machine and a deliberate departure from the standard layout of its era. Hunt for drop targets and you will find none, there is not a pop bumper anywhere on the playfield, and no lane change either, so your flipper buttons will not shuffle the inlane lamps. Instead there is a burning building at the top, four banks of flame targets, two long ramps that climb until the ball nearly touches the glass, and a loop whose entrances raise and lower to route the ball three ways. Understanding those entrances is most of the game.
The skill shot lane

The shooter lane ends partway up the playfield at a one-way gate angled at about 45 degrees. Past it sit five rollover sensors and a standup at the far end, and their values are deliberately out of order: **20,000, then 10,000, then 30,000, then 100,000, then 5,000**, with the standup worth a miserable 1,000. You score the highest sensor the ball crosses, so the target is the fourth — reach it, stall, and let the ball roll back into play. Overcook it and you get a thousand points.

There is a trick here with a real cost: plunge very lightly and the ball can trip the first sensor without clearing the gate, which then pushes it back for another go. It is only 20,000 a time, and every second in the lane is a second the current fire burns your bonus level down.
Putting out fires

This is the whole game. Flame targets light in groups of three, and every target in a group has to go out before the group counts as extinguished. Four banks of three exist: one on each small building flanking the ladder ramp, and one inside each of the two lock buildings halfway up the playfield. Any trip through the loop puts out one lit flame for free, which makes it the most efficient and safest way to work a group down.

What makes it urgent is the bonus level. A column runs 10x, 7x, 5x, 3x, 2x. At the start of a ball the 10x is blinking and the rest are solid. Dawdle over a fire and the 10x drops out, the 7x starts blinking, and so on down until you are getting nothing. Put the fire out and the timer resets with the column back at the top. Take too long and the machine lights a second group alongside the first — or, if you are lucky, relights the one you are already working on.
Reading the loop entrances
Both outer loop entrances raise and lower independently, and the combination decides where a ball ends up. Nothing on the playfield explains it.

items: **Both entrances up** — the starting position. A ball into the left comes out the right and vice versa, running the lower loop.
**Both entrances down** — the same behaviour, routed over the upper loop instead.
**One up, one down** — shoot the lowered side and the ball runs the top loop, crosses the raised entrance, and is dropped into a building and locked.
**Shooting the raised side** while the other is down just lets the ball back out again.

body.text: That third case is how locks happen. Put out every flame on the building you want to fill, and the loop entrance on the **opposite** side drops. Shoot up that far side, ride the top loop, and your fireman is trapped in the building you just cleared. This is where most players shoot the wrong hole — the entrance that opens is not the one next to the building.
The turnaround, the ladder and the fire plug

A U-shaped channel curls away behind the ladder ramp, taking a mouth on either side of it, and each mouth carries its own insert lamp. It is the most underrated shot here, because it does three jobs. Every pass raises the **fire plug** — a small post between the flippers that blocks the centre drain — for a few seconds. A pass from the lit side also raises the bonus level and puts the ladder up.

With the ladder flush, a centre shot bounces off a post and comes straight back. Raised, the same shot goes through the window into the building. It only stays up for an operator-set period, and the machine ticks the seconds off audibly while the rescue lamp flashes — that flashing is your clock, not decoration.
Multiball, the extra ball and the specials

With a ball locked in each building, both loop entrances come back up and the rescue lights come on. Run a ball through the lower loop to raise the ladder, then take the window shot to start it. Once you are in, **put out every lit fire while at least two balls are still in play and the machine pays a million**.

The extra ball is a two-stage ask. Go all the way up each of the two long side ramps once — the sensor is right at the top, so a weak shot does not register — and one of them will then light at random. Hit the target at the top of the lit ramp again and the extra ball is yours. Slingshot hits cycle which side carries the light, and which turnaround lamp is lit, so a rattle in the lower playfield can hand you the side you want.
Push the bonus level to 10x and take one more lit turnaround, and both outlanes light for special. On this machine, at that moment, draining is the correct play.

name: Firepower
description: How to play Williams' Firepower: completing F-I-R-E and P-O-W-E-R, keeping the Shield lit, lighting all three locks for the first solid-state multiball, and the outlane Specials.

body.text: Firepower, released in March 1980, is one of the most important machines ever built: the first solid-state game with multiball, and over seventeen thousand were made. The ruleset is small by modern standards but unusually well balanced, and it repays a player who knows what each shot actually buys.
The layout

Two flippers in the standard place, four pop bumpers, three eject holes and one spinner. The plunger lane sits on the right and releases the ball near the top. Going anti-clockwise: the **Lower Right Lock** on the inside of the curve, the **Upper Right Lock** above the curve exit, the four **F-I-R-E rollover lanes** at the top centre with a bullseye standup among them, four pop bumpers below in a square, then two banks of three **centre stand-up targets**. Down the left is the **Left Spinner Lane** with the **Left Lock** beside it, and at the bottom right the three **P-O-W-E-R** stand-ups. The left outlane holds a kickback called the Shield.

One frequent misreading: the three inserts stacked below the bullseye target marked 10,000, 30,000 and 50,000 have nothing to do with that target. They track the Firepower Bonus. The bullseye itself is worth 1,000.
The plunge, and F-I-R-E

You get two plunges. A **light plunge** drops the ball straight down to the flippers. A **full plunge** carries it round the curve into the area above the F-I-R-E lanes — and because one-way gates guard both entrances, a ball that gets up there has to leave through one of the four lanes. That is a guaranteed letter, and the right flipper rotates lit lanes one place at a time, so completing F-I-R-E is genuinely cheap.

Each completion steps the bonus multiplier: **2X, 3X, 4X, 5X**. Once you are at 5X, one more completion lights the extra ball, which is then collected on the P-O-W-E-R bank. On factory settings all of that has to happen within a single ball, which is what makes the extra ball hard — more liberally set machines carry multipliers over and make it much easier.
The centre targets do everything
Six standups in two banks of three, and they are the engine of the game. Learn what each completion buys:

items: **One bank** lights the Shield — the left outlane kickback — whether those targets were already collected or not.
**Both banks** light two of the three eject holes and put the spinner on 1,000 a spin instead of 100.
**Both banks again** lights the third eject hole and lights the remaining two pop bumpers.
Every target is worth 1,000 whether lit or unlit, which makes this the safe default shot when nothing else is on.

body.text: **Keeping the Shield lit is the single best habit on this machine.** It goes out the moment it fires, and relighting it costs one bank of targets — a shot you were making anyway. With the Shield up, the left outlane stops being a drain and becomes a free return.
Multiball, and the shot that gets you there

Lock a ball in all three eject holes and all three release at once. Two are easy — the Left Lock and the Lower Right Lock are both straightforward from the flippers. The **Upper Right Lock** is the problem, and also the best shot on the playfield. It cannot be entered from the right: a ball from the plunger lane passes underneath it. The only reliable way in is up the **left spinner lane**, which hooks hard right at the top and fires the ball through a gate across the F-I-R-E area into the hole from the far side. Hit crisply with the spinner lit, it pays twice — once in spins, once in the lock.

Be honest about what multiball is here. There is no jackpot and no objective — this predates all that. What it gives you is two or three times the playfield activity, which is exactly when finishing F-I-R-E, sweeping P-O-W-E-R and building bonus get easier. Treat it as a feature-collection window, not a scoring mode.
Firepower Bonus and the Specials

Complete both **F-I-R-E** and **P-O-W-E-R** in the same ball and you collect the Firepower Bonus: 10,000, then 30,000, then 50,000, tracked by those stacked inserts in the bumper area. Take it all three times and **both outlanes light for Special** — the deepest thing in the ruleset, and not something anyone reaches by accident.
P-O-W-E-R is worth completing on its own regardless. It turns both return lanes from 1,000 into 3,000, and it is where a lit extra ball is collected.
Bonus, and a simple game plan

End-of-ball bonus runs from 1,000 to 29,000 and multiplies up to 5X, so a fully built ball is worth 145,000. Bonus comes from collecting features for the **first** time, not from repeating shots — so spread your shots around, and get the multiplier up early so everything after counts for more.

items: Keep the Shield lit at all times. It costs one target bank.
Work F-I-R-E with lane change every time the ball is at the top.
When nothing is lit, hit the centre stand-ups — 1,000 each, no risk, and they move the Shield, the locks and the bumpers along at once.
Learn the spinner lane. It is the one hard shot, and it unlocks both the third lock and the game's best sound.
Collect features in multiball rather than trying to score in it.

name: Fish Tales
description: A guide to Fish Tales: the Long Cast loop, the captive ball ladder, Monster Fish parity, Rock the Boat, Feeding Frenzy, and the hundred-million Super Jackpot.

body.text: Fish Tales has a reputation as an easy game and it is not entirely deserved. The ramps are friendly and the layout is open, but the two shots that decide your score — the Caster's Club and the captive ball — are both awkward, and everything worth having runs through one of them.
The left return lane is the most important lane on the machine

It always lights the **Long Cast**, the right looping shot, and its light never goes out. Your first Long Cast is worth a million and it climbs to five, but the points are not the reason to shoot it — every Long Cast lights the next unclaimed value on the captive ball, and that is where the game's best awards live. If one is about to time out, rolling the left return lane again refreshes the whole timer without dropping your current value. If Long Cast is dark, shooting the right loop anyway just turns it back on.

The captive ball sits inside an inclined boat, so a soft hit moves it without registering — only a hit hard enough to reach the top switch counts. The ladder runs Hold Bonus at one million, Video Mode at two, Rock the Boat at three, Light Extra Ball at five and Instant Multiball at ten. You can light every value before collecting any, but each hit takes only one award. Every registered hit also pays **Grab Yer Gear** — a million times the highest award still lit, or 500,000 when nothing is. Finish the ladder and the captive ball pays five million a hit, rising 500,000 to a ten-million ceiling.
Monster Fish, and playing the parity

Six lit ramp shots light the school of fish under the boat and turn the spinner into a hurry-up. The ramps themselves pay 500,000 rising to three million, so lighting a Monster Fish has already banked 10.5 million before you shoot the spinner. The hurry-up starts at twenty million and drops 100,000 every tenth of a second down to a five-million floor, then gives you five more seconds at that floor.

Always collect it, even at the floor. Miss it and the value sits where it stopped; take it at any price and the next is worth ten million more, up to a fifty-million ceiling. The habit that separates good scores from great ones is counting where you are in the school so the sixth ramp comes off the **left** flipper. Shooting the last fish from the right means the ball has to transfer across before you can reach the spinner, and every tenth of a second costs you 100,000.
The timed modes

items: **Stretch the Truth** — completing a Stringer lights the spinner for ten to fifteen seconds. It scores one tale per Stringer you hold, each fish worth up to five million. Every L-I-E you spell darkens the lowest spinner value until only the 5x survives.

**Rock the Boat** — twenty seconds from the captive ball, thirty from four tales. Every boat shot is ten million, and there are three: both ramps and the captive ball. Live on the ramps; backhanding one repeatedly grooves faster than alternating.

**Feeding Frenzy** — four purple fish on a rolling fifteen-second clock, worth 5M, 5M, 5M and then 20M. Take the Long Cast and spinner fish first, and hold the ramp fish back to buy another fifteen seconds.

**Video Mode** — twenty torpedoes, twenty seconds, boats at three distances. Shoot the far row: it pays 1.5 million each and the extra ball only appears on the back line. The flipper buttons fire torpedoes better than the rod button, and the game never says so.

body.text: The U-turn is a real shot

A ramp attempt that runs out of steam and comes back down the other side pays a million, counts as a boat shot for Rock the Boat, and collects both ramp fish at once during Feeding Frenzy, because only the boat ramp sensor is needed. Stop treating weak ramps as failures.
Multiball is two shots repeated

Caster's Club to light a jackpot, eject hole within fifteen seconds to score it. Jackpots run twenty, thirty and forty million, and the tackle box shows which is next. With all three balls alive the Caster's Club flashes for **Doubles Jackpot** — a second ball doubles the value and restarts the clock, but time out and both balls come flying back with nothing scored.

Take all three jackpots and the captive ball lights for a hundred million per hit, repeatedly, until multiball ends. You do not need all three in one multiball; the machine remembers where you are for the whole game. Better still, every completed sequence multiplies all the jackpots — including the captive ball — and the multiplier climbs as far as six.
Two habits worth building

First, do not waste an Instant Multiball. Cashing it during multiball throws it away, and with two balls locked you should always start regular multiball first, because Instant Multiball leaves you with no locks afterwards. Second, do not force the Stringer targets — they are frequent drain shots, and unless you are one fish from Feeding Frenzy the ball will find them on its own. Autocast, the ball save, is quick enough to return a ball before it has finished draining, and a death save on the one you lost leaves you with a small multiball.

name: The Flintstones
description: A guide to The Flintstones pinball: the 1-2-3 ramps and four modes, spelling CONCRETE for multiball, Bronto Crane awards, bowling, and where the real points hide.

body.text: The Flintstones is a four-ball game with an unusually generous rule set for its era: almost everything runs concurrently. Modes stack with each other, they carry on through multiball, and you can start the Time Machine target modes while three balls are loose. That changes how you should play it — instead of clearing one thing at a time, you want several counters running at once and a multiball on top of them.
The layout in one pass

Two ramps feed a bottom loop running above the centre drain, which means either ramp can hand the ball to either flipper — and the game chooses based on what it wants you to shoot next. Two orbits run around the back. A narrow centre lane sits right of the Bowl-A-Rama targets and feeds the DIG rollovers. An upper flipper guards the right orbit and is the honest way to reach the BED drops, the U-Turn lane and Bronto Crane. Watch that centre lane: it is tight enough that a fast ball rattles and comes straight back down the middle.
1-2-3 and the four modes

Three lit ramp shots — not always on the same ramp — pay 2, 4 and 6 million and start a mode. Which mode starts is whichever one is flashing on the mode row, and bumper hits move that along, so you have more control than it first appears.

items: **Fred's Choice:** twenty seconds, three lit shots, three voices arguing. Left orbit is 20 million, right orbit 15, centre lane 10, and each shot raises its own value by 3 million.

**Joe's Diner:** fifteen million counts down until your first shot lands, then that frozen value is paid three times — two more shots inside twenty seconds, with the centre lane collecting the lot. Shoot early to freeze it high.
**Bedrock Water Buffalos:** twenty-five seconds of throwing things at a band using the BED drops, switching to the ROCK drops partway through.
**Dino Frenzy:** a two-ball multiball on the three Dino/Frenzy standups, starting at 10 million a hit.

body.text: Dino Frenzy deserves special attention because it is the one mode you can prepare all game. One of the three targets is always lit for Dino, and hitting the lit one adds a million to the frenzy value permanently — not just during the mode. Feed that target every time you see it and the mode pays several times what it otherwise would. Finish all four modes and Mystery Mode opens: twenty seconds, both drop banks, 5 million a target and 100 million if you clear all seven.
Inventing concrete

Multiball needs CONCRETE spelled out, and there are four ways to add letters: clearing the BED bank, clearing the ROCK bank, completing DIG for your first multiball only, and the Spell CONCRETE award from Bronto Crane. Letters often arrive two at a time, so it comes around faster than eight letters suggests. Start it on either orbit. The jackpot opens at 40 million and keeps growing for as long as at least one ball is sitting in the Time Machine wheel — so parking a ball up there is the strategy, not an accident. Collect the jackpot at the centre lane and the super at the U-Turn; the ball that scores the jackpot usually carries on to the upper flipper to set up the super.
Bronto Crane and the Time Machine target

One left orbit lights the crane, the next one collects it. The award pool is small and several of them are worth hunting: doubled 1-2-3 values, an extra ball, Spell CONCRETE, the bowling power-up, 2x playfield, a maxed bonus multiplier, 20 million, or Bedrock Derby — a bumper race worth 30 million that a handful of bumper hits will usually win. Separately, the standup facing the flippers hands out three modes in a fixed order, so you always know what the next hit buys: Time Machine, then Job Change, then Help.
Bowling

One of the two ramps is always lit for Go Bowling. Take it, the ball comes back to your right flipper, and you have about five seconds to throw at the Bowl-A-Rama targets — centre for a 5 million strike, either side for a 3 million spare, nothing at all for a miss. Three strikes starts a two-ball Bowl-A-Rama multiball where the same targets pay 20 and 10 million. Completing the target bank during ordinary play, rather than after a Go Bowling shot, builds Yabba-Dabba-Doo, and finishing that hands you the bowling power-up: a guaranteed strike on your next throw.
Small rules that add up

items: The centre lane keeps a running count all game. The seventh one is your extra ball; the award after that is DIG Millions, which turns the bumpers into a scoring feature.
The U-Turn is worth an increasing million even with nothing lit on it, starting at 2 million. Its switch is at the entrance, so a shot that fails the loop still counts.
DIG completions pay 5 million each and build the bonus multiplier to 10x, after which every completion is a flat 10 million.
The shell targets on either wall light Drain Shield on the outlanes. There is no kickback — a saved ball is auto-plunged, so be ready rather than cradling.
Buying an extra ball starts whichever mode is currently flashing, so set the mode row with the bumpers before your last ball drains.

name: Game of Thrones
description: How Game of Thrones actually plays: picking a house, qualifying and stacking battles, both multiballs, the battering ram multiplier engine, and the road to Iron Throne.

body.text: Game of Thrones asks you a question before the ball is in the shooter lane, and most players answer it badly. Your house choice is not flavour — it is a permanent perk plus a button power you will press dozens of times. Everything after that is the same seven shots in different arrangements.
Choose your house first, and choose on purpose
Whichever house you pick is immediately qualified to battle, so you can start scoring straight away. The persistent perk matters more than the button in most cases.

items: **Tyrell** keeps one inlane permanently lit for the combo multiplier and lets you move it with lane change. In a game built out of 40-second timed battles, free multiplier on every return is the strongest quiet perk on the machine.

**Lannister** pays around 1.5x gold from the standups you hit by accident all game, and its button buys playfield multiplier levels outright at 600 gold per level — capped at eight uses, so spend them deliberately.
**Greyjoy** starts already complete and inherits the perk of every house you defeat. The price is that every battle needs more shots and you can only fight one house at a time.
**Targaryen** spots its entire three-level battle for free, which is a large head start toward the wizard modes, and its button freezes every running timer for 15 seconds.
**Stark, Baratheon and Martell** are narrower: bigger Winter is Coming hurry-ups, a head start plus outlane saves, and an add-a-ball in any multiball respectively.

body.text: Seven shots, seven houses

Each house owns a shot, and three hits on that shot qualifies it. Left drop bank is Baratheon, left loop is Greyjoy, the Dragon lane — or Castle Black on Premium and LE — is Targaryen, the left ramp is Lannister, the right ramp is Stark, the right loop is Martell, and the right 2-bank is Tyrell. The left ramp is the busiest shot in the game: it locks balls, starts every battle, and starts both wizard modes.
Battles and stacking

With two or more houses qualified you can stack a pair into one battle, which is the main way of getting through seven houses inside three balls. You can also pass and bank the qualification, though you cannot pass when only one house remains. A battle that times out does not need requalifying — just shoot the ramp again — and Lannister, Greyjoy, Tyrell and Targaryen remember the progress you already made. Read the objective early: Martell only needs three orbits inside a rolling ten-second window, while Greyjoy lights everything and gives you fifteen seconds that refresh on each shot.
The multiballs

items: **Blackwater** is the workhorse. Complete the right 2-bank to light a lock, then lock at the left ramp — and you must lock before you can light the next one. The first lock needs one green target, the second needs both, the third and later need both on a timer.
**Battle at the Wall** is a grind: six top lane completions on the Pro, or six Castle Black shots on Premium and LE. The second one costs eleven, so it is not a repeatable strategy.

**Castle Multiball** lives entirely on the Premium and LE upper playfield, collected in four steps — Archers, Charge, Breach, then the multiball. Each step raises a drop target in front of your right ramp until you clear it.

body.text: The battering ram is the scoring engine

Almost all of this machine's big numbers route through the ram. Three hits qualify the playfield multiplier and a fourth starts it, with each further 1x costing four more hits up to 5x. The catch is the blue arrow in front of it — advance while it flashes or the progress lapses and a three-hit ladder quietly costs you six. Wildfire lit at the ram drops each level from four hits to three. Swords, collected on the right ramp after every completed battle, raise the multiplier ceiling from 3x toward 5x. When the ball is heading down, press the action button to cash your multipliers rather than watching them expire.
Winter is coming, and then it comes

Every shot you use to qualify a house ices over. Freeze three of them and a hurry-up starts on the last one you froze. Four collected hurry-ups drop you into Winter Has Come, a four-ball multiball alternating between a Horde phase with a hidden ticking timer and a Lieutenant phase that freezes your left flipper if you let a shot expire. One trap worth memorising: starting a hurry-up on the mode-start ramp with your third Blackwater lock lit launches multiball with no chance to stack a house into it.
A workable plan

items: Pick Tyrell or Lannister if you want points, Targaryen or Greyjoy if you want to reach the wizard modes.
Qualify houses in pairs and stack them; four completed houses lights Hand of the King, all seven lights Iron Throne.
Bash the ram whenever the arrow is flashing, and collect swords so the multiplier can actually climb.
Save Lord of Light — by default the drop bank only gives it once for the whole game — for a multiball rather than spending it on ball one.
If the machine boots into casual mode and will not let you choose a house, hold the right flipper for three seconds before starting.

name: Game Show
description: A guide to Bally's Game Show: the skill shot and bonus multiplier, lighting and collecting the four prizes, spinning and nudging the Wheel, and starting Showcase Bonanza.

body.text: Game Show is a simple machine and an honest one. One lock, one diverter, a lamp wheel in the lower centre and four prizes to win. Nothing is hidden or clever, which makes it a good machine to learn structured play on — every award has a visible lamp and every lamp has a shot attached. What separates a good game from a bad one is knowing which inlane you just rolled through, and whether the diverter will let your ramp shot reach the saucer.
The skill shot and your multiplier

The plunger delivers the ball onto a raised plastic above the C-A-S-H rollovers, with four holes to drop through. One of the four lanes below is flashing, and you cannot move it — plunge strength is your only control. Land the flashing lane and the bonus multiplier advances one step. It starts at 2X and climbs by one to a ceiling of **10X**. Because the Collect Ramp joins the plunger lane, a weak plunge rolls back down the ramp into play rather than being wasted, and a very weak one simply returns to the plunger.
Winning the four prizes

There are four: a TV, a trip, a truck and a car. The TV is two targets, TRIP is four down the right wall, TRUCK is five down the left wall, and the car is a single drop target left of the CASH lanes. Completing a set makes that prize flash at the base of the Collect Ramp, and you cash it at the Collect Saucer on the far left, which is only reachable through that ramp. Once a prize is collected it cannot be won again until all the others have been collected too, so the game naturally pushes you around all four.

items: You do not have to hit every target. **A full traversal of the rear loop spots a letter** for you, in the direction the SPOT arrow indicates.
Only complete loops count — half a loop that dies in the CASH lanes does not.
The arrow does not move when you complete a loop, so a ball returning to the opposite flipper can be sent straight back for another. Chain them.
Letters are spotted cheapest first: TV, then TRIP, then TRUCK, then the car.
Bumper and slingshot hits swap which loop entrance carries the arrow, so check before you shoot.

body.text: Reading the Collect Ramp

One ramp, two destinations. With nothing lit, the Collect Ramp carries on up to the skill shot plastic and drops you into the CASH lanes, which is useful in itself because those rollovers build your bonus. Only when Collect is lit does the diverter open the path to the Collect Saucer — and even then, an under-hit shot never clears the skill shot area and you end up back on the plastic. Shoot it freely when nothing is lit, and shoot it **hard** when a prize is waiting.
Showcase Bonanza

The moment the Collect Ramp could finish off all four prizes, Lock lights there too — it does not matter whether some are already banked, only that this shot could complete the set. Take it and you get the prize awards, then a two-ball multiball with the ramp lit for a jackpot. It opens at **$3,000,000**, holds for a few seconds, then falls about $100,000 every couple of seconds until it floors at $1,000,000. After the second ball is plunged the diverter stays shut until you hit any switch, and that hit also ejects the locked ball.
The Wheel

The circle of lamps in the lower centre holds point values and four feature awards on its rim. The right inlane lights SPIN at the Wheel Ramp; a complete 270-degree loop spins the wheel and pays whatever it lands on. Straight after a spin, NUDGE lights — and every further loop while it is lit steps the wheel along exactly one space. Because the ramp returns the ball to the left inlane and the left inlane relights NUDGE, you can walk the wheel a full circle under complete control. That is the key insight of the machine: the wheel is not luck, it is a dial you turn.
Choosing a feature

Four spaces on the rim carry features, marked with clear round lamps, and one flashes at a time. Landing on the flashing one pays the feature plus that space's points. One is a flat million. One lights the left loop for two million, and making it in time lights the right loop for another two. One lights the extra ball at the left loop, and unlike almost everything else here it stays lit for the rest of the ball — so nudge toward it deliberately. The last is Hold Bonus, which carries your multiplier into the next ball. Once a feature is taken it stays steadily lit, and none return until all four have gone.
Two last things

Drop the car target and a sinkhole opens behind it. Big Bucks pays $100,100 and adds the same again on every repeat within the ball, and since it returns to the right inlane it feeds its own repeat with SPIN freshly lit. It is a long shot for a modest reward, so treat it as a bonus rather than a plan. And take comfort in the Wheel Ramp: a ball rejected off its initial rise will not drain down the middle. Shoot it without fear.

name: GoldenEye
description: A player's guide to Sega's GoldenEye: the Satellite dish and its 200M shot, the Eject or Die ball save, the five 007 Encounters, and the five-item wizard mode checklist.

body.text: GoldenEye is Sega at its most inventive. The centrepiece is a rotating satellite dish with a magnet at its hub, loaded by a ramp that rises up out of the playfield when you roll the left inlane. Down at the outhole there is a second magnet that catches draining balls and flings them back into play. Three genuinely shootable ramps give the game a flow that earlier Segas never had. Underneath all of it is a wizard mode gated behind a five-item checklist, and that checklist should be your entire plan for the game.
The five requirements

Everything else is decoration. Five boxes have to be ticked before the Mode Start Lane will light for the wizard mode: all five 007 Encounters started and ended, the 0-0-7 top lanes rolled, Shootout beaten, Q's Pen carried all the way through its third hit, and GOLDENEYE spelled out with ramp shots. Note the wording on the encounters — you only have to **start and end** them, not complete them, so a mode you are losing badly is still doing its job. You know the wizard mode is ready when all five mode indicators start flashing together.

items: Do the **0-0-7 lanes on ball one**. A plunged ball rolls them for free; after that the only route in is a lucky bumper kick, and none of them count during multiball.
**Q's Pen** is the piece most players are missing. Three hits on the white target just to arm it, then three more inside fourteen seconds.
**Shootout** is not solved with the ball — see below.
**GOLDENEYE** is spelled with ramp shots during single-ball play with no encounter running.
Xenia Extra Ball is one of the five encounters and it is the **only** extra ball in the entire game. Never pass on it.

body.text: Shootout and Eject or Die

Clear the three white targets on the Shootout bank, hit the small yellow target between them, and three guards appear with an instruction to shoot. Players stand there hammering the flippers. The machine has a **gun on the front of the cabinet** — six pulls of the trigger, two per guard, finishes the mode. The shots climb 2M, 4M, 6M, 8M and 10M, and then Eject or Die lights at both outlanes. This matters enormously because GoldenEye has no kickback. With Eject or Die lit, an outlane drain during single-ball play gets caught by the outhole magnet and thrown back out, and a six-second clock starts. Land the Center Eject Target inside it or that ball really is finished. Six seconds is about one attempt, so make it a good one — and note that the clock pauses while the ball is rattling around in the bumpers. Eject or Die stacks, so finishing Shootout several times banks several saves.
One target controls the whole economy

The white Satellite Value target in the satellite bank toggles a number through 10M, 25M, 50M, 75M and 100M. That number is the Guard award for clearing all six green Guard targets, and it is also the jackpot value in both multiballs. Setting it before you start anything is the single cheapest decision on the machine. The flip side is a trap: during Tank Multiball, hitting any Guard target **cycles the value**, so a careless stray hit can turn a 100M jackpot into a 10M one.
The two multiballs are not equal

One hit on the Center Eject Target puts the Lock Ramp on, and the ramp itself is what banks the Virtual Lock. Two locks light Satellite Multiball, and from there the left inlane is what throws the pop-up ramp into position for a swing at the dish. Both multiballs use the same four jackpot shots — three ramps and the Mode Start Lane — but Satellite Multiball has a payoff Tank Multiball does not. Sweep all four jackpots without dropping below two balls and the ramp arms again to knock the stuck ball off the dish for **200M**, followed by a roving 150M Super Jackpot. Tank Multiball has none of that, which is why you can and often should cancel it outright by pulling the gun trigger during the opening animation. Satellite Multiball stays lit for later.
The GOLDENEYE hurry-ups

Spelling GOLDENEYE pays 10M and immediately lights all three ramps for hurry-ups. Each opens at 50M and bleeds a million a second down to 20M. Collect all three and the left inlane arms the pop-up ramp one more time, and landing that Satellite shot pays your hurry-up total all over again plus another 10M. A clean run is worth over 300M, which dwarfs almost anything else outside multiball. Hesitation is what costs you here, so decide your ramp order before the sequence starts.
Small things that add up

A trip through the right inlane arms Mystery at the Mode Start Lane for a couple of seconds — take it on reflex, but know that its 2X award does not spot the top lanes toward the checklist. Ramp combos start at 10M and grow 2M for each unbroken link, resetting the moment you miss. Your bonus is a flat million per ramp and Mode Start Lane shot times your multiplier, and the Collect Bonus lane above the right inlane cashes it mid-ball. And before your very first plunge, pull the trigger during the opening animation — there are a dozen different hidden endings hiding in there.

name: Guns N' Roses
description: Data East's Guns N' Roses rules: locking the Guitar mode you want, the Double shot, the ramp ladder, Snake Pit multipliers, six-ball Multiball and the billion-point Riot jackpot.

body.text: Guns N' Roses is a widebody with two plungers. The **gun autoplunger** sits in the usual place; the **Rose Plunger** is manual, on the left side of the cabinet, fed by the G Ramp when the yellow globe flashes. Everything it launches spins in the Snake Pit, and how long it spins decides some of the biggest numbers in the game.
The trigger is a control, not a launcher

There are nine Guitar modes, and the lit one steps forward every time the ball hits a **pop bumper**, skipping anything already played. Pull the autoplunger trigger and the lit mode **locks** — the red globe above the gun confirms it. Start it at the Guitar saucer behind the G Ramp.

That turns Extra Ball, one of the nine modes, from luck into arithmetic. Count the bumper hits needed to walk the lit mode round to EB, listen for them, and lock it. The mode directly above Gilby Rolls is Extra Ball, so the video mode is a useful staging post. Lock EB and drain before collecting it, and Start Guitar Feature at the plunger next ball takes it. The lit mode unlocks itself at every ball start and mode end.
The Double shot

Start certain modes **at the Guitar saucer** and the Mini-Loop lights for a few seconds. Take it and the mode inflates: Duff Rocks goes from 100M to 200M, Super Snake's hurry-up starts at 100M, Slash Solo runs to a 100M finish. Modes started from the plunger award cannot be doubled at all — the real cost of picking Start Guitar Feature at launch.
Normal play

items: **The ramps.** G spells GUNS N, R spells ROSES. 5M a shot, 10M if the opposite inlane lit it, climbing 5M a hit if you alternate without missing. All ten letters starts a 50M hurry-up that bottoms out at 30M.

**R-O-C-K.** Left drops spot R then O, right drops spot C then K, 10M a letter. All four lights a 100M hurry-up at the left orbit, paused while the ball is in the bumpers. A live ROCK countdown blocks new modes.
**Mystery.** The Mini-Loop lights the Center Scoop — two loops the first time, three the next. The pool: 25M, 50M, Super Kickback, 20x bonus, extra ball, Multiball.
**S-N-A-K-E.** A full right orbit adds a letter and spots a J-A-M lane. Completing it feeds the Rose Plunger for a four-award pick.
**Axl Combo.** Full right orbit into the Center Scoop: 5M plus a million per unlit-scoop shot that ball, capped at 30M.
**J-A-M.** The rollovers step your bonus multiplier 2x, 4x, 6x, 8x, 10x. Past 10x, each completion pays a flat 20M.

body.text: Modes worth choosing

**Matt Scoring** always runs first: a 10M jackpot at the left orbit, every switch worth 250K and adding 250K to it, and the orbit both collects and doubles the switch value. Highest ceiling in the game, especially under Coma. **Slash Solo** is a 20M-to-50M count-up collected at either orbit or the Mini-Loop. **Duff Rocks** wants ten captive-ball target hits in thirty seconds for a hundred million. **Super Snake** banks a 50M hurry-up at the G Ramp, then feeds the Rose Plunger, where Snake Pit revolutions step a multiplier through 1x, 2x and 3x — plunge hard, a fast ball circles longer.

**Coma** is the exception to every rule: the one mode that runs on top of another, which effectively converts your existing mode into a multiball. Two balls, a 10M jackpot growing 250K per bumper hit, collected at the Right Hole. **Dizzy Ball** and **Axl 3 Ball** pay more the more drops you knocked down first — 10M plus a million per downed target, climbing toward 50M on the ramps and 30M at the scoop.
Multiball

Band members are collected at the Right Hole, 10M each. At five you choose: shoot the Right Hole again for a **six-ball with 50M jackpots**, or shoot the G Ramp to the Rose Plunger and let the Snake Pit decide — the spins alternate the base value between 35M and 65M, whatever is lit when the ball drops out is what you play with, and four balls follow. The first two Multiballs let you keep members between balls; from the third onward all six must come on one ball.

Inside it, each ramp pays a jackpot once and unlights. Both ramps lights the Right Hole for **100M**, which adds a ball and relights the ramps. Do that twice and the Mini-Loop lights for a **Super Jackpot starting at 250M**, growing a million per bumper hit. Lose all but one ball without ever hitting a ramp and the G Ramp or Right Hole restarts it at base values. There is no grace period anywhere — Multiball ends the instant the second-to-last ball reaches the outhole.
Riot

The wizard bonus is a six-ball with nothing to aim at. Forty switches gives R for 40M, sixty gives I for 60M, eighty gives O for 80M, a hundred and twenty gives T for 100M, and each letter auto-plunges another ball. Then the Mini-Loop lights for the **Riot Jackpot — one billion**. Collect it and the ladder restarts, switch counts higher and letter values 20M larger, with no ceiling.
One habit to build: three shots backhand beautifully — the R Ramp, the Right Hole and the Guitar saucer. The R Ramp returns to the right inlane, so one backhand sets up the next indefinitely.

name: The Hobbit
description: How to read The Hobbit's widebody layout, qualify and start its 31 modes, run both multiballs, climb the Mystery ladder and light an Arkenstone wizard mode.

body.text: The Hobbit is a widebody with a lot running at once: 31 modes, two multiballs, a thirteen-dwarf collection, a spinner-fed journey across a map, a four-step Mystery ladder and a third cabinet button called the Ring. There is no instant info screen — the backbox LCD shows everything in quadrants, and learning to read it is most of learning the game. The shot map underneath is simpler than that sounds: two crossing ramps, two outside loops with spinners, three drop banks, two kicker holes and a captive ball.
The layout

items: **Left ramp** — utility. Qualifies Gandalf modes, pages the book, buys mode time, lights the Spider.
**Right ramp** — business. Qualifies five Bilbo modes, starts modes, takes Smaug locks, lights the Warg.
**Left and right loops** — spinners worth 11 points a spin, both feeding the road to Erebor.
**ELF, DWARF and MAN banks** — lower left, upper left, lower right. Each qualifies its own mode family and hides dwarf targets behind it.
**Kicker holes** — the right qualifies Radagast modes; the left is walled off by the DWARF bank.
**Captive ball** — between the ramps; where Super Spinners is cashed.
**Bag End** — pop bumpers upper right that start Super Jets.

body.text: Modes: qualify, page, start

Modes come in six families, each with one qualifying shot. Left ramp gives a Gandalf mode, right ramp gives five Bilbo Baggins modes, the right kicker hole gives four Radagast modes, and the ELF, DWARF and MAN banks give three each. Qualified modes queue in the book. Page through them with the left ramp when BOOK is lit, then start the one you want with the right ramp when MODE is lit — and choosing matters, because a one-shot hurry-up sits in the same queue as a frenzy you could stack into a multiball.

Most modes run 30 seconds, and the left ramp is also your clock: TIME lit blue adds ten seconds and turns purple, and purple is worth only three. Mode progress flips it back to blue, so the pattern is score, ramp, score, ramp — not two ramps in a row.
Smaug and Beast Frenzy

Smaug Multiball uses the four L-O-C-K rollovers across the middle of the playfield. Complete them and the right ramp lights for a lock; Smaug takes the ball and returns it from the left kicker hole. The first multiball is generous — one completion arms all three locks. The second makes you complete the rollovers once per lock. From the third on you must complete them and collect the lock before a new set will start.

Beast Frenzy runs off the four inlanes, marked Warg, Orc, Goblin and Spider from left to right. Each beast is a pop-up target woken by its own shot: right ramp for Warg, right loop for Orc, left loop for Goblin, left ramp for Spider. Roll a lit inlane and the target rises for a few seconds — hit it before it drops. All four down starts a two-ball multiball. For your first Beast Frenzy an inlane roll alone lights one; after that only the shots work, though the Light Beasts mystery award will do it for you.
The two multiballs stack, and stacking adds a ball. Beast progress counts during Smaug, and Smaug locks can be lit and cashed during Beast Frenzy — so arm one and hold it while you build the other.
The long games: dwarves and Erebor

Thirteen dwarves sit on thirteen shots — three behind ELF, three behind the A, R and F drops in DWARF, three behind MAN, one on each spinner, one in the left kicker hole and Thorin on the captive ball. Collecting all of them starts Feast Frenzy, where the drop targets themselves score for a short window, then the set resets. Separately, every spinner rip advances a map from the Shire to the Lonely Mountain. Reach it and Super Spinners runs 60 seconds, building a jackpot only the captive ball will cash — and cashing ends the mode, so time it.
The Mystery ladder and the Ring

items: Crossing one left inlane and one right inlane advances the ladder a level.
**Level 1** lights the Mystery target — awards include Advance Erebor, Super Jets, Light Kickback, Light Beasts, a spotted dwarf and an extra tilt warning.
**Level 2** lights the captive ball blue for a free dwarf.
**Level 3** lights Load Arrow at the left outlane: stop a swinging power meter with the Ring and fire the kickback at the MAN targets.
**Level 4** lights Precioussss at the right outlane — stop a moving line inside a blue window and a drain gives your ball back.

body.text: The Ring charges from switch hits and then does whatever the game needs: fire the kickback, take a free swing at a beast mid-hurry-up, postpone a lock or a mode start, or just pay points. Postponing is what stops locks and mode starts fighting over the same ramp.
What to aim for

An Arkenstone mode lights only once you have completed a mode, started both multiballs, run Super Spinners and collected all thirteen dwarves. The dwarves are usually the last requirement standing, so chip at the drop banks early rather than treating them as mode fodder. The extra ball needs either every mode qualified or five barrels tipped in Super Jets, then both kicker holes hit — clear the DWARF bank before hunting the left one.

name: Johnny Mnemonic
description: A guide to Johnny Mnemonic pinball: the Data Glove and Matrix locks, tripled jackpots, Yakuza Strike, all five modes, Throwing Spears and the Power Down wizard mode.

body.text: Johnny Mnemonic is a narrow-body four-ball game built around one idea nobody else tried: you choose where your locked balls go. The Data Glove is a magnetic crane you drive yourself, and the Matrix is a three-by-three grid of sensors it drops balls onto. Where you drop decides your award and your jackpot shots — the one decision that separates a good score from a great one.
The Matrix is a choice, not a lock

Shoot Crazy Bob's in normal play and it tells you where one Matrix award is hiding, then lights your first Cyberlock. Locks sit at the centre lane, the spinner lane and the right loop, and all three feed an upkicker that fires the ball to the glove. You then have about seven seconds, flipper buttons moving the crane sideways and the extra buttons moving it forward and back.

After the first lock the display cycles through most of the available awards while the lamps on the physical Matrix flash in time with it. The game is telling you which square holds which prize — but only on the playfield.
