**Glidercraft** — the toy rises and the two kicker targets beside the Pyramid pay five to twenty million a hit.
**Save Sari** — a falling countdown at the right lane. It is the one mode genuinely not worth playing; hold the ball and spend the time on a STARGATE letter.

body.text: The two wizard modes

Complete all seven Segments — Sarcophagus, Trade Quartz, Transporter, spelling STARGATE, a Hurry-Up, a combo and all seven White Pyramids — and you start Stargate Multiball, a three-ball round with every major shot lit for a twenty million jackpot at once. Sweep all seven for the Super Jackpot and they relight. You only get this once per game. Separately, playing all six modes lights the eye at the centre of the mode circle for Eye of Ra, a four-ball multiball in three stages: five Glidercraft hits, then the left lane and Trade Quartz while the Guardians raise and lower on their own, then three Pyramid shots. Each stage pays a Super Jackpot, and clearing all three with balls still alive drops you into multiball at level two.
The trick worth knowing

Three times scoring is a thirty second Transporter award that multiplies everything, super jackpots included — but its timer stops dead during any multiball. Carry it into one and you have triple scoring for the entire thing. So the correct play is to avoid collecting it until you are ready to start something big, using the left Glidercraft target to push the award order around. If it lands at the wrong moment, salvage it by starting Battle, Glidercraft or Rebellion, all of which score heavily under a multiplier.

name: Starship Troopers
description: Sega's Starship Troopers explained: killing bugs by colour, the three multiballs, Recon Levels, the mini flipper trick, and the Klendathu wizard mode.

body.text: Starship Troopers gives you a war and a scoreboard, and they pull in opposite directions. Six planets have to be cleared of bugs one at a time, but bugs can only be killed in single-ball play — so every long multiball is time spent not winning the war. Learning where those two demands meet is what separates a decent game here from a huge one.
The extra flipper

Before anything else: there is a **third flipper**, small, above and right of the standard right one, on its own button underneath the normal one. Most players ignore it for their first several games, and that is a mistake twice over. A bug standup hit with the mini flipper **counts as two kills**, roughly halving the work of clearing a planet. It is also your control flipper — it drop-catches Recon scoop kickouts and bleeds the speed off anything arriving down the right inlane. And it is the only realistic route to the Arm Nukes hole: cradle on the right flipper, hold it up, flick the mini flipper.
The bug war

Four species, four colours: **yellow Warriors, green Hoppers, blue Plasma Bugs, red Tankers**. Shoot any flashing standup of the matching colour. Displays above the flippers count what is left on the planet you are attacking, and the lit standups thin out as you work through them.

items: **Antilles** — 5 Warriors, 3 Hoppers. Warriors are 100K here.
**Zegema Beach** — 4 Warriors, 7 Hoppers.
**Dantana** — 6 Warriors, 5 Hoppers, 3 Plasma Bugs.
**Tango Urilla** — 8 Warriors, 6 Hoppers, 5 Tankers, with Tankers at 500K.
**Planet P** — 9 Warriors, 5 Plasma Bugs, 7 Tankers, and the highest values in the game.
**Klendathu** — the wizard mode, and it does not play by the same rules.

body.text: Clear a planet and the **Brain Bug** rises in front of the right ramp. Each hit is a million, and the required number of hits climbs every time — one, then two, then three. It is timed. Later on, cradling the ball and letting it escape is often the smarter play, because you unlock the next stage either way.
Advance, or nuke

With the Brain Bug gone, two shots light and stay lit until you use one: the **Recon scoop** advances you to the next planet, the **Arm Nukes hole** starts Planet Multiball. A 5M hurry-up runs alongside, collected by either. Advance whenever you can — Planet Multiball nukes every flashing planet at once, and the scaling is enormous. One planet is a 1M Nuke, a 10M Super Nuke and two balls; five planets is a 12M Nuke, a **120M Super Nuke** and four balls. Making the five Nuke shots (both loops, both ramps, the scoop) lights the Super at the Warrior, and collecting it relights everything.
The other two multiballs

**Regular Multiball** is at the Warrior — a standup that walks backwards as you hit it, revealing a sinkhole. Four hits the first time, six the second. It is a four-ball with both ramps lit for jackpots starting at 3M. Every unlit bug standup you hit raises that toward a 4M ceiling, and lighting all of them awards an extra ball, so bash the standups before you start collecting. Five jackpots lights a **15M Super Jackpot** for sixteen seconds, then the cycle repeats. If you finish without collecting a single jackpot, you get fifteen-odd seconds to get back in the sinkhole for a two-ball restart.

**Orbit Multiball** costs six loop shots and — unusually — that number never increases. The inlanes cross-light the loops for about five seconds each; three lit loops spell ONE and a magnet drops the ball in the lock, three more spell TWO and start it. A lit loop stays lit after you hit it, so three down the same side in a row is entirely legal. Both loops pay 5M throughout, and the first two loop shots each add a ball.
Recon Levels

Ramps raise your Recon Level, the scoop cashes it in, and there are six. Level one gives a 1M bounty or the **Psychic Test** video mode; level three brings Double Scoring and Multiball Ready; level four brings the Ramp Hurry-up and Nuke Chase. **Level five is where you want to be** — it almost always awards regular Multiball if you have not had one, Orbit Multiball if you have. Level six mostly pays a flat 25M, worse than either multiball, so collect at five and resist the climb. A random Recon Boost can shove you up without warning. To climb fast: right ramp, left ramp, scoop is worth three extra levels.
Klendathu

Nuke and clear all five stocked planets and Klendathu flashes. Shoot the Recon scoop and you get **unlimited balls for thirty seconds**, with every bug standup lit at once. To finish it you need nine bugs of each species and all five Nuke shots — 5M a Nuke, 10M for the Double Nuke at the scoop, and a **50M completion bonus** if you get through the whole thing. When the timer expires the mode continues with whatever is still in play, so a good ball here runs long.

Extra balls are scattered in places nothing announces. Fifteen shots to an unlit Arm Nukes hole lights one, as does fifty ramp shots, as does lighting every bug standup during regular Multiball. And playing badly enough lights one for you on ball three.

name: Surf 'N Safari
description: How Surf 'N Safari's five-by-five bonus grid drives everything: which shots advance which columns, what each row award does, the timed rounds, multiball and Double.

body.text: Surf 'N Safari is built around one thing, and once you see it the machine makes sense: a five-by-five grid of lights above the flippers. Five major shots each own a column. Filling a column starts a timed round. Filling a row switches on a feature — an outlane award, a multiball lock, an extra ball, a scoring target. Everything else serves that grid, and Rodney the crocodile tells you when a column is one light from finishing.
The five slides

items: **The Pipeline** — a saucer on the left that returns the ball through a metal pipe. Carries the Lock light and the Adv. Double light.
**The Rapids** — a ramp around the back of the playfield. Jackpots, Super Jackpots, the Special and Go For The Record all live here.
**The Boomerang** — a spinner lane that plays like a left orbit, worth 50K a spin at all times.
**The Splash** — three centre drop targets under Rodney, worth 500K for the set whenever you clear them.
**The Whirlpool** — a spiral cup fed by its own ramp, counting swirls on the way down.

body.text: The inlane rollovers are marked Advance Random Slide and give a free column advance when lit. On your first grid both are lit; after that only one is, and slingshot hits swap which. Columns also cannot be advanced during multiball or any timed round except Double, so building the grid while a round runs is wasted effort.
What each row does

items: **Bottom row** — the Exit awards on both outlanes, worth a random 5K to 5M for a drain.
**Second row** — lights the Arcade target at 100K, climbing 100K a hit to a 600K ceiling.
**Third row** — lights the Lock at the Pipeline for multiball, and it stays lit until you collect or lose the ball.
**Fourth row** — lights the Souvenirs target for an extra ball; three quick hits walk the purple lights up to it.
**Top row** — Super Score. The Arcade target starts at a million and climbs a million a hit for the rest of the ball.

body.text: The rounds

Each completed column starts its own short timed round. The Pipeline column lights the Three Million target for nine seconds at 3M a hit. The Boomerang column lifts the spinner from 50K to roughly 250K a spin, also for nine seconds, so shoot it hard — the award is per spin. The Whirlpool column lights two random slides for twelve seconds and pays an extra ball if you hit both, so reading the playfield matters more than shooting fast.

The Splash column starts **Safari**, the best round on the machine. Four animals light for nineteen seconds — the toucan on the Rapids, the elephant on the Boomerang, the monkey on the Whirlpool and the lion on the Arcade target — and taking them in any order pays 1M, 2M, 3M and then a Special. The Rapids column instead lights the Pipeline for multiball as a hurry-up starting at 5M. That one is urgent: if the hurry-up expires you lose the multiball, not just the points.
Multiball

Lock at the Pipeline and multiball begins. Lock the ball and then make the skill shot and you get three balls; every other route, Instant Multiball included, gives two. Two random slides light — drawn from Pipeline, Rapids, Boomerang, Whirlpool and Arcade, never the Splash or Souvenirs — and hitting both lights the Rapids for a 5M jackpot. Collect it and all five light; clear those and the Rapids goes up for a 30M Super Jackpot, then it repeats. When multiball ends the Rapids lights briefly to arm the Whirlpool Million, where every swirl is a full million with no cap.
Double, and the Plunge

D-O-U-B-L-E is the single most valuable thing here. Once the Pipeline column is complete, Pipeline shots briefly light Adv. Double for a letter — and after collecting one you must hit another target before the Pipeline will relight it. The Plunge saucer can also award letters or complete the word outright. Finish it and everything doubles until you lose the ball: scores, extra balls, specials, even grid advances. Letters cannot be collected during multiball or a timed round, so build the word first and then go and start something expensive.

The Plunge is lit whenever you are not in multiball or a round, and its table is deep: 5K to 5M, extra ball, special, instant multiball, a lit Souvenirs target, a catch-up score, five free Whirlpool swirls, Double letters, or Award Everything — which completes the grid but skips the bonus rounds you would have earned. Shoot it on sight.
Long-game and consolation rules

Each grid you finish puts another 5M on your end-of-ball bonus, and every light still burning on it pays 10K. From the second grid onward the Special is lit, and after odd-numbered grids Extra Special lights too — but it goes out if you lose the ball before finishing the next grid. Once the Rapids column is done, consecutive Rapids shots count toward Go For The Record; beat it for your initials and a Special at the Rapids, and in Double round the counter climbs two at a time. The game is also kind to bad players: start your last ball under about 10M and the Souvenirs target is already sitting on Extra Ball, and if you have not had multiball by then, the Plunge simply gives you one.

name: Taxi
description: A guide to Taxi: the five-passenger fare cycle, raising and collecting the jackpot, Carry Passengers, the AIRPORT ramps, multiball and the outlane special.

body.text: Taxi is a small, honest late-eighties game with one enormous scoring feature and a lot of pleasant filler around it. The feature is the jackpot. It starts at 500,000, tops out at four million, and carries over between balls, between players and even between games until somebody collects it. Nothing else on the machine scores close. Learn how to raise it and how to cash it.
The fare cycle

Five passengers, picked up in a fixed order: GORBY, PINBOT, DRAC, LOLA and SANTA. Two of them, PINBOT and GORBY, are already lit when the game starts, and collecting one lights the next. Each pickup pays a 20,000 tip and adds 20,000 to your end-of-ball bonus. Load all five and the jackpot lights.
Each name belongs to a shot, and knowing which is which stops you wasting a lit window:

items: **GORBY** — the JOYRIDE eject hole entered from above, via the right semi-orbit.
**PINBOT** — the three drop targets on the centre right. Fifteen seconds to clear the bank.
**DRAC** — the hole at the end of the U-loop on the centre left.
**LOLA** — the three centre drop targets. Only ten seconds here, so take the bank in one visit.
**SANTA** — the same JOYRIDE hole, but shot directly off the flippers from below.

body.text: Once the jackpot is collected the cycle reverses and you drop everyone off — SANTA, PINBOT, DRAC, LOLA, GORBY. Completing that relights the jackpot and lights one outlane for special. The second run through, only one passenger is lit at a time, and a second full cycle will not light the other outlane, so the special is effectively a once-per-game prize.
Raising the jackpot is a switch-hunting exercise

Spell C-A-B in the three top lanes and **Raise Jackpot** lights for ten seconds. During that window every switch on the playfield adds 2,000 to the jackpot value. That is the key insight: this is not a moment for careful aimed shots. A ball rattling around the drop banks or bouncing through the lower playfield is worth far more than one clean ramp. Feed it into the busiest part of the machine you can reach and let it stack.

Collecting is a specific shot. With all five passengers aboard, the jackpot is paid by entering the JOYRIDE hole from above, around the right semi-orbit. You have fifteen seconds once it lights, and if you miss it LOLA gets out of the cab and has to be picked up all over again to relight it.
Carry Passengers is the habit that wins games

The small target just right of the JOYRIDE hole lights for about ten seconds whenever you complete either drop bank — LOLA or PINBOT, lit for a pickup or not. Hitting it holds every passenger you are carrying into the next ball, which is the difference between finishing the fare cycle and starting from nothing every time you drain. It is reachable from both flippers but much easier as a left backhand. Repeat hits on the same ball pay 20,000, then 30,000, then 50,000, and taking it on your final ball adds a Passenger Payoff of 20,000 per passenger.
The AIRPORT ramps and the million

The inlanes cross-light the ramps: right inlane lights the left ramp, left inlane lights the right. A lit ramp scores the current airport value and advances it — 20,000, 40,000, 60,000, 80,000, then 100,000 plus the airport million, which is collected at the JOYRIDE hole with no time limit at all on default settings.

The ramps are the least forgiving shots here and a soft attempt rolls back down at you, so if the left ramp is a problem on your machine, shoot DRAC instead — the catapult throws the ball at the right ramp and advances the airport value for you. Watch one interaction: if DRAC is lit for a pickup, the airport award times out before the eject fires.
Multiball, and what it is actually good for

Lock a ball in the right lock hole and shoot the left ramp with a subsequent ball. The lock carries between players, which means you can quite legally start multiball on a ball somebody else locked. Once it runs, relock both balls in the Express lanes in order — the lock hole first, DRAC second. The second lock pays 300,000, both balls are ejected, and both ramps light for a 100,000 Airport Ride.
It is easy to start and hard to milk, because those ramps punish anything less than a clean shot. The genuinely useful thing to do with two balls in play is take the PINBOT and LOLA banks.
Extra balls and the bonus

There are two routes. JOYRIDE can award one outright, on the spot. The other is three C-A-B completions inside a single ball, and that one must be collected at DRAC before you drain — it does not carry over, so go and get it the moment it lights. Beyond 5x the C-A-B lanes stop advancing the multiplier and pay a flat 50,000 CAB Bonus instead. The end-of-ball bonus itself caps at 99,000 before multiplying, plus 20,000 per passenger, for a theoretical maximum of 595,000. Be aware of one mean detail: passengers from a completed earlier sequence do not count. Pick up all five, collect the jackpot, drop off SANTA and drain, and the machine credits you with one passenger, not six.

name: Tee'd Off
description: A player's guide to Gottlieb's Tee'd Off: playing the nine holes in order, the five volcano modes, holes in one, and the lightning storm multiballs where the real points live.

body.text: Tee'd Off is a round of golf with a gopher problem. The whole game is built on playing nine holes in strict numerical order, and what you get for finishing them changes each time round. It is a Gottlieb, which means catch-all flippers that hold nearly anything, and that turns out to be the single most important thing about it — every enormous score on this machine comes from trapping balls and looping one shot over and over.
The layout

items: **Volcano** — a plastic volcano with a vertical kicker underneath it. Covers holes one, six and nine, and is your mode start once its insert is lit.
**Mean Hole** — a saucer in a walled pocket right of the volcano. Mystery when lit, and where Anything Goes and Quickpick are offered.
**Right ramp** — wraps behind the captive ball and hands off to the top flipper. Covers holes two, four and eight.
**Saucer** — a plain Gottlieb hole over on the left. Covers holes three, five and seven.
**Centre lane** — reached through a gap in four coconut drop targets. A hole in one with all coconuts standing, a Gopher wheel spin with any of them down.
**Gopher wheel** — twelve lettered pockets set in a roulette wheel that sits recessed into the wood at the bottom of the playfield. Spelling GOPHER on it starts a multiball.
**Captive ball** — top right. Each hit builds the end-of-ball bonus and pushes the multiball jackpot up.
**Slice target** — spots letters in SLICE for a fifty million hurry-up, and collects a lit extra ball.
**Top flipper** — puts the volcano, the twenty million target and the feed to the Mean Hole in range, and a post beside it will hold the ball while you aim.

body.text: Playing the nine holes

Three shots cover all nine holes and each only spots the one you are currently on, so shots at the wrong feature are simply wasted. The volcano covers one, six and nine. The right ramp covers two, four and eight. The saucer covers three, five and seven. Reaching the ninth hole starts something different every time: the first completed round gives you Multiball, the second gives Raining Cats And Dogs, the third Multiball again, the fourth Anything Goes, and then the cycle begins over. That escalation is the game's real structure, and getting to the fourth round is what separates a decent game from a huge one.
Holes in one are a separate counter

Do not confuse them with the nine holes. Holes in one come from three places: the plunge skill shot, the centre lane with every coconut still standing, and the Mean Hole when lit — which the right orbit also feeds around into. Both outlanes are permanently lit for one as well, so a drain down the side at least buys you something. Seven holes in one awards an extra ball, and nine lights the Mean Hole for Quickpick, a straight choice between lighting a Special and starting a lightning storm. That coconut detail is a real trade-off: each drop target you knock down adds a million to your bonus but converts the centre lane from a hole in one into a wheel spin. Decide which you are chasing before you start swinging.
The five modes

items: **Skins Game** — spell SKINS at the volcano, then take ten million or gamble it on a random shot in twenty seconds. Lose and your score goes to zero, but Recover Score lights at the Dogleg for the rest of the ball.
**Find The Gopher** — fifteen seconds to shoot any hole. Thirty million if he is in it, insults if he is not.
**Extra Ball** — the slice target lights for fifteen seconds. Trap first, then shoot; do not swing at a live ball.
**Tee'd Off** — repeat the centre lane for a value starting at five million and climbing.
**Pitch And Putt** — ten million per Mean Hole shot for fifteen seconds, with the lane post available to hold the ball for you.
Modes start at a lit volcano. First time round the volcano relights itself; after that the right ramp does. All five lights the big score target and ends modes for that ball.

body.text: Where the points actually are

Plain Multiball is two balls unless you launch the second one straight into the Mean Hole for a third. Jackpots run around five million and the captive ball pushes them up, so bang the captive ball a few times before you start cashing. Clear down to the last remaining jackpot and taking it pays three hundred million and relights the lot. The storm modes are better still. Raining Cats And Dogs strobes every jackpot shot and the centre lane at twenty five million each into a running total, and Anything Goes doubles that to fifty million. Both pay at the end of the ball, which means a tilt throws away everything you built.
The loop that runs up the score

Start any multiball other than the plain one, trap two balls on the right flipper, and loop the centre lane with the third. The catch-all flippers hold what comes back from the volcano and the centre lane reliably enough that this becomes a rhythm rather than a gamble, and at fifty million a shot in Anything Goes it is where the billion-point games come from. Two rules go with it: build the captive ball value before you cash jackpots, and never nudge hard while a storm total is unpaid.

name: Wheel of Fortune
description: How to score on Stern's Wheel of Fortune: the Toss-Up skill shot, steering the flashing contestant, the three inline drops, Bonus Wheel modes and both multiballs.

body.text: Wheel of Fortune looks like a licence game and plays like a puzzle box. The flippers sit where you do not expect them, the outlanes can hand a ball back, and draining between the flippers is sometimes the best thing that happens to you. Underneath it all sits one idea: **points go wherever the Wheel is pointing when you collect them**, so the skill is deciding when to collect.
Start with the Toss-Up

Every ball opens with a skill shot. Plunge firmly but not fully and the ball rides the Toss-Up loop for a million, plus another million for every skill shot you have already banked this game. Then shoot the scoop straight away — it starts a hurry-up at **double** whatever the skill shot just paid. Outside the skill shot the same loop switch is worth a million, climbing 250K a hit to a two and a half million ceiling, so a plunge you have dialled in keeps paying all game.
The Wheel, the contestants, the puzzle

Three bobbleheads sit in front of the Wheel — Lonnie in red, Maria in yellow, Keith in blue — and each has a matching arrow on top of it. Hit a contestant and they guess a consonant, worth whatever their arrow is currently sitting on. The values are randomised every game, and two wedges actively hurt: **Bankrupt wipes that contestant's points and prizes**, and Lose A Turn benches them until the next spin. The center ramp respins the whole set, which makes it the most important non-scoring shot on the playfield.

One contestant always flashes rather than sitting solid, and everything bankable goes to that one. Hitting a solidly lit contestant makes them the flashing one instead. This matters because **only the flashing contestant's prize bank pays out when you solve the puzzle** — so an Extra Ball sitting in Keith's bank is worthless if Maria was flashing when you finished.
Vowels and prize banks

items: Once enough consonants are down, the scoop lights to buy a vowel. Each one costs the flashing contestant **25K off their bank**, so buy after a good respin, not before.
Clearing every consonant is a one million bonus; clearing every vowel is two million.
Three prizes can drop into a bank from the Wheel or a Wild Card: Extra Ball, Special and Trip.
Each solved puzzle also adds 50K to your end-of-ball bonus.

body.text: The three inline drops are three separate features

Guarding the right ramp is a bank of three inline drop targets, and each one is worth knowing on its own. The front target lights **Free Spin** at the outlane rollovers — a drain down a lit one relaunches the ball immediately, two light per hit, and unused ones carry to your next ball. The middle target lights **Big Money** at the two lanes between the flippers, where draining spins the Wheel for whatever it lands on with a multiplier growing five at a time. The back target lights the **Wild Card** lane on the far left, which pays a random award plus the value the pop bumpers have been quietly stacking, up to 500K.
Bonus Wheel modes

Every major shot — left ramp, center ramp, right ramp, left loop, right orbit — carries a BONUS letter. Spell all five and the scoop lights with the Bonus Wheel inserts chasing like a spinning wheel; shooting the scoop stops them, and you get whichever of the seven modes they land on. You cannot time it. All seven run about thirty seconds, only one runs at a time, and none of them can be started during a multiball — but starting one **just before** a multiball stacks them together.

items: **Ramp Rampage** is the cleanest: each ramp scores ten times its matching wedge, and every repeat on the same ramp adds another ten to that ramp's multiplier.
**Risky Spinning** lights all five BONUS shots for the sum of the lit wedges — hitting an unlit contestant adds their value, hitting a lit one takes it away.
**Contestant Hurry-Up** starts at ten times a contestant's wedge and adds five more for every hurry-up you finish.
**Wheel Frenzy**, **Combos**, **Keep It Spinning** and **Stop The Wheel** round out the set, and the center ramp respins values inside any of them.

body.text: Two very different multiballs

Wheel of Fortune Multiball comes from the nine MULTIBALL standups and starts at the scoop: three balls, four jackpots from 750K, then Double, Triple and a five-times Super. Extra target hits before you start add 7.5K to the base, as does every revolution of the Wheel. The requirement hardens each time — the first run spots a letter off any target, the second needs every letter hit once, the third needs each hit twice.

Trip Multiball is the one that rewards planning. Bank a Trip on a contestant, make sure they are flashing, then solve. Four shots light from 500K and the base climbs 100K every wave you clear. Take one jackpot immediately after another and the next is doubled.
Habits worth building

items: Either outer ramp doubles your next shot; both ramps in sequence quadruples it. Spend that on a jackpot, never on a standup.
Every fourth left loop shot pays a Hold award, and the loop count carries between balls.
The right orbit steps the pop bumper multiplier to five times, which grows the Wild Card value too.
Ten ramp shots light the extra ball outright.

name: Who Dunnit
description: How to play Who Dunnit: reading the eleven elevator floors, collecting clues and equipment, working the slots and roulette, and catching the killer for the four-ball multiball.

body.text: Who Dunnit is a four-ball game with a 1930s detective theme and one of the most unusual central mechanisms Bally ever shipped: an elevator. A wide ramp feeds three habitrails marked UP, EXIT and DOWN, and which one takes your ball decides which of eleven floors you get off at. Floors are how modes start. Once the elevator stops being a shot you take hopefully and becomes one you take on purpose, the machine opens up.
The floors
You cannot play this well without knowing what sits behind each floor, and the machine never tells you.

items: **Basement** — a three-ball multiball.
**Main Floor** — lights Slots and Roulette.
**2nd** — spots all four TAXI letters, which is a free clue, and lights the phone.
**3rd and 5th** — collect evidence for 25M, or name your killer.
**4th** — spins the slot machine.
**6th** — hands you the leftmost piece of equipment you are missing.
**7th** — starts Elevator Madness. The display will tell you it is the 8th floor. It is lying.
**8th** — interrogate a suspect, or name your killer.
**Penthouse** — Penthouse Party, locked until you hold the Penthouse Key.
**Roof** — Catch the Killer, open once you have visited every other floor.

body.text: A three-target bank sits in front of the elevator and sinks into the playfield. Down, the elevator is wide open. Up, you are threading a very narrow gap — and during several modes the bank cycles up and down on its own, so wait for it to drop rather than firing into a raised target.
Cases, clues and the phone

Every case follows the same shape: collect evidence, interrogate suspects, name a killer, and if you named the right one, catch them. Five cases cycle, and the case names have no bearing on what you actually do. Clues come from spelling T-A-X-I, from the super skill shot, and from three fingerprints on the slots. Each clue lights the telephone.

Answering the phone puts a question to one of the suspects, and the whole mystery hangs on a single tell: **a suspect always talks about the killer, unless they are the killer**. Anyone deflecting is worth a hard look. Carrying the Magnifying Glass eliminates a suspect outright when the phone has nothing else to give you.

Here is the counter-intuitive strategy, though. Naming the killer correctly closes the case and **resets your clue count to zero** — and five clues inside one case lights an extra ball. If you are three clues deep and already know the answer, stall. Keep spelling TAXI, keep the multiplier climbing, and cash the case when the extra ball is banked.
Equipment, the sewer and the slots

Four pieces of equipment each turn a dead shot into a live one, and they chain. Two consecutive train ramp shots hand you the **Flashlight**; with the Flashlight but no Map, an unlit sewer gives you the **Map**; with both, the sewer becomes a rotating award of a multiplier, an interrogation, evidence, a lit WhoDunnit or 50M. Without either, the same hole pays a million times the number of visits you have made. The **Revolver** raises multiball jackpots five million at a time in the bumpers instead of one.

The slot machine has eight results and some very large ones: three bars is 100M, three question marks starts Elevator Madness, three wilds sends you to the Roof. Every reel carries a wild, and the middle one lets you pick between the two outer results. Two matching reels gives a Second Chance redeemable by completing any spin shot — the phone, roulette, the sewer, or an elevator exit.

That Second Chance is also this machine's hidden safety net. There is no physical kickback here, but with an outlane lit for Slots, draining spins the reels on the way out — and a two-of-three match hands you an autolaunched ball.
Roulette, Taxi Chase and the ramp

Roulette raises your bonus multiplier whether you bet or not, which is the real reason to shoot it. Set red or black with the standup targets first — hit both and you have cancelled your own choice — and let the spinner rip on the way in, because how much it spins decides the size of the stake offered.

Rolling a lit inlane starts Taxi Chase, which raises the train ramp and lights both orbits. Each orbit shot extends the timer and spots a TAXI letter, which makes it the fastest clue engine in the game. With the ramp down instead, consecutive train shots pay a ladder: the first lights Roulette, the second gives the Flashlight, the third lights an extra ball, and the fourth starts a chase against the machine's own loop record.
Catch the killer

Complete the lit Taxi Chase and then the phone. A hurry-up starts at 100M and falls to 25M, and whatever value you catch them at becomes the value of **every lit shot in the four-ball multiball that follows**. Shoot the phone fast. Penthouse Party is the other big earner: escalating 10M steps at every flashing shot until the timer runs out, and a clean run is worth roughly three quarters of a billion. There is no wizard mode beyond these — the end-of-ball bonus is where a long game gets paid, and it can pass a billion on its own.

name: World Challenge Soccer
description: A guide to World Challenge Soccer: the two plunger skill shots, raising the goal value, soccer ball line-ups, challenge matches, the World Championship and Riot, plus tournament settings.

body.text: World Challenge Soccer is built around one number and one mechanism. The number is the goal value, and the mechanism is a goal unit that stays shut unless you have earned the right to shoot it. Everything else on the playfield exists to feed those two things. Get that relationship straight and the machine stops feeling random.
Two plunges, two different games

The plunger offers a genuine choice. Fire it hard and the ball runs the top rollover, worth three goals and one open shot at the goal. Feather it and the ball settles in the top hole, paying whichever award is lit — Mystery, Advance Goal Value, or Hit All Targets. **The flipper buttons select which drop-target award is lit, and only while the ball is still in the shooter lane.** Set it before you pull, because there is no changing your mind afterwards.
Goal value first, goals second

Every goal you score pays the current goal value, and that value resets to one million at the start of every ball. The ladder runs 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10 and 25 million, advanced by hitting whichever left or centre target is lit, or by taking Advance Goal Value from the plunge. The difference this makes is not subtle: the ten-goal jackpot at the bottom of the ladder is twenty million, and the same jackpot at the top is two hundred and fifty. Raise the value before you go looking for goals.

Goals themselves accumulate all game to a maximum of ninety-nine. Twenty of them lights an extra ball, fifty qualifies the mystery award for Super Riot, and beating the machine's all-time goal count awards a Special.
Lining up the soccer balls

Three columns of lamps sit in the centre of the playfield, each advanced by something different. The left kicking rubber, a scored goal, or a lit hit on the goal unit moves the left column. The right kicking rubber or a lit right ramp moves the right. Only the lit centre target moves the middle. Get all three onto one row and you are paid for it: the white row switches on Superscore, worth ten, twenty, then forty million and remembered between balls, while the top purple row qualifies a Hurry-up Extra Ball at the left side rollover for about twenty seconds. Advancing any lamp afterwards breaks the alignment and kills Superscore.
Ways into the goal

items: **The Boo:** press both flipper buttons together and the goal opens for one shot. One per ball, so save it for something worth having — usually an extra ball.

**The penalty kick:** hitting the goal unit or scoring resets a hidden rollover drop target and sets the upper flipper lane flashing. Take that target while it flashes and the goal opens for one shot.
**The velocity plunge:** the top rollover opens the goal as well as paying three goals outright.

**Drop targets:** clearing the bank collects whichever of five award lamps is lit — Extra Ball Round, Multi, Special Round, Ball, Points Round — and once all five are gone the bank awards Light Challenge instead.

body.text: Three words at once

The machine is spelling three words simultaneously. WORLD awards the Center Target Round, ten million a hit on the centre target. CHALLENGE lights the two lower holes for a challenge match. SOCCER awards Players Choice, which offers eight goals or a multiball — take goals when your goal value is high. Each completed letter is worth a million in outhole bonus, and finishing all three words pushes that bonus to a hundred million, which is often reason enough to change what you were shooting at.
Matches, the Championship and Riot

A challenge match is a short round with one objective: score a goal. Win and you advance; lose and the holes go dark and must be requalified. There is no safe stall — trapping the ball and letting the clock run out is a loss, not a draw. Five wins qualifies both holes for the World Championship, a three-ball multiball where three goals wins it. That third goal pays fifty million, ends the round and rolls straight into Riot, where every shot is worth thirty million for as long as your multiball survives. Draining right after winning throws away the best scoring on the machine.
Multiball and jackpots

Multi and Ball from the drop targets light the holes for multiball — three balls, or two if you had one parked in the top hole. Take the rollover on the multiball plunge if you can, because it spots every target and qualifies both jackpots at once. The goal jackpot pays ten goals, then twenty, then thirty, all within the same multiball. The ramp jackpot pays thirty million, then a hundred, then an unlimited three hundred. Collecting either resets the drops, and the two ladders do not step each other.
In competition

Tournament settings strip most of the randomness out. Challenge match progress no longer carries between balls, so reaching the Championship means winning two matches on a single ball. The bottom three soccer lamps start aligned each ball, which puts Superscore on from the start and makes the extra ball harder because the centre target now needs at least five hits. Mystery pays a token award unless you are past fifty goals or on your last ball without a multiball, and the left rollover no longer qualifies the penalty kick.

name: World Poker Tour
description: A guide to World Poker Tour: building hold 'em hands and the main pot, all four multiballs, the six Poker Corner modes, chip trick combos, and the three wizard modes.

body.text: World Poker Tour hides a deep ruleset behind a layout that looks simple. Six red-arrow shots run across the lower playfield, sixteen drop targets sit in three banks, and a full second deck floats above it all. Understand this before anything else: the game runs two economies at once — the poker hand you build with the ramps, and the pot you build with the spinners — and your payout is one multiplied by the other.
The layout

Left to right: left orbit, left ramp, the VUK, the scoop, right ramp, right orbit. Each orbit carries a spinner. The VUK is the longest shot on the machine, firing the ball off the back of the playfield and up onto the mini-playfield, where a second pair of flippers takes over. Up there sit the Ace in the Hole jail and its captive ball, three white standups, a re-light target on the far left, and an exit slot that drops you into the pop bumpers.
Hands and the pot

Either ramp advances your hold 'em hand through Flop, Turn and River. Completing a hand pays the main pot multiplied by the strength of the hand you were dealt, and that multiplier is the whole ballgame — a high card halves the pot, a royal flush pays it nine times over. In tournament play hands arrive in ascending strength, starting with a pair.

The pot opens at 250,000 and grows 25,000 for every hand you finish. Spinner rotations add 5,000 apiece, and that per-spin figure grows by 500 per completed hand. **Build the pot before you close a strong hand, never after.** When it climbs past the All In figure — 750,000 the first time, 250,000 higher after each one — All In Multiball starts by itself and hands you a free completed hand plus the pot's base value.
The four multiballs

items: **Ace in the Hole:** knock the jail bars open, then hit the captive ball three times. Both balls start on the mini-playfield, and re-locking one immediately pays a million and adds a third ball. Jackpots open at 200,000 and rise to 500,000, and every three reopens the jail. Deep in, each captive ball hit is a 1.5 million super jackpot.
**All In:** starts itself when the pot is fat enough. Every main shot except the orbits is a jackpot from 150,000 up; use the orbits for side pots instead.

**No Limit:** three hits on the left standup lights all three locks the first time, stackable at the VUK or scoop. The left ramp is a one million jackpot, relit by a cleared drop bank — centre at 1X, right at 2X, the eight-target left bank at 3X.
**Poker Hands:** light every hand on the insert ladder for a four-ball mini wizard mode. Jackpots start at a million, spinners raise them, and the ninth lights a five million super.

body.text: Poker Corner

Every completed hand lights one mode at the scoop, and the relights do not stack — skip a mode and you have burned a hand. Each runs thirty seconds with one goal worth a Trophy, and each Trophy is a million points and raises the Poker Wizard payout later. Learn the goals ahead of time: two Big Blinds, three button shots, sixteen drops, twenty drops, two tells, or eight shots across both decks. In competition the two drop target modes are better ignored than fought, and Change Gears is worth holding until you have a multiball ready.
Chip tricks and triple scoring

Chip tricks are the combo system, and they live on every major shot except the VUK. The left orbit and right inlane flash the left-side tricks; the right orbit and left inlane flash the right-side ones. Chaining flashing shots pays double and triple the base, and your fifth spotted trick starts Super Trick — a rolling ten-second window worth roughly 200,000, then 300,000, then 400,000. Clear every flashing trick during it and an extra ball lights, but it will not carry to your next ball. Separately, completing a poker hand off the drops lights triple scoring on an inlane for three seconds — and it counts as triple progress toward super jackpots, not just triple points.
The wizard ladder

Three modes sit at the top. Poker Wizard opens at the scoop once you have played all six Poker Corner modes, and pays by Trophies earned — 1.6 million a jackpot with two, up to 3.1 million with four. Winning your sixth tournament starts the WPT World Championship, a ramp grind for ten million that pays another ten on completion. Above that is the Keefer Invitational: the Championship plus twenty-five million banked in each of six categories, then one more mystery award to open the door.
A working game plan

items: Rip the orbits early — a pot built before your first strong hand is worth several times the same hand on an empty pot.
Take the scoop whenever Poker Corner is lit. An unplayed mode light is a wasted hold 'em hand.
Stack deliberately: start a mode, then a multiball on top of it. Modes cannot begin during multiball, but multiballs can begin during a mode.
If the jail is open during any multiball, lock a ball in it — that briefly lights ball save and puts a fresh ball into play.
Move triple scoring to the side your next shot comes from. It turns a routine jackpot into three.

name: WWF Royal Rumble
description: A guide to Data East's WWF Royal Rumble: the mode grid, collecting nine wrestlers, the upper playfield, both carry-over jackpots and the six-ball wizard round.

body.text: WWF Royal Rumble is a widebody with no toys, which sounds like a complaint until you realise the upper playfield does all the work a toy would. The rules are unusually legible: three wrestler shots, a grid of nine modes you steer between them, and a wizard round at the end.
Three shots, nine wrestlers

The left ramp, center ramp and right orbit are the wrestler shots, three wrestlers each. Collecting all nine lights multiball, and the requirement hardens every time round. First run, any order works. Second run, you clear a whole group of three before moving on. After that it is strictly left ramp, center ramp, right orbit. Each wrestler is also a million in the bonus.

Those same three shots steer the mode grid. The nine modes sit in a three-by-three layout and **each wrestler shot owns a column** — left ramp, center ramp and right orbit, left to right. Shooting one moves the selection into its column, or up a row if you are already in it. Once a column is played out, its shot stops moving anything.
The extra ball route

Light Extra Ball is one of the nine modes and there is a reliable path to it. Shoot the center ramp until Search For Doink is selected, then take the left ramp — that moves you onto Light EB. The trap is that you now need a lit mode hole, and **another center ramp shot would move the selection away**. So go up the right lane instead, play the upper playfield, and drain from there: the ball returns to the right inlane, which relights the left mode hole.
The upper playfield is worth visiting

The right lane ends in a kicker that throws the ball upstairs to two small flippers, and there is real money up there even outside modes. The Loop is easy — hold the left flipper up and the return bounces to the right flipper for a free catch — and it pays one million, then two, three, four and five. That fifth shot also **raises the multiball jackpot base to twenty million**, and twenty-five the next time.

items: Drop into the Top Hole for a free MACHO MAN letter, and the Exit swings open with it.
Clear the upper drop bank and you take a step of bonus multiplier, and again the Exit opens.
The Exit pays 5M and drops you at the right inlane — but while it is open the Loop is unavailable.
The bonus multiplier caps at 9x; a repeat completion gives Bonus Hold, and one after that lights an extra ball.

body.text: Two jackpots that carry between games

**Get Back In The Ring** lives at the Left Lane. Rolling down it unlit starts a fifteen-second window; shooting back up the lane inside it pays a jackpot that persists across players and games, ranging from around eleven million to nearly a hundred. Balls leaving the bumpers often roll down that lane and arm it for you.

**RIP** works off the D-E-A-D drop targets. Each full clear in single-ball, non-mode play spots a letter, and spelling it pays another carry-over jackpot starting north of eleven million. Letters are tracked per player.
The modes

items: **Pandemonium** is a frenzy where target value scales with balls in play: 250K at one ball up to 2M at six. The Top Hole adds a ball. Once the timer dies you cannot add more, but the value never drops back.

**Championship Belt Round** is three belts, each won by clearing the upper drops. Each opens at 20M and loses a million a second, and the clock resets to twenty when you get upstairs — so speed is the score.
**Raise The Undertaker** pays 2M, then 3M and upward to a 10M ceiling on the D-E-A-D targets, which reset after every hit.
**Banzai** is the left ramp four times for 5, 10, 15 and 20 million — or twenty and forty with the 2x Banzai skill shot.
**Macho Madness** needs MACHO MAN spelled, then three completions of the upper drops for 15M each and a 20M Loop hurry-up.
**Search For Doink**, **Sleeper Hold Super Pops**, **Tag Team Millions** and the **No Holds Brawl** video round complete the nine.

body.text: Multiball

Nine wrestlers lights it; the left ramp, right lane, Loop or Top Hole starts it. One wrestler shot at a time is lit for a jackpot from fifteen million, climbing five each time you collect one or clear the upper drops. Let a jackpot timer expire and the game **launches another ball** rather than punishing you. Collect all nine and the Super lights at the Top Hole from a hundred million, growing while balls keep moving and shrinking if you hold the flippers.

The left ramp is hard enough with one ball, so a common approach is to let one go and hold the other two, one per flipper, for clean shots. And if you lose two balls without collecting a jackpot, any start shot inside fifteen seconds gives you a two-ball restart.
Royal Rumble

Play all nine modes and both start holes flash. Hit either, then all three wrestler shots, and six balls come out. You eliminate wrestlers with twenty bumper hits or a cleared upper drop bank, and the two counters run independently. Eliminate all nine and the wrestler shots light for 30, 40 and 50 million, climbing ten a cycle to a ninety million ceiling. No ball saver, and it ends when one ball is left.

name: X-Files
description: A player's guide to Sega's X-Files: the agent skill shot, lighting the big X for THE TRUTH, the eight episodes, and the file cabinet multiball jackpot sequence.

body.text: Sega's X-Files is a fast, bouncy machine built around one central toy: a movable three-drawer file cabinet with a magnet in front of it that flings anything you do not hit dead centre. Learn to live with that magnet and the game opens up.
The layout

Six main shots, arranged symmetrically. From either flipper you have an **inner orbit** that runs around the cabinet and feeds the opposite flipper, an **outer orbit** that feeds the pop bumpers, and a **ramp**. The ramps want a precise line — but a shot that dies halfway drops back out to the inner orbits rather than screaming down the middle, so missing is cheap. A pop-up diverter on the right decides which flipper the left ramp returns to.

Three red standups sit outside each slingshot, three pop bumpers and the **E-B-E rollover lanes** sit at the top, and a trapdoor in front of the cabinet hides the scoop where episodes begin. There is a small post between the flippers, which you will be grateful for.
The skill shot happens before you plunge

Two faces alternate on the display with a box flashing around each in turn. Press **right for Mulder, left for Scully**, timed to when the box is around that agent. Get one right and you are offered a second pick — take the *other* agent, because picking the same one twice throws the second chance away and you want both bonus types running. Be ready as soon as the ball starts; leave it too long and the game moves on without you.
Lighting the big X
The large X insert in the lower playfield takes five shots to fill, and the chain is strictly ordered:

items: The two **inner orbits** are lit first. Shoot one.
That lights the **outer orbit on the same side**. Shoot that.
That sets the **ramp X** on that side flashing.
When both ramp Xs are flashing, either ramp starts **THE TRUTH**.
Every X shot pays 50K whether it was lit or not, so nothing is wasted.

body.text: THE TRUTH is a four-ball multiball where each ramp and each orbit pays a jackpot with a 200K base, then three file cabinet hits arm the Super Jackpot and a fourth collects it — while the cabinet rides up and down, so the shot needs timing as well as aim. **The trick worth knowing:** during THE TRUTH the magnet stays permanently energised. Anything short of a hard centre shot gets grabbed and held, so with a ball or two parked on it you effectively get a calm two-ball game to clear the shots. If you drain everything else, the magnet lets go after a few seconds and the mode carries on.
Episodes

Right ramp shots spell F-B-I (already spotted at the start of a game). Complete it, the trapdoor drops open, and the scoop underneath starts one of eight episodes for 100K plus whatever you score. Nothing on the playfield tracks which you have played, so keep count yourself:

items: **Four-shot rounds** — Colony, Smoking Man and Talitha Cumi each pay **1.4M** for a completion, with values stepping 250K, 300K, 350K, 400K. The most reliable points in the game.

**Syzygy** — the one to milk. Alternate left ramp and trapdoor for 100K, 200K, 300K, 400K and upward with no ceiling, and every made shot adds a ball, up to four. It ends the moment you are back to one ball.
**Countdown rounds** — Herenvolk and Terma open at 420K and fall hard. Miss the opening collect and the episode simply ends.
**Ramp rounds** — Hambug (30 seconds) and The Host (20 seconds) just want repeated flashing ramps.

body.text: Multiball, and the order that matters

Hit the file cabinet enough times — five by default — and it sinks two drawers, exposing the top one. Shoot that drawer for a three-ball multiball. The magnet frequently throws rejected balls straight back into the cabinet, so you get free progress; a green light on top means it is ready. Each later multiball costs one more cabinet hit than the last.

The jackpot sequence runs on rails: **left ramp, left ramp, right ramp, cabinet**. The diverter feeds the first jackpot right back to the same flipper for the second, then hands you to the left flipper for the double jackpot, then the cabinet pays a Super Jackpot worth at least double that. Collect it and the whole cycle repeats.

Raise the base before you start, not during. Sweeping a red target bank adds 50K to the jackpot, cabinet hits during multiball add 25K each, and bumper hits nudge it up as well. And remember the safety net: if you fall to one ball without collecting a single jackpot, you get about fifteen seconds to shoot the cabinet and restart multiball — once per multiball only, and it disappears the moment you collect anything.
Small things worth doing

The inner orbits feed flipper to flipper, so chaining them collects a **mini-loop award** — 250K, then 500K, with the required count rising each time. The E-B-E lanes step your bonus to 2x, 3x, 4x, 6x and 8x with lane change, but there is no bonus hold, so it resets every ball. Four left ramps light the extra ball at the right ramp, which can be backhanded. Enough bumper hits triggers Super Pops at 20K a hit — they start at 1.5K and every outer orbit shot adds 500.

name: Frank Thomas' Big Hurt
description: A guide to Frank Thomas' Big Hurt: innings and the 7th Inning Stretch, glove catches, the billion-point loop, six rounds, multiball jackpots, and the sixteen-card score double.

body.text: Big Hurt is a narrow-body baseball machine with a four-ball multiball and one of the largest single awards in pinball hiding inside its trading card system. It is also a game where the correct strategy is unusually clear, which makes it worth learning deliberately rather than by feel.
Reading the playfield

A wide metal ramp dominates the centre, and where you hit it decides everything. Left of centre goes to the left gap, dead centre to the home run hole, right of centre to the right gap. Fall short and the ball drops into the warning track, a trench that spits it out to the left flipper or into the pop bumpers depending which way it rolls. A moving glove guards the top of the ramp, and the ramp's centre section raises to expose the signs behind it.

Around the outside sit a left field loop and a right field loop, a left scoop that lifts the ball onto a habitrail feeding the upper left flipper, a captive ball, a three-target drop bank, and a right hole that starts rounds. Above the pop bumpers are a Load Bases lane and the Big Hurt pothole.
The one habit that matters

**Shoot the right loop every single time it flashes.** That is the jackpot builder — ten million a shot, and the value carries between balls. Four things set it flashing: shooting it, scoring a home run, a warning-track roll-out to the left, and the left inlane switch. Raising the jackpot before you reach the 7th Inning Stretch is what turns that multiball into a serious score, because the double jackpots there pay off the number you built.
Innings, catches and the loop ladder

items: **Innings:** the left gap advances one, during single-ball play outside a mode. Each inning adds a hundred million to the super jackpot, which tops out at nine hundred million after the ninth. Finishing the sixth starts the 7th Inning Stretch automatically.

**Catches:** a firm hit on the glove is a catch worth a million and re-lights Start Round; a weak one is a single worth a hundred thousand. Ten catches lights a timed extra ball at either loop, twenty pays fifty million, thirty pays a hundred million and lights the right orbit for the same. End-of-ball bonus is a million per catch.

**The left field loop:** its ladder climbs by a factor of ten each shot — 500,000, then 5 million, 50 million, 500 million, and finally one billion points. Each hit flashes the value briefly and a repeat both raises it and resets the timer.

body.text: Rounds

Rounds start at the lit right hole, and a glove catch re-lights it afterwards. Four of the six are multiball rounds. Golden Glove counts every glove hit as a catch, weak or firm, which makes it the fast route to the Catches board. Frank's HR Derby wants the home run hole. Steal Home is timed and single-ball: left scoop, then centre drop target, for twenty million, thirty, then an extra ball plus forty. All Stars is a ramp grind worth 450 million for all nine players. Frank Thomas Cards lights both orbits. Night Game moves two lit shots around the five majors, and each one completes an inning. Complete all six and World Series lights — four thirty-million shots, then a super jackpot at the home run hole.
Multiball

Regular multiball comes from Players Choice or a bullpen award, and its sequence is strict: home run for the jackpot, an orbit, then home run again inside five seconds for the double, then orbit and home run once more for the super. Miss the five-second window and another orbit simply restarts the timer and raises the ramp — the sequence is delayed, not lost. Third and fourth balls join after the first and second home runs.
Trading cards, and the sixteen

Cards come from steals, the Cards round, bullpen awards, and three at a time from a left outlane drain. At the end of the game they pay ten million each, which is a trap — trading them in at the right hole is worth far more. The trade table climbs from a flashed left field award through advancing innings, jackpots and an extra ball, and then hits the one that matters: **exactly sixteen cards doubles your entire score.** Not fifteen, not seventeen.

items: Trade ten to twelve the first time for the extra ball, then work back toward exactly sixteen.
Steals are the only source that pays one card at a time, so they are how you land on the number precisely.
Stay out of the pop bumpers when you are close — a bullpen award of three, five or ten cards will overshoot and cost you the double.
If you do overshoot, take a super jackpot trade rather than chasing thirty cards, and start climbing back to sixteen.

body.text: Small things worth knowing

Use the manual plunger before the game launches for you, and plunge softly — the ball drops into the Big Hurt pothole for a letter, then feeds the pops and comes back neatly onto the right flipper. At Players Choice, take the award that is not the GRAND SLAM letters, or the list stalls and stops offering multiballs. And every combo ends on the same pair, left scoop into centre drop, which is also how you collect walks and steals.

name: The Party Zone
description: A guide to The Party Zone: the Door Prize plunge, Way Out Of Control awards, the Payoff lane, party passes into Happy Hour, and the 10x scoring loop.

body.text: The Party Zone looks like chaos and plays like arithmetic. Under the rocket and the robot comic sits a clear structure: one lane pays a climbing million, one target bank hands out a 10x multiplier, and together they are worth more than everything else combined.
Start with the plunge

There is a Door just right of the B-O-P lanes, and plunging each new ball through it pays a Door Prize — a million the first time and another million every time after, reportedly to at least ten. It costs you nothing but plunge control and it means you have millions on the board before you have made a real shot. Do it on every ball.
The Payoff lane and Way Out Of Control

The Payoff lane sits behind the four Way Out Of Control targets on the right. When nothing is lit, it pays a million and climbs a million each time you make it, reportedly up to around ten million a shot. Clearing the Way Out Of Control targets lights one of four awards, and the Payoff lane is where you collect it.

items: **5 Million** — straightforward, and the least interesting.
**Millions Per Bop** — every bopper is worth a million for the rest of the ball.
**10x Playfield** — about ten seconds where everything except the Big Bang is multiplied tenfold.
**Special** — an extra game, and the only award swapped out if you drain before collecting it.

body.text: The important rule is that only one award can be waiting at a time. Once something is lit, further hits on those targets are wasted effort — go and collect. Then the loop that produces genuinely large scores: grind the Payoff lane to its ceiling first, light 10x playfield, and cash a maxed Payoff lane inside the multiplier. If Millions Per Bop is already running on the same ball, each bopper is worth ten million while 10x is up.
Eat, drink and be merry

The five green targets down the left side light EAT at the base of the ramp. Collect it on the ramp for a million and DRINK lights for about ten seconds; take the comic saucer through the comic entry for two million and BE MERRY lights for another ten; finish at the Captain Bizarre saucer in the middle of the playfield for three million. It is a genuine three-shot chain on a rolling clock, and the ramp doubles as Ozone Bonus and extra ball progress.
The ramp pays twice

The Ozone Bonus opens at 100,000 and climbs by 100,000 per ramp shot, capping at two million on most machines and five million on some. More usefully, ramp shots accumulate toward extra balls on a ladder that lengthens each time: six ramps for the first, then eight, eleven, fourteen and eighteen. Alternating ramp and comic saucer shots is a well-worn route, since the Ha-Ha-Ha targets that relight the comic sit on the way to his saucer.
The comic, and what he is worth

The comic starts every ball lit and goes dark once you use him. What his saucer pays depends entirely on two lights. With DRINK running it is two million, plus a Comic Award between 100,000 and 900,000 if he is lit as well. With the comic lit and no DRINK, you get one of three things: 2x on your bonus multiplier, a Laff Attack frenzy where every target is worth 100,000 for about twenty seconds, or a surprise two-ball multiball. With nothing lit at all it starts at a miserly 10,000 — which is the machine telling you to hit the Ha-Ha-Ha targets first.
Passes, Happy Hour and the Big Bang

Party passes come from the Captain. Light both Request targets, take the Captain Bizarre saucer, and you get a request — 250,000, the music selection, and a pass. Turn up at the Cosmic Cottage without one and the bouncer sends you away. With a pass flashing, run the Cottage and finish in the comic saucer for Party Animals, then Party Monsters, then Party Dudez, which brings the two-ball Happy Hour with it.

Happy Hour runs on rocket fuel. It opens with five million of it, or only one million if you have already collected a Big Bang. The comic saucer and the Back-2-Bop lane each add a million of fuel; the ramp cashes whatever the current value is, between one and seven million. Bank enough and the next ramp shot pays ten million and locks the first ball, leaving you to send the second one up the ramp for the Big Bang itself — worth anywhere from ten million to just under a hundred, depending on how long it has been since the last one. Collecting it drops the playfield into a frenzy at 250,000 a target until you lose a ball. Note that 10x playfield does not multiply the Big Bang, so save the multiplier for the frenzy that follows.
One for the patient

Leave the Captain alone long enough and he starts playing his own favourites. Make a request while that is happening and you collect the Party Saver: five million, and five million more every time you catch it again. There is no light for it — the only cue is the music changing — so have both Request targets already lit and listen. Some ROM revisions do not run it at all.

name: The Champion Pub
description: A guide to The Champion Pub: filling life bars, winning fights, landing a knockout, all five multiballs, building the purse, and putting every jewel on the belt.

body.text: The Champion Pub is a checklist game wearing a boxing game's clothes. Five jewels go on a championship belt, each worth 500,000, and collecting all five is the only route to the Ultimate Challenge. Everything else — the rope, the bag, the video modes, the multiballs — feeds one of those five. Play it as a fighting game and you will score badly.
The five jewels

items: **Training:** six cumulative jump rope jumps, six cumulative speed bag hits, and roughly ten heavy bag hits that counted toward a life bar. The game forces you to rotate — once you satisfy one discipline it locks out until you have done the other two.
**Multiballs:** play all three of Multi-Brawl, Fisticuffs and Raid. Each is earned a completely different way, and Raid only exists as a reward for winning your third fight.
**Knockout:** land one K.O. during a fight.
**Jackpots:** work all fifteen jackpot levels, from 100,000 up to 1.5 million.
**Pub Champion:** win five fights. The fifth win starts Champion Multiball.

body.text: Fighting, properly

You start with three of twelve life bars already banked. Heavy bag hits fill the meter, the corner saucer usually adds half a bar, and during a fight the left ramp and the beer targets add one or two more. When the meter is full, the corner or either orbit starts the match. Body shots pay 100,000 and take one or two bars off your opponent; head shots up the green hook ramps pay 500,000 and take three to six. A Smart Punch on the launch button counts as a head shot. The red post between the flippers drops partway through, and after that an outlane or centre drain costs you the fight as well as the ball — a tilt is an automatic loss.
The knockout is a two-part shot

This is the jewel most players never collect. Run jab combos through the scoops on both sides — one each, so a jab on the left owes you one on the right — and a K.O. light comes on for about five seconds. Land a head shot inside that window and the fight is over, worth a million bonus on top of the purse. The first knockout of a game needs one combo per side; the second needs three, the third four. A Smart Punch will close it out for you if the ball is somewhere unhelpful.
Build the purse before you commit

The purse is what a fight actually pays, and it is the biggest scoring decision on the machine. The corner raises it, the left ramp and beer targets raise it mid-fight, ten consecutive jumps or speed bag hits double it, and a Pair in Poker Night doubles it too. The ceiling is 60 million, reachable in one hit only through an extremely rare Straight Flush. Walking into a fight with a starved purse wastes the match, and rematches get harder each time.
Multiballs, and stacking them

Multi-Brawl is the standard lock-three. The first one is cheap at three left orbits; every one after needs the beer targets completed to light each lock, and from the third onward each target needs two hits. Fisticuffs accumulates from heavy bag hits in the background. Raid comes free with your third fight win. This game deliberately lets them run together — a stack gives you four balls and a fresh ball saver, and there is roughly a one-second grace period to sneak the last one in when everything drains but a single ball. Champion Multiball folds all three together and pays a million per major shot.
What each win unlocks

items: First win lights Spittin' Gallery, the catching video mode worth up to 10 million with an extra ball sometimes hidden in it.
Second win lights the extra ball.
Third win starts Raid Multiball on the spot — every switch climbs in 1,000-point steps toward a 50,000 ceiling.
Fourth win starts Contender Challenge, a hurry-up over every major shot falling from a million toward 25,000 and resetting on each shot made.
Fifth win makes you Pub Champion and starts the four-ball Champion Multiball.

body.text: Things the playfield does not tell you

Hold the launch button at the plunge to pick your skill shot rather than take what you are given; the Door Prize is the most valuable choice because it is the only route to several rules, including Second Wind. Second Wind is the closest thing this machine has to a kickback — there is no kickback at all otherwise — and it saves the ball, adds three life bars and starts a fight if you were ready. It is lit only by a Door Prize or a third shadow boxing completion. And after a heavy bag hit, listen: if you hear an insect buzzing, slap the launch button for 100,000 and a free Smart Punch.
The end of the road

With every jewel on the belt, fill your life bars one last time and the corner offers the Ultimate Challenge instead of Start Fight. Five remaining fighters, one life bar, and over 50 million for a clean run. It happens once. Win or lose, the rest of the game becomes Cash Fights — a genuine gamble where you stake points against a chosen opponent, capped at 240 million in either direction. Start small there, because losing can drop you back below the replay threshold you already earned.

name: The Lord of the Rings
description: A guide to Lord of the Rings pinball: collecting Rings, the six Ring modes, all three movie multiballs, farming Souls, Destroy the Ring and the requirements for Valinor.

body.text: Lord of the Rings looks like a shot-arrow game and plays like a bookkeeping game. Almost everything you do feeds one of four independent ledgers: Rings, Souls, Fellowship members and K-E-E-P letters. None of them talk to each other, and the ending sits behind all of them at once.
Rings are the engine

Four shots carry Ring inserts: the left ramp, the inner orbit, the Sword Ramp and the right orbit. At any moment each one shows an Elf, Dwarf or Man insert, and hitting it banks that type. The moment you collect one, every shot lights red for a few seconds for two more of the same type, so a single Ring should always be the first note of a three-shot phrase rather than a shot on its own. The Spot Ring target down the right side gives a free Ring of a random type and is relit by the left inlane, which makes the left inlane feed quietly one of the most productive rollovers in the game.

items: **Three Elf Rings** light Mode Start at the Ring.
**Seven Dwarf Rings** light Mystery at the Shire.
**Nine Rings of Man** light Gollum Multiball at Gollum's Cave.
Finishing all three races starts **Ring Frenzy**, a ten-second hurry-up where every insert resets the clock and feeds a jackpot that starts at 600,000 and multiplies up to five times.
Rings collected after an award is already lit only pay points — cashing the award resets that race.

body.text: The six modes, and why you should not save them

Mode Start sits on the Ring shot, which is only reachable by jumping the Ring ramp — a firm shot clears the gap to the backboard, a weak one dribbles into Barad-Dur or the top lanes. Flip either button to change the selected mode before you shoot. Escape the Ringwraiths is a countdown chase with the Sword Ramp always live to top the clock back up. Gandalf vs Saruman rewards back-to-back ramps with doubles. Warg Battle opens on the left ramp and then lights all seven main shots. War of the Ents is the one to prioritise: every shot into Orthanc rides the ball up to the Paths of the Dead, which is the only source of Souls in the game. Attack of Shelob alternates sides and takes a shot off the board each round. Kill the Witchking is pure combo work — the left ramp or right orbit arms the Sword Ramp, and only the Sword Ramp follow-up counts.

Each mode can only be played once per game, win or lose, and everything but the first runs on a 30-second timer. Every mode you actually finish lights a Gift of the Elves at the left orbit, collected at Barad-Dur, and the Gifts include 2X scoring for a full minute, a lit extra ball, five million flat, and Ring Multiball.
Three multiballs, three completely different jobs

items: **Fellowship of the Ring** — collect all nine members from their own shots, then hit Barad-Dur. Then it is Balrog, ramp, Balrog, ramp, eight times over, with the ninth Balrog hit paying five million.

**The Two Towers** — spell K-E-E-P with the inlanes and outlanes, then physically lock three balls on the Sword Ramp. Jackpots multiply by the number of balls in play and again by an escalating streak number, but pausing more than about three seconds resets the streak to one.

**Return of the King** — bank 5,000 Souls first. Seven levels of four jackpots, and the trick is that collecting each level's four shots in ascending multiplier order raises every multiplier on the next level.

body.text: Gollum Multiball is different in kind. It adds a ball without stopping anything else, so it stacks with everything, and it flips between doubling and halving all scoring every seven seconds. Time your big shots to the Smeagol half of the cycle. It also has a rescue use: start it during the fanfare at the end of a movie multiball and you get pulled back into two-ball play.
The quiet earners

Gollum's Cave counts your shots into it and hands out Super awards at fixed intervals — Super Spinner, Super Pops, Super Ramps, Super Loops, Super Everything — and those points score regardless of what else is running. Barad-Dur pays on its third, seventh and twelfth hits and relights the Palantir every time. The Palantir is not truly random: the game reads your situation, so shoot it when a mode is about to time out rather than hoarding it.
Destroy the Ring, and the long road past it

Play all three movie multiballs, win or lose, and the Ring qualifies. Take the four Ring shots for one through two and a half million, then the Ring itself for three million — the magnet grabs your ball and a fresh one launches — then knock the trapped ball loose for five million.

Behind that is Valinor, which demands the harder version of everything: all three multiballs genuinely completed, all six modes plus There and Back Again played, all six Gifts collected, and the Ring destroyed. The catch is ordering. Finishing the multiballs qualifies Destroy the Ring, and while it is qualified you cannot start modes at all. So play modes early and hold back the last Two Towers lock, or you will find yourself needing a whole second lap through the multiballs to get another chance at the modes you skipped.

name: Indiana Jones: The Pinball Adventure
description: A complete guide to Indiana Jones: The Pinball Adventure — mode selection with the ramps, the Path of Adventure and The Pit, multiball jackpots, and the Eternal Life wizard round.

body.text: Indiana Jones: The Pinball Adventure is a widebody built on the same footprint as Twilight Zone, and it plays like a game that wants you to have a plan. Twelve movie modes, a raised mini-playfield you steer by tilting, a three-ball lock in a golden idol, and a captive ball you are supposed to punish. Almost nothing here is redundant, and the trap is treating it as a shoot-what-flashes game.
The layout

Going around from the left flipper: the **A-D-V standup bank**, the **left orbit**, then the **Start Mode saucer** — a short tunnel into a hole that is the most important shot on the machine. Above it sits the **Path of Adventure**, a raised playfield you tilt with the flippers. Centre-left is the **left ramp**; centre are the **E-N-T drop targets** hiding both the **lock sinkhole** and a small **Raise Jackpot** target, with three pop bumpers and the **I-N-D-Y rollover lanes** behind them. Right of centre: a **captive ball** behind its own drop target, the **right ramp**, the **right orbit**, the **U-R-E standups**, and **the Idol**, which stores locked balls and returns them to the right flipper.
There is no skill shot. The plunger is a six-shooter and it auto-launches, though the trigger is a live button used inside two of the video modes.
Modes, and how to choose one

Twelve modes, four from each film, started at the Start Mode saucer whenever nothing else is running. Each pays 5M just for starting, and mode scoring goes into your end-of-ball bonus rather than straight onto the score. Most cap near 60M, so no single mode wins a game.

Here is the edge most players miss: the queued mode advances on **ramp shots**, not on the pop bumpers. Count ramps and you can line up whichever mode you want before you take the saucer. Two are worth targeting deliberately, because both light an extra ball — **Survive the Rope Bridge** (four ramps carry Indy across, a fifth cuts the rope) and the **Raven Bar** video mode, where an extra ball appears among the targets after enough hits. Two more are pure value: **Well of Souls** is a six-ball multiball paying 2M per ball in play for every sinkhole shot, and **Escape in the Cart** is a video mode worth up to 55M for steering cleanly through 25 junctions.
The Path of Adventure and The Pit

Spell ADVENTURE across the three target banks and the right ramp lights for the raised playfield. You get fifteen seconds a visit to steer across the lit rollovers, worth 5M each and more if you spelled ADVENTURE repeatedly without cashing it. Clearing your first set lights the extra ball hole up there.

**The Pit is a patience play.** Every Path you complete without dropping into The Pit raises its value by 25M, to a ceiling of 150M — the largest single award on the machine. Bank the completions, then take it. Afterwards the lit rollovers start travelling and the Path becomes considerably harder. One related warning: do not start a multiball while the Path is lit. It stays active, you cannot steer it and juggle three balls at once, and if it times out you have thrown away the whole ADVENTURE build.
Multiball, and building it before you start it

Drop the E-N-T targets, shoot the sinkhole, repeat three times. You can lock with the targets standing — the game calls you a cheat and pays 5M anyway. In multiball the jackpots run in sequence as the Ark, the Stones and the Grail at base values of 20M, 30M and 40M. The left ramp or the sinkhole lights the jackpot and the right ramp collects it.
The real scoring lever is the **raise jackpot total**, a running figure added to every jackpot and super jackpot you ever collect. Build it before you lock the third ball, not after:

items: **Captive ball** — 5M a hit, or 10M if you strike it hard enough to close the rear switch.
**Captive ball drop target** — 3M each.
**Start Mode saucer** — 2M each.
**Raise Jackpot target** behind the drops — adds to the total as well.
During multiball, balls parked in the sinkhole multiply jackpots: one ball is 2x, two is 3x, on a twenty-second timer.

body.text: Collect all three jackpots and the captive ball lights for a **Super Jackpot** at 80M, 90M and 100M, each lit in turn from the left ramp. Supers cannot be multiplied and have no grace period whatsoever, so take the shot the moment it lights.
Quiet points and the wizard round

Two things score far more than they look like they should. **Super Pops** arrives after 75 pop bumper hits and makes every subsequent hit a million for the rest of the ball — it does not time out, so stacking a multiball on top is enormous. **Narrow Escape** pays for saving a ball out of the right outlane through the gate: 1M, then 2M, then 3M, held all game and effectively uncapped.
